```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate iCTRL app icon with proper font rendering."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

SIZE = 1024
CENTER = SIZE // 2

img = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Background gradient
for y in range(SIZE):
    for x in range(SIZE):
        t = (x + y) / (2 * SIZE)
        r = int(30 * (1 - t) + 13 * t)
        g = int(34 * (1 - t) + 15 * t)
        b = int(53 * (1 - t) + 26 * t)
        img.putpixel((x, y), (r, g, b, 255))

# Load fonts
font_i = ImageFont.truetype("/System/Library/Fonts/SF-Pro-Rounded-Bold.otf", 300)
font_ctrl = ImageFont.truetype("/System/Library/Fonts/SF-Pro-Rounded-Bold.otf", 270)

# Measure "i" and "CTRL" actual rendered bounds
i_bbox = font_i.getbbox("i")
ctrl_bbox = font_ctrl.getbbox("CTRL")

i_w = i_bbox[2] - i_bbox[0]
i_h = i_bbox[3] - i_bbox[1]
ctrl_w = ctrl_bbox[2] - ctrl_bbox[0]
ctrl_h = ctrl_bbox[3] - ctrl_bbox[1]

# Total width and max height for centering
spacing = 8
total_w = i_w + spacing + ctrl_w
max_h = max(i_h, ctrl_h)

# True center position
text_left = (SIZE - total_w) // 2
text_top_center = (SIZE - max_h) // 2

# "i" position — align baseline with CTRL
i_x = text_left - i_bbox[0]
i_y = text_top_center - i_bbox[1]

# "CTRL" position — align vertically by baseline
ctrl_x = text_left + i_w + spacing - ctrl_bbox[0]
# Align baselines: "i" bottom = i_y + i_bbox[3], "CTRL" bottom = ctrl_y + ctrl_bbox[3]
ctrl_y = (i_y + i_bbox[3]) - ctrl_bbox[3]

# Orbit center = visual center of the text block
orbit_cx = text_left + total_w // 2
orbit_cy = text_top_center + max_h // 2

def draw_arc(cx, cy, radius, start_angle, end_angle, color, width, alpha=255):
    overlay = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    odraw = ImageDraw.Draw(overlay)
    bbox = [cx - radius, cy - radius, cx + radius, cy + radius]
    odraw.arc(bbox, start_angle, end_angle, fill=color + (alpha,), width=width)
    img.alpha_composite(overlay)

# Orbits centered on text
draw_arc(orbit_cx, orbit_cy, 270, -160, 200, (0, 153, 255), 7, 90)
draw_arc(orbit_cx, orbit_cy, 330, -150, 210, (0, 120, 230), 5, 45)
draw_arc(orbit_cx, orbit_cy, 390, -140, 220, (80, 60, 200), 3, 22)

# Draw "i" in cyan
i_overlay = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
ImageDraw.Draw(i_overlay).text((i_x, i_y), "i", font=font_i, fill=(0, 200, 255, 255))
img.alpha_composite(i_overlay)

# Draw "CTRL" in white
ctrl_overlay = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
ImageDraw.Draw(ctrl_overlay).text((ctrl_x, ctrl_y), "CTRL", font=font_ctrl, fill=(255, 255, 255, 255))
img.alpha_composite(ctrl_overlay)

# "i" dot glow — find rendered dot position
i_dot_cx = i_x + i_bbox[0] + i_w // 2
i_dot_cy = i_y + i_bbox[1] + 20  # top of "i" glyph

for r in range(45, 0, -1):
    alpha = int(60 * (1 - r / 45))
    glow = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    ImageDraw.Draw(glow).ellipse(
        [i_dot_cx - r, i_dot_cy - r, i_dot_cx + r, i_dot_cy + r],
        fill=(0, 229, 255, alpha)
    )
    img.alpha_composite(glow)

# Particles
for px, py, pr, pc in [(820, 340, 5, (0, 204, 255, 100)), (190, 690, 4, (123, 66, 246, 90)), (765, 725, 4, (0, 136, 255, 65))]:
    p = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    ImageDraw.Draw(p).ellipse([px - pr, py - pr, px + pr, py + pr], fill=pc)
    img.alpha_composite(p)

output = "iCTRLApp/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/icon_1024x1024.png"
img.save(output, "PNG")
print(f"✅ Icon saved to {output}")
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/DDI/DDIMountView.swift`:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import UniformTypeIdentifiers

/// The on-device DDI mounting flow.
///
/// Presented from the Automation section when no image is mounted. Deliberately
/// laid out as ordered prerequisites rather than a single button: the mount has
/// three preconditions the user must satisfy in order, and a button that just
/// says "failed" would leave them guessing which one was missing.
struct DDIMountView: View {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss
    @StateObject private var mounter = DDIMounter()
    @StateObject private var images = DeveloperDiskImageStore()

    @State private var showPairingPicker = false
    @State private var pairingError: String?
    @State private var hasPairingFile = PairingFileStore.exists
    @State private var imagesReady = DeveloperDiskImageStore.isComplete
    @State private var downloadError: String?
    @State private var vpnInstalled = false
    @State private var tunnelUp = false
    /// Last connection test through the tunnel, and the interfaces seen then.
    @State private var tunnelProbe: LocalDevVPN.TunnelProbe?
    @State private var interfacesSeen = ""
    @State private var probing = false
    @State private var onWiFi = false
    @State private var networkObserved = false

    /// All three prerequisites, in the order the steps present them. The tunnel
    /// is included because it drops on every reboot — leaving it out let the
    /// mount fail with a socket error naming nothing the user could act on.
    /// All prerequisites, in the order the steps present them. Wi-Fi is included
    /// because the tunnel needs a local interface that cellular doesn't offer.
    private var canMount: Bool {
        hasPairingFile && imagesReady && onWiFi && tunnelUp && !mounter.isRunning
    }

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List {
                Section {
                    Text(L10n.t(.mountIntro))
                        .font(.footnote)
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }

                // Order matters: download the image before touching the VPN.
                // The tunnel takes over local networking, so fetching ~100MB
                // afterwards is asking for a stalled download.
                // Pairing file first: it is the one step that needs another
                // machine, so surfacing it early avoids finishing the on-device
                // steps only to discover a Mac is required.
                pairingSection
                imageSection
                wifiSection
                tunnelSection
                mountSection
            }
            .listStyle(.insetGrouped)
            .navigationTitle(L10n.t(.mountTitle))
            .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarTrailing) {
                    Button(L10n.t(.doneButton)) { dismiss() }
                }
            }
            .onAppear {
                refreshVPNState()
                subscribeToNetworkOnce()
            }
            .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(
                for: UIApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification)) { _ in refreshVPNState() }
            .onOpenURL { url in
                if !url.isFileURL { refreshVPNState() }   // LocalDevVPN bounced us back
            }
            .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: PairingFileStore.didImport)) { _ in
                hasPairingFile = true
                pairingError = nil
            }
            // LocalDevVPN bounces back a fixed second after it starts
            // connecting, often before the tunnel is up: keep checking until it is.
            .onReceive(Timer.publish(every: 2, on: .main, in: .common).autoconnect()) { _ in
                if !tunnelUp { refreshVPNState() }
            }
            .fileImporter(isPresented: $showPairingPicker,
                          allowedContentTypes: PairingFileStore.supportedContentTypes) { result in
                switch result {
                case .success(let url):
                    do {
                        try PairingFileStore.importFile(from: url)
                        hasPairingFile = true
                        pairingError = nil
                    } catch {
                        pairingError = error.localizedDescription
                    }
                case .failure(let error):
                    pairingError = error.localizedDescription
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Names the first unmet prerequisite, so a disabled button explains itself.
    private var missingPrerequisite: String {
        if !hasPairingFile { return L10n.t(.noPairingFile) }
        if !imagesReady { return L10n.t(.imagesNotDownloaded) }
        if !onWiFi { return L10n.t(.notOnWiFi) }
        if !tunnelUp {
            if tunnelProbe == .localNetworkDenied { return L10n.t(.localNetworkDeniedDetail) }
            return vpnInstalled ? L10n.t(.vpnNotConnected) : L10n.t(.vpnNotInstalled)
        }
        return "something is missing"
    }

    /// …and subscribe once for later changes.
    ///
    /// NWPathMonitor resolves asynchronously, so a single read at appear returns
    /// the pre-update default — which reported "not on Wi-Fi" on a device that
    /// plainly was. The observer fires immediately when the path is already
    /// known, and again whenever it changes. Guarded because refreshVPNState
    /// runs on every appear and return-to-foreground; subscribing there would
    /// stack observers that never go away.
    private func subscribeToNetworkOnce() {
        guard !networkObserved else { return }
        networkObserved = true
        NetworkTypeMonitor.shared.observe { type in
            Task { @MainActor in onWiFiChanged(type == .wifi) }
        }
    }

    /// Hop back to the main actor for the @State write.
    @MainActor private func onWiFiChanged(_ connected: Bool) { onWiFi = connected }

    private func refreshVPNState() {
        vpnInstalled = LocalDevVPN.isInstalled
        // Up means a connection through the tunnel worked — not that some
        // address looks right: another VPN can use the same range, and
        // LocalDevVPN's addresses are configurable. One probe at a time; the
        // timer fires faster than a failing probe returns.
        if !probing {
            probing = true
            Task { @MainActor in
                let result = await LocalDevVPN.probeTunnel()
                tunnelProbe = result
                interfacesSeen = LocalDevVPN.interfaceSummary()
                tunnelUp = result == .reachable
                probing = false
            }
        }
        // Read the current value on every refresh…
        onWiFi = NetworkTypeMonitor.shared.current == .wifi
    }

    // ① The tunnel. LocalDevVPN exposes localdevvpn://enable?scheme=…, so this
    //    can send the user straight into connecting and get them back, instead
    //    of just naming an app and hoping.
    private var tunnelSection: some View {
        Section {
            stepRow(4, done: tunnelUp,
                    title: L10n.t(.startLocalDevVPN),
                    detail: tunnelUp
                        ? "\(L10n.t(.tunnelUpDetail)) (\(DDIMounter.tunnelAddress))"
                        : tunnelProbe == .localNetworkDenied
                          ? L10n.t(.localNetworkDeniedDetail)
                          : vpnInstalled
                            ? "\(L10n.t(.vpnInstalledDetail)) (\(DDIMounter.tunnelAddress))"
                            : L10n.t(.vpnMissingDetail))

            if !tunnelUp, tunnelProbe == .localNetworkDenied {
                actionButton(L10n.t(.openSettings)) {
                    UIApplication.shared.open(URL(string: UIApplication.openSettingsURLString)!)
                }
            } else if !tunnelUp {
                actionButton(vpnInstalled ? L10n.t(.openVPNAndConnect) : L10n.t(.getVPNFromAppStore)) {
                    // enable? starts the tunnel and bounces back to us; the bare
                    // App Store link is the fallback when it isn't installed.
                    UIApplication.shared.open(vpnInstalled ? LocalDevVPN.enableURL
                                                           : LocalDevVPN.appStoreURL)
                }
            }
        } header: {
            Text(L10n.t(.prerequisiteHeader))
        } footer: {
            if tunnelUp {
                Text(L10n.t(.tunnelDetectedFooter))
            } else if case .unreachable? = tunnelProbe, vpnInstalled {
                // Connected but still not found: show what is there, so a
                // changed tunnel address is visible at a glance.
                Text(L10n.t(.cannotStartVPNFooter) + "\n\n" + L10n.t(.interfacesSeen) + " " + interfacesSeen)
            } else {
                Text(L10n.t(.cannotStartVPNFooter))
            }
        }
    }

    // ② Wi-Fi. The tunnel rides the local network interface, which cellular
    //    does not provide — so any Wi-Fi will do, but some Wi-Fi is required.
    private var wifiSection: some View {
        Section {
            stepRow(3, done: onWiFi,
                    title: L10n.t(.wifiRequired),
                    detail: onWiFi ? L10n.t(.wifiConnected) : L10n.t(.wifiMissing))
        } footer: {
            Text(L10n.t(.wifiFooter))
        }
    }

    // ② The pairing file — proves to lockdownd that we're a trusted host.
    private var pairingSection: some View {
        Section {
            stepRow(1, done: hasPairingFile,
                    title: L10n.t(.importPairingFile),
                    detail: hasPairingFile
                        ? "\(L10n.t(.pairingImported))\(PairingFileStore.importedAt.map { " · " + $0.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened) } ?? "")"
                        : L10n.t(.pairingHint))

            actionButton(hasPairingFile ? L10n.t(.replacePairingFile) : L10n.t(.choosePairingFile)) {
                showPairingPicker = true
            }

            if hasPairingFile {
                actionButton(L10n.t(.removePairingFile), role: .destructive) {
                    PairingFileStore.remove()
                    hasPairingFile = false
                }
            }

            if let pairingError {
                Label(pairingError, systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
                    .font(.caption)
                    .foregroundColor(.orange)
            }
        }
    }

    // ③ The image itself.
    private var imageSection: some View {
        Section {
            stepRow(2, done: imagesReady,
                    title: L10n.t(.ddiComponentTitle),
                    detail: imagesReady
                        ? "\(L10n.t(.ddiDownloaded)) · \(ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount: DeveloperDiskImageStore.totalBytesOnDisk, countStyle: .file))"
                        : L10n.t(.ddiDownloadHint))

            if images.isDownloading {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    ProgressView(value: images.progress)
                    if let msg = images.statusMessage {
                        Text(msg).font(.caption2).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            } else if !imagesReady {
                actionButton(L10n.t(.downloadImageFiles)) {
                    Task {
                        do {
                            try await images.download()
                            imagesReady = DeveloperDiskImageStore.isComplete
                            downloadError = nil
                        } catch {
                            downloadError = error.localizedDescription
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            if let downloadError {
                Label(downloadError, systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
                    .font(.caption)
                    .foregroundColor(.orange)
            }
        } footer: {
            Text(L10n.t(.ddiSourceFooter))
        }
    }

    private var mountSection: some View {
        Section {
            switch mounter.phase {
            case .idle, .failed:
                Button {
                    Task { await mounter.mount() }
                } label: {
                    Label(L10n.t(.mountButton), systemImage: "externaldrive.badge.plus")
                }
                .disabled(!canMount)

            case .connecting, .queryingDevice, .finalizing:
                HStack(spacing: 8) {
                    ProgressView()
                    Text(phaseLabel).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }

            case .uploading(let fraction):
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    ProgressView(value: fraction)
                    Text("\(L10n.t(.uploadingImage)) \(Int(fraction * 100))%")
                        .font(.caption).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }

            case .mounted:
                Label(L10n.t(.mountedOK),
                      systemImage: "checkmark.circle.fill")
                    .foregroundColor(.green)
            }

            if case .failed(let message) = mounter.phase {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    Label(L10n.t(.mountFailed), systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
                        .foregroundColor(.orange)
                    Text(message)
                        .font(.caption)
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
                }
            }
        } footer: {
            if case .mounted = mounter.phase {
                Text(L10n.t(.mountNotPersistentFooter))
            } else if !canMount, !mounter.isRunning {
                Text("\(L10n.t(.finishStepsFirst)) — \(missingPrerequisite).")
            } else {
                Text(L10n.t(.firstMountNetworkFooter))
            }
        }
    }

    private var phaseLabel: String {
        switch mounter.phase {
        case .connecting:     return "Connecting through the tunnel…"
        case .queryingDevice: return "Reading device identity…"
        case .finalizing:     return "Finalizing…"
        default:              return ""
        }
    }

    /// One numbered step: badge, title, explanation.
    ///
    /// The badge is the row's `Label` icon, so SwiftUI indents the text to a
    /// consistent leading edge — and `actionButton` pads to match, which is what
    /// keeps a step's button aligned with its own text instead of the card edge.
    private func stepRow(_ n: Int, done: Bool, title: String, detail: String) -> some View {
        Label {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                Text(title)
                Text(detail)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundColor(done ? .green : .secondary)
                    .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
            }
        } icon: {
            stepBadge(n, done: done)
        }
    }

    /// A step's action, indented to line up with that step's text.
    ///
    /// `.body` rather than `.footnote`: these are the things the user is meant
    /// to tap, and at caption size they read as annotations instead of actions.
    private func actionButton(_ title: String, role: ButtonRole? = nil,
                              action: @escaping () -> Void) -> some View {
        // Built as a Label with an INVISIBLE badge rather than a guessed
        // padding: the real indent is the badge width plus whatever spacing
        // Label uses, which varies with Dynamic Type. Reusing the same layout
        // makes the text land exactly under the step title by construction.
        Button(role: role, action: action) {
            Label {
                Text(title)
                    .font(.body)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            } icon: {
                stepBadge(0, done: false).hidden()
            }
        }
    }

    private func stepBadge(_ n: Int, done: Bool) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .fill(done ? Color.green : Color.accentColor)
                .frame(width: 22, height: 22)
            if done {
                Image(systemName: "checkmark")
                    .font(.caption2.bold())
                    .foregroundColor(.white)
            } else {
                Text(verbatim: "\(n)")
                    .font(.caption2.bold())
                    .foregroundColor(.white)
            }
        }
    }
}

```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/DDI/DDIMounter.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import IDevice

enum DDIError: LocalizedError {
    case invalidPairingFile(String)
    case missingPairingFile
    case missingImage
    case tunnelUnavailable(String)
    case tunnelDown
    case localNetworkDenied
    case ffi(String, String)          // operation, message
    case downloadFailed(String, String)

    var errorDescription: String? {
        switch self {
        case .invalidPairingFile(let why):
            return "Pairing file rejected: \(why)"
        case .missingPairingFile:
            return "No pairing file imported yet."
        case .missingImage:
            return "Developer Disk Image files are missing — download them first."
        case .tunnelDown:
            return "LocalDevVPN isn't connected. The tunnel doesn't survive a reboot — "
                 + "open LocalDevVPN and connect it (step 1), then mount again."
        case .localNetworkDenied:
            return "iOS blocked the connection to the tunnel: Local Network access is off for iCTRL. "
                 + "Turn it on in Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network (or Settings → iCTRL), then mount again."
        case .tunnelUnavailable(let why):
            return "Can't reach the device's debug service: \(why)"
        case .ffi(let op, let msg):
            return "\(op) failed: \(msg)"
        case .downloadFailed(let file, let why):
            return "Couldn't download \(file): \(why)"
        }
    }
}

/// Mounts the Developer Disk Image on this device, from this device.
///
/// The trick — and it is StikDebug's, ported here — is that no privileged
/// entitlement is involved. A local VPN app (LocalDevVPN / StosVPN) makes the
/// device's own `remoted` service routable at 10.7.0.1:49152, and this code then
/// talks to it as an ordinary network client, exactly as Xcode on a Mac would.
/// The pairing file is what authenticates that conversation.
///
/// All of the real work happens in the `idevice` Rust library (MIT); this is the
/// Swift side that sequences it.
@MainActor
final class DDIMounter: ObservableObject {

    /// Where LocalDevVPN/StosVPN publishes this device. Both use the same
    /// address, and it is not configurable in either app.
    static let tunnelAddress = "10.7.0.1"
    /// `remoted` — the RemotePairing service the tunnel exposes.
    static let tunnelPort: UInt16 = 49152

    enum Phase: Equatable {
        case idle
        case connecting
        case queryingDevice
        case uploading(Double)      // 0…1
        case finalizing
        case mounted
        case failed(String)
    }

    @Published private(set) var phase: Phase = .idle {
        didSet {
            // Progress ticks would flood the file; every other transition is
            // exactly the breadcrumb trail a failed mount needs.
            if case .uploading = phase { return }
            ictrlLog("DDI phase → \(phase)")
        }
    }

    var isRunning: Bool {
        switch phase {
        case .idle, .mounted, .failed: return false
        default: return true
        }
    }

    /// Mount the image. Long-running and blocking at the FFI layer, so the whole
    /// sequence runs off the main actor and only publishes back to it.
    func mount() async {
        guard !isRunning else { return }
        phase = .connecting

        do {
            guard PairingFileStore.exists else { throw DDIError.missingPairingFile }
            guard DeveloperDiskImageStore.isComplete else { throw DDIError.missingImage }
            // Check the tunnel before dialling it. Without this a disconnected
            // VPN surfaces as "device socket io failed", which names a socket
            // rather than the step the user has to fix — and the tunnel is down
            // after every reboot, so this is the common case, not an edge one.
            switch await LocalDevVPN.probeTunnel() {
            case .reachable: break
            case .localNetworkDenied: throw DDIError.localNetworkDenied
            case .unreachable: throw DDIError.tunnelDown
            }

            let pairingPath = PairingFileStore.storedURL.path
            let method = DeveloperDiskImageStore.mountMethod
            let imageDir = DeveloperDiskImageStore.directory.path

            // A dedicated Thread with an explicit stack, not a Task.
            //
            // The TSS request builds a reqwest client, whose TLS setup needs far
            // more stack than a Swift concurrency worker provides — it aborted
            // there (SIGABRT, panic inside ClientBuilder::build) on the first
            // real mount. StikDebug runs the same call on a plain Thread for the
            // same reason; 4MB is generous enough not to have to think about it.
            try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { (cont: CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>) in
                let thread = Thread {
                    do {
                        try Self.performMount(pairingPath: pairingPath, method: method,
                                              imageDir: imageDir) { phase in
                            Task { @MainActor in self.phase = phase }
                        }
                        cont.resume()
                    } catch {
                        cont.resume(throwing: error)
                    }
                }
                thread.stackSize = 4 * 1024 * 1024
                thread.name = "ictrl.ddi.mount"
                thread.qualityOfService = .userInitiated
                thread.start()
            }

            phase = .mounted
        } catch {
            ictrlLog("❌ DDI mount failed: \(error.localizedDescription)")
            phase = .failed(error.localizedDescription)
        }
    }

    // MARK: - FFI

    /// Ask the device what images it already has mounted.
    ///
    /// iOS refuses a second mount with a bare "ImageMountFailed", so without
    /// this an already-mounted device reports a hard failure that reads like
    /// something is broken. StikDebug guards its mount the same way.
    ///
    /// Returns nil when the question can't be answered (no tunnel, no pairing
    /// file) — the caller should treat that as "unknown", not "not mounted".
    nonisolated static func mountedImageCount(adapter: OpaquePointer,
                                              handshake: OpaquePointer) -> Int? {
        var client: OpaquePointer?
        if let err = image_mounter_connect_rsd(adapter, handshake, &client) {
            idevice_error_free(err)
            return nil
        }
        guard let client else { return nil }
        defer { image_mounter_free(client) }

        var devices: UnsafeMutablePointer<plist_t?>?
        var count = 0
        if let err = image_mounter_copy_devices(client, &devices, &count) {
            idevice_error_free(err)
            return nil
        }
        if let devices { idevice_plist_array_free(devices, UInt(count)) }
        return count
    }

    /// Whether the DDI cryptex (iOS 26.4+) is installed. False when cryptexd
    /// can't be asked — an older OS has no such service.
    nonisolated static func cryptexDDIInstalled(adapter: OpaquePointer, handshake: OpaquePointer) -> Bool {
        var installed: UnsafeMutablePointer<InstalledCryptexC>?
        if let err = cryptexd_installed_ddi(adapter, handshake, &installed) {
            idevice_error_free(err)
        }
        defer { if let installed { cryptexd_free_installed_cryptex(installed) } }
        return installed != nil
    }

    /// Install the DDI as a cryptex (iOS 26.4+). cryptexd takes the whole
    /// restore directory — image, trust cache, manifest, cryptex info and root
    /// hash — and does the personalization itself, so there is no ECID to read
    /// and no upload progress to report.
    nonisolated private static func installCryptex(adapter: OpaquePointer, handshake: OpaquePointer,
                                                   imageDir: String,
                                                   report: @escaping (Phase) -> Void) throws {
        var assets: OpaquePointer?
        try check("Reading the DDI cryptex files") { cryptex1_assets_load(imageDir, &assets) }
        guard let assets else { throw DDIError.ffi("Reading the DDI cryptex files", "nothing loaded") }
        defer { cryptex1_assets_free(assets) }
        report(.uploading(0))
        try check("Installing the DDI cryptex") { cryptexd_install_ddi(adapter, handshake, assets, nil) }
        report(.finalizing)
    }


    /// Force the rustls crypto provider to be installed before anything needs it.
    ///
    /// The TSS request builds a reqwest client, and this library is compiled
    /// with `rustls-no-provider` — so if no process-default provider has been
    /// installed, `Client::new()` panics and aborts the app. The library only
    /// installs one from inside `start_session`, which the RSD path never calls
    /// (an RSD connection is already authenticated by the RemotePairing
    /// handshake — calling it there is what produced InvalidConnection).
    ///
    /// So we open a throwaway plain connection to the tunnel and start a session
    /// on it purely for that side effect. Both the connection and the session are
    /// expected to be short-lived; failures here are deliberately ignored,
    /// because the goal is the provider install, not the session.
    nonisolated static func primeCryptoProvider() {
        ictrlLog("Priming rustls crypto provider via a throwaway session")
        var pairing: OpaquePointer?
        guard idevice_pairing_file_read(PairingFileStore.storedURL.path, &pairing) == nil,
              let pairing else { return }
        defer { idevice_pairing_file_free(pairing) }

        var addr = sockaddr_in()
        addr.sin_family = sa_family_t(AF_INET)
        addr.sin_port = tunnelPort.bigEndian
        guard tunnelAddress.withCString({ inet_pton(AF_INET, $0, &addr.sin_addr) }) == 1 else { return }

        var device: OpaquePointer?
        withUnsafePointer(to: &addr) { ptr in
            ptr.withMemoryRebound(to: idevice_sockaddr.self, capacity: 1) { sa in
                if let err = idevice_new_tcp_socket(sa, idevice_socklen_t(MemoryLayout<sockaddr_in>.size),
                                                    "iCTRL-crypto-prime", &device) {
                    idevice_error_free(err)
                }
            }
        }
        guard let device else { return }
        defer { idevice_free(device) }

        // The session itself may well fail — the provider is installed before
        // that can matter, which is the whole point of the call.
        if let err = idevice_start_session(device, pairing, false) {
            idevice_error_free(err)
        }
    }

    nonisolated private static func performMount(pairingPath: String,
                                                 method: DeveloperDiskImageStore.MountMethod,
                                                 imageDir: String,
                                                 report: @escaping (Phase) -> Void) throws {
        ictrlLog("DDI mount starting — \(method.rawValue) image from \(imageDir)")
        primeCryptoProvider()

        var pairing: OpaquePointer?
        try check("Reading pairing file") { rp_pairing_file_read(pairingPath, &pairing) }
        defer { if let pairing { rp_pairing_file_free(pairing) } }

        var addr = sockaddr_in()
        addr.sin_family = sa_family_t(AF_INET)
        addr.sin_port = tunnelPort.bigEndian
        guard tunnelAddress.withCString({ inet_pton(AF_INET, $0, &addr.sin_addr) }) == 1 else {
            throw DDIError.tunnelUnavailable("bad tunnel address")
        }

        var adapter: OpaquePointer?
        var handshake: OpaquePointer?
        try withUnsafePointer(to: &addr) { ptr in
            try ptr.withMemoryRebound(to: idevice_sockaddr.self, capacity: 1) { sa in
                try check("Connecting to the device") {
                    tunnel_create_rppairing(sa, idevice_socklen_t(MemoryLayout<sockaddr_in>.size),
                                            "iCTRL", pairing, nil, nil, &adapter, &handshake)
                }
            }
        }
        defer {
            if let handshake { rsd_handshake_free(handshake) }
            if let adapter { adapter_free(adapter) }
        }
        guard let adapter, let handshake else {
            throw DDIError.tunnelUnavailable("tunnel returned no handles")
        }

        report(.queryingDevice)

        // Already mounted? iOS answers a second mount with a bare
        // "ImageMountFailed", which reads like a real failure rather than
        // "nothing to do". Ask first and treat that case as success. Both
        // kinds are asked about whatever this OS uses: an image mounted by
        // Xcode, or before an OS update, counts just the same.
        if cryptexDDIInstalled(adapter: adapter, handshake: handshake) {
            ictrlLog("✅ The developer disk image cryptex is already installed — nothing to do")
            return
        }
        if let mounted = mountedImageCount(adapter: adapter, handshake: handshake) {
            ictrlLog("Device reports \(mounted) mounted image(s)")
            if mounted > 0 {
                ictrlLog("✅ A developer image is already mounted — nothing to do")
                return
            }
        }

        if method == .cryptex {
            try installCryptex(adapter: adapter, handshake: handshake, imageDir: imageDir, report: report)
            return
        }

        // Mapped, not read: the personalized image is about 100MB.
        let image = try Data(contentsOf: URL(fileURLWithPath: imageDir).appendingPathComponent("Image.dmg"),
                             options: .mappedIfSafe)
        let trustCache = try Data(contentsOf: URL(fileURLWithPath: imageDir).appendingPathComponent("Image.dmg.trustcache"))
        let manifest = try Data(contentsOf: URL(fileURLWithPath: imageDir).appendingPathComponent("BuildManifest.plist"))

        // The ECID identifies this specific device to Apple's signing service.
        // A personalized image is signed for one device and one nonce, which is
        // why this can't be pre-baked.
        let ecid = try uniqueChipID(adapter: adapter, handshake: handshake)

        var client: OpaquePointer?
        try check("Opening the image mounter") {
            image_mounter_connect_rsd(adapter, handshake, &client)
        }
        defer { if let client { image_mounter_free(client) } }
        guard let client else { throw DDIError.ffi("Opening the image mounter", "no client") }

        report(.uploading(0))

        // Progress arrives on a Rust thread; the context carries the callback so
        // no global state is involved.
        final class ProgressBox { let report: (Phase) -> Void; init(_ r: @escaping (Phase) -> Void) { report = r } }
        let box = Unmanaged.passRetained(ProgressBox(report))
        defer { box.release() }

        try image.withUnsafeBytes { img in
            try trustCache.withUnsafeBytes { tc in
                try manifest.withUnsafeBytes { mf in
                    try check("Mounting the image") {
                        image_mounter_mount_personalized_with_callback_rsd(
                            client, adapter, handshake,
                            img.bindMemory(to: UInt8.self).baseAddress, image.count,
                            tc.bindMemory(to: UInt8.self).baseAddress, trustCache.count,
                            mf.bindMemory(to: UInt8.self).baseAddress, manifest.count,
                            nil,
                            ecid,
                            { progress, total, context in
                                guard let context, total > 0 else { return }
                                let box = Unmanaged<ProgressBox>.fromOpaque(context).takeUnretainedValue()
                                box.report(.uploading(Double(progress) / Double(total)))
                            },
                            box.toOpaque())
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        report(.finalizing)
    }

    /// Read `UniqueChipID` (ECID) from lockdownd.
    nonisolated private static func uniqueChipID(adapter: OpaquePointer, handshake: OpaquePointer) throws -> UInt64 {
        var client: OpaquePointer?
        try check("Connecting to lockdownd") {
            lockdownd_connect_rsd(adapter, handshake, &client)
        }
        defer { if let client { lockdownd_client_free(client) } }
        guard let client else { throw DDIError.ffi("Connecting to lockdownd", "no client") }

        // No start_session here. A lockdownd client reached over the RSD tunnel
        // is already authenticated by the RemotePairing handshake, so opening a
        // second session on it is rejected — that is the InvalidConnection
        // (code 15) this used to fail with. WebDriverAgent's equivalent (and
        // StikDebug's) reads the value straight off the connected client.
        var value: plist_t?
        try check("Reading UniqueChipID") {
            lockdownd_get_value(client, "UniqueChipID", nil, &value)
        }
        defer { if let value { plist_free(value) } }
        guard let value else { throw DDIError.ffi("Reading UniqueChipID", "no value") }

        var ecid: UInt64 = 0
        plist_get_uint_val(value, &ecid)
        guard ecid != 0 else { throw DDIError.ffi("Reading UniqueChipID", "device returned 0") }
        return ecid
    }

    /// Turn an `IdeviceFfiError*` into a Swift error, freeing it either way.
    ///
    /// The FFI reports failure by returning a pointer that the caller owns —
    /// ignoring it leaks, and reading `.message` after freeing is a use-after-free,
    /// so the message is copied out before the free.
    @discardableResult
    nonisolated private static func check(_ operation: String,
                              _ call: () -> UnsafeMutablePointer<IdeviceFfiError>?) throws -> Bool {
        guard let err = call() else { return true }
        let message = err.pointee.message.map { String(cString: $0) } ?? "code \(err.pointee.code)"
        let code = err.pointee.code
        idevice_error_free(err)
        ictrlLog("❌ \(operation): \(message) (code \(code))")
        // "ImageMountFailed" is the device's own word for it and says nothing
        // about why, so attach what it usually means rather than passing a bare
        // string to someone with no way to look it up.
        var detail = "\(message) (code \(code))"
        if message.contains("device socket io failed") || message.contains("connect:") {
            detail += ". The tunnel isn't reachable — LocalDevVPN is most likely disconnected "
                    + "(it doesn't survive a reboot). Connect it and try again."
        }
        if message.contains("ImageMountFailed") {
            detail += ". The device rejected the image — usually because it doesn't match this "
                    + "iOS version, or the download is incomplete. Re-download the image files "
                    + "and try again; if it persists, this iOS build may be newer than the mirror."
        }
        throw DDIError.ffi(operation, detail)
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/DDI/DeveloperDiskImageStore.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

/// The files a DDI mount needs, kept on disk.
///
/// Which files depends on the OS: up to iOS 26.3 the personalized image is
/// mounted through the image mounter; from iOS 26.4 the DDI is a cryptex,
/// installed through cryptexd from a different set of files. Each set lives in
/// its own directory, so an OS update that crosses 26.4 downloads the other
/// set instead of mounting files the device no longer accepts.
///
/// Not bundled in the app: the images change with Xcode releases, and most
/// users mounting a DDI already have network. Downloaded once and reused — the
/// mount itself is what needs to be repeated after a reboot, not the download.
@MainActor
final class DeveloperDiskImageStore: ObservableObject {

    enum MountMethod: String {
        /// iOS 17 – 26.3: image mounter, personalized image.
        case personalized
        /// iOS 26.4 and later: cryptexd installs the DDI cryptex.
        case cryptex

        /// Mirror folder, maintained by the pymobiledevice3 author. Apple does
        /// not publish these for direct download; the same content ships inside
        /// Xcode, so a user with a Mac can supply their own copy instead (see
        /// `importComponent`).
        var mirrorFolder: String {
            switch self {
            case .personalized: return "Xcode_iOS_DDI_Personalized"
            case .cryptex: return "Xcode_iOS_DDI_Cryptex"
            }
        }

        var components: [Component] {
            switch self {
            case .personalized: return [.buildManifest, .image, .trustCache]
            case .cryptex: return [.buildManifest, .image, .trustCache, .cryptexInfo, .rootHash]
            }
        }
    }

    /// The method this device's OS needs.
    nonisolated static var mountMethod: MountMethod {
        let v = ProcessInfo.processInfo.operatingSystemVersion
        return v.majorVersion > 26 || (v.majorVersion == 26 && v.minorVersion >= 4) ? .cryptex : .personalized
    }

    private static let mirrorBase =
        "https://github.com/doronz88/DeveloperDiskImage/raw/refs/heads/main/PersonalizedImages"

    enum Component: String, CaseIterable {
        case buildManifest = "BuildManifest.plist"
        case image = "Image.dmg"
        case trustCache = "Image.dmg.trustcache"
        case cryptexInfo = "Image.dmg.cryptex_info"
        case rootHash = "Image.dmg.root_hash"

        /// Download location for this device's mount method.
        var remoteURL: URL {
            URL(string: "\(DeveloperDiskImageStore.mirrorBase)/\(DeveloperDiskImageStore.mountMethod.mirrorFolder)/\(rawValue)")!
        }

        /// Share of the download, for a progress bar that moves with the bytes.
        var weight: Double {
            switch self {
            case .image: return 0.9
            case .buildManifest: return 0.07
            default: return 0.01
            }
        }
    }

    @Published private(set) var isDownloading = false
    @Published private(set) var progress: Double = 0
    @Published private(set) var statusMessage: String?

    private nonisolated static var rootDirectory: URL {
        FileManager.default.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
            .appendingPathComponent("DDI")
    }

    /// This device's file set. Builds before the cryptex split kept the
    /// personalized files directly in `DDI/`; they are moved into place
    /// rather than downloaded again.
    nonisolated static var directory: URL {
        let dir = rootDirectory.appendingPathComponent(mountMethod.mirrorFolder)
        migrateLegacyFiles(into: dir)
        return dir
    }

    private nonisolated static func migrateLegacyFiles(into dir: URL) {
        guard mountMethod == .personalized else { return }
        let fm = FileManager.default
        for c in MountMethod.personalized.components {
            let old = rootDirectory.appendingPathComponent(c.rawValue)
            guard fm.fileExists(atPath: old.path) else { continue }
            try? fm.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
            let new = dir.appendingPathComponent(c.rawValue)
            if fm.fileExists(atPath: new.path) { try? fm.removeItem(at: old) } else { try? fm.moveItem(at: old, to: new) }
        }
    }

    nonisolated static func url(for component: Component) -> URL {
        directory.appendingPathComponent(component.rawValue)
    }

    /// True when every file of this device's set is present. Deliberately does
    /// not validate their contents — a corrupt image surfaces as a mount error,
    /// and guessing at validity here would just add a second place to be wrong.
    static var isComplete: Bool {
        mountMethod.components.allSatisfy {
            FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url(for: $0).path)
        }
    }

    static var totalBytesOnDisk: Int64 {
        mountMethod.components.reduce(0) { sum, c in
            let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: url(for: c).path)
            return sum + ((attrs?[.size] as? Int64) ?? 0)
        }
    }

    func download() async throws {
        guard !isDownloading else { return }
        isDownloading = true
        progress = 0
        defer { isDownloading = false }

        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: Self.directory,
                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)

        // Weight by size so the bar reflects reality: the image dwarfs the
        // rest, and an evenly-weighted bar would sit near the end for the
        // whole download.
        let components = Self.mountMethod.components
        let total = components.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.weight }
        var completed = 0.0

        for component in components {
            let dest = Self.url(for: component)
            let weight = component.weight / total
            if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dest.path) {
                completed += weight
                progress = completed
                continue
            }
            statusMessage = "Downloading \(component.rawValue)…"
            try await download(component, to: dest) { [weak self] frac in
                Task { @MainActor in self?.progress = completed + frac * weight }
            }
            completed += weight
            progress = completed
        }
        statusMessage = nil
    }

    /// Generous limits: the mirror is GitHub, which can crawl and stall for
    /// long stretches on some networks, and the default 60s idle limit then
    /// fails the image partway.
    private static let session: URLSession = {
        let config = URLSessionConfiguration.default
        config.timeoutIntervalForRequest = 120
        config.timeoutIntervalForResource = 60 * 60
        return URLSession(configuration: config)
    }()
    private static let downloadAttempts = 4

    /// Download one file, resuming from what already arrived when the
    /// connection drops (a Range request; a server that ignores it sends the
    /// whole file again, and the partial copy is discarded).
    private func download(_ component: Component, to dest: URL,
                          onProgress: @escaping (Double) -> Void) async throws {
        var data = Data()
        var expected: Int64 = -1
        var lastError: Error?
        for attempt in 1...Self.downloadAttempts {
            do {
                var request = URLRequest(url: component.remoteURL)
                if !data.isEmpty { request.setValue("bytes=\(data.count)-", forHTTPHeaderField: "Range") }
                let (bytes, response) = try await Self.session.bytes(for: request)
                guard let http = response as? HTTPURLResponse, http.statusCode == 200 || http.statusCode == 206 else {
                    throw DDIError.downloadFailed(component.rawValue,
                        (response as? HTTPURLResponse).map { "HTTP \($0.statusCode)" } ?? "no response")
                }
                if http.statusCode == 200 {
                    data = Data()
                    expected = response.expectedContentLength
                } else if expected < 0, response.expectedContentLength > 0 {
                    expected = Int64(data.count) + response.expectedContentLength
                }
                if expected > 0 { data.reserveCapacity(Int(expected)) }

                var lastReport = 0.0
                for try await byte in bytes {
                    data.append(byte)
                    if expected > 0 {
                        let frac = Double(data.count) / Double(expected)
                        // Reporting every byte would flood the main actor; 1% is
                        // plenty for a progress bar.
                        if frac - lastReport >= 0.01 {
                            lastReport = frac
                            onProgress(frac)
                        }
                    }
                }
                try data.write(to: dest, options: .atomic)
                ictrlLog("Downloaded \(component.rawValue) — \(data.count)B" + (attempt > 1 ? " (attempt \(attempt))" : ""))
                onProgress(1.0)
                return
            } catch let error as DDIError {
                throw error
            } catch {
                lastError = error
                ictrlLog("⚠️ \(component.rawValue) download interrupted at \(data.count)B (attempt \(attempt)): \(error.localizedDescription)")
                statusMessage = "Downloading \(component.rawValue)… (retrying, \(attempt)/\(Self.downloadAttempts - 1))"
            }
        }
        throw lastError ?? DDIError.downloadFailed(component.rawValue, "no response")
    }

    /// Accept a user-supplied copy, for people who'd rather pull the files out
    /// of their own Xcode than trust a third-party mirror.
    static func importComponent(_ component: Component, from url: URL) throws {
        let scoped = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
        defer { if scoped { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }
        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        let data = try Data(contentsOf: url)
        try data.write(to: self.url(for: component), options: .atomic)
    }

    static func removeAll() {
        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: rootDirectory)
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/DDI/LocalDevVPN.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Network
import UIKit

/// Talking to LocalDevVPN, the app that makes this device's debug service
/// routable so the DDI mount can reach it.
///
/// It registers `localdevvpn://` and takes a callback scheme, so we can send the
/// user straight into "connect" and get them back — rather than telling them to
/// go find an app and return on their own.
enum LocalDevVPN {

    /// Bare scheme, used only as a `canOpenURL:` probe. The app's handler falls
    /// through to `default: break` for it, so probing can't cause side effects.
    static let probeURL = URL(string: "localdevvpn://")!

    /// Starts the tunnel, then returns to `ictrl-app://`.
    static let enableURL = URL(string: "localdevvpn://enable?scheme=ictrl-app")!

    static let appStoreURL = URL(string: "https://apps.apple.com/app/localdevvpn/id6755608044")!

    /// Whether LocalDevVPN is installed.
    ///
    /// Requires `localdevvpn` in this app's `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` —
    /// without it iOS answers `false` no matter what is installed, which would
    /// silently send every user to the App Store.
    @MainActor
    static var isInstalled: Bool {
        UIApplication.shared.canOpenURL(probeURL)
    }

    enum TunnelProbe: Equatable {
        /// The device's own service answered through the tunnel.
        case reachable
        /// iOS refused the connection: Local Network access is off for iCTRL.
        case localNetworkDenied
        /// Nothing answered (tunnel down, or set to other addresses).
        case unreachable(String)
    }

    /// Whether the tunnel actually works: a TCP connection to the service the
    /// mount talks to.
    ///
    /// Not "is there a 10.7.0.x address": LocalDevVPN's addresses are
    /// user-configurable, another VPN can use the same range, and another
    /// app's tunnel interface is not always listed. A connection is exactly
    /// what the mount needs, and it tells a Local Network denial apart from
    /// "nothing there".
    static func probeTunnel(timeout: TimeInterval = 1.5) async -> TunnelProbe {
        let host = NWEndpoint.Host(DDIMounter.tunnelAddress)
        guard let port = NWEndpoint.Port(rawValue: DDIMounter.tunnelPort) else { return .unreachable("bad port") }
        let conn = NWConnection(host: host, port: port, using: .tcp)
        let queue = DispatchQueue(label: "ictrl.tunnel.probe")
        let result: TunnelProbe = await withCheckedContinuation { cont in
            var done = false
            func finish(_ r: TunnelProbe) {
                guard !done else { return }
                done = true
                conn.cancel()
                cont.resume(returning: r)
            }
            conn.stateUpdateHandler = { state in
                switch state {
                case .ready:
                    finish(.reachable)
                case .waiting(let err), .failed(let err):
                    if #available(iOS 14.2, *), conn.currentPath?.unsatisfiedReason == .localNetworkDenied {
                        finish(.localNetworkDenied)
                    } else if case .waiting = state {
                        // Keep waiting: a refused connect retries until the timeout.
                        _ = err
                    } else {
                        finish(.unreachable(err.localizedDescription))
                    }
                default:
                    break
                }
            }
            conn.start(queue: queue)
            queue.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout) {
                if #available(iOS 14.2, *), conn.currentPath?.unsatisfiedReason == .localNetworkDenied {
                    finish(.localNetworkDenied)
                } else {
                    finish(.unreachable("no answer in \(timeout)s"))
                }
            }
        }
        ictrlLog("Tunnel probe \(DDIMounter.tunnelAddress):\(DDIMounter.tunnelPort) → \(result); interfaces: \(interfaceSummary())")
        return result
    }

    /// Every IPv4 address on an up interface, as "name address" — for the log
    /// and the screen when the tunnel can't be found.
    static func interfaceSummary() -> String {
        var head: UnsafeMutablePointer<ifaddrs>?
        guard getifaddrs(&head) == 0, let first = head else { return "unavailable" }
        defer { freeifaddrs(head) }
        var out: [String] = []
        for ptr in sequence(first: first, next: { $0.pointee.ifa_next }) {
            let flags = Int32(ptr.pointee.ifa_flags)
            guard flags & IFF_UP != 0, let addr = ptr.pointee.ifa_addr,
                  addr.pointee.sa_family == UInt8(AF_INET) else { continue }
            var host = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: Int(NI_MAXHOST))
            guard getnameinfo(addr, socklen_t(addr.pointee.sa_len), &host, socklen_t(host.count),
                              nil, 0, NI_NUMERICHOST) == 0 else { continue }
            let name = String(cString: ptr.pointee.ifa_name)
            if name == "lo0" { continue }
            out.append("\(name) \(String(cString: host))")
        }
        return out.isEmpty ? "none" : out.joined(separator: ", ")
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/DDI/PairingFileStore.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import UniformTypeIdentifiers

/// Where the device pairing record lives.
///
/// The pairing file is what `idevicepair pair` writes on a Mac: a plist holding
/// the host certificate and keys that let a client authenticate to this device's
/// `lockdownd`. Mounting a DDI needs one because the mount goes through the same
/// trusted channel Xcode would use.
///
/// Only its *path* matters to the mounting code — the plist is parsed by the
/// idevice library, never here.
enum PairingFileStore {

    /// Types the import picker accepts.
    ///
    /// `.fileImporter` matches a picked file's type against this list, and the
    /// match has to hold for the file's *actual* UTI. A pairing record is an
    /// XML property list, which iOS types as `public.xml` — a sibling of
    /// `public.data`, not a subtype, so `.data` alone does not let it through.
    ///
    /// Two traps made the old list miss real files:
    ///  * `UTType(filenameExtension:)` returns nil for `plist` /
    ///    `mobiledevicepairing` on iOS — no such UTI is registered — so those
    ///    entries silently vanished and the list collapsed to `.data`.
    ///  * A picker only enables what the list *contains*; `.xml` has to be
    ///    listed on its own because it is not covered by `.data`.
    ///
    /// So declare every type explicitly with `UTType(tag:tagClass:conformingTo:)`
    /// (which does not depend on a system-registered UTI) and keep `.data` last
    /// as the permissive catch-all. The file is validated after the pick anyway,
    /// so a wider list costs nothing but a clearer failure.
    static let supportedContentTypes: [UTType] = {
        var types: [UTType] = []

        // The standard property-list type (both XML and binary forms).
        types.append(.propertyList)
        // A pairing record is usually XML: iOS reports `public.xml`, and the
        // picker must be told about it explicitly.
        types.append(.xml)

        // Apple's tooling and the community write these extensions. Build the
        // types from their tags rather than by filename lookup, so they exist
        // even where the system has no UTI registered for the extension.
        for ext in ["mobiledevicepairing", "mobiledevicepair"] {
            if let t = UTType(tag: ext, tagClass: .filenameExtension,
                              conformingTo: .propertyList) {
                types.append(t)
            }
        }
        // A plain `.plist` extension, in case the file keeps it.
        if let t = UTType(tag: "plist", tagClass: .filenameExtension,
                          conformingTo: .propertyList) {
            types.append(t)
        }

        // Permissive catch-all: every file conforms to `.data`, so this keeps
        // the picker from greying out a record saved under an unexpected
        // extension. Content is validated by `validate(_:)` after import.
        types.append(.data)

        return types
    }()

    /// Application Support/Pairing/pairingFile.plist — outside Documents so it
    /// isn't casually deleted from the Files app, since losing it means
    /// re-pairing from a Mac.
    static var storedURL: URL {
        let base = FileManager.default.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory,
                                            in: .userDomainMask)[0]
        return base.appendingPathComponent("Pairing/pairingFile.plist")
    }

    static var exists: Bool {
        FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: storedURL.path)
    }

    /// When the current file was imported — shown in the UI so a stale pairing
    /// file (a common cause of confusing mount failures) is at least visible.
    static var importedAt: Date? {
        try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: storedURL.path)[.modificationDate] as? Date
    }

    /// Copy a user-picked file into place.
    ///
    /// The picker hands back a security-scoped URL that is only readable inside
    /// a start/stop pair, so the bytes are copied out immediately rather than
    /// holding the URL.
    static func importFile(from url: URL) throws {
        let scoped = url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()
        defer { if scoped { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() } }

        let data = try Data(contentsOf: url)
        try validate(data)

        let dest = storedURL
        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dest.deletingLastPathComponent(),
                                                withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        // 0600 from the start: this file authenticates as a trusted host to the
        // device, so it deserves the same care as a private key.
        try data.write(to: dest, options: [.atomic, .completeFileProtection])
        try? FileManager.default.setAttributes([.posixPermissions: 0o600],
                                               ofItemAtPath: dest.path)
        ictrlLog("Pairing file imported (\(data.count)B)")
    }

    /// Posted after a pairing file is stored, so a screen showing the old
    /// state can refresh.
    static let didImport = Notification.Name("PairingFileStore.didImport")

    /// Store a file shared to the app ("Open in iCTRL"). iOS hands over a copy
    /// in an inbox folder of ours (Documents/Inbox, or tmp/<bundle id>-Inbox
    /// on newer systems), which is removed afterwards whatever the outcome.
    static func importShared(from url: URL) throws {
        defer {
            if url.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent.hasSuffix("Inbox") {
                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
            }
        }
        try importFile(from: url)
        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: didImport, object: nil)
    }

    static func remove() {
        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: storedURL)
    }

    /// Reject anything that clearly isn't a pairing record, so the failure lands
    /// at import time with a clear message instead of surfacing later as an
    /// opaque error from deep inside the mount.
    private static func validate(_ data: Data) throws {
        guard let plist = try? PropertyListSerialization.propertyList(
                from: data, options: [], format: nil) as? [String: Any] else {
            throw DDIError.invalidPairingFile("Not a property list. Expected the file "
                + "`idevicepair pair` writes (a .plist / .mobiledevicepairing).")
        }
        // These are the fields a lockdown pairing record always carries.
        let required = ["HostID", "HostCertificate", "HostPrivateKey"]
        let missing = required.filter { plist[$0] == nil }
        guard missing.isEmpty else {
            throw DDIError.invalidPairingFile(
                "Missing \(missing.joined(separator: ", ")). This looks like a "
                + "property list but not a pairing record — re-export it with "
                + "`idevicepair pair` (libimobiledevice) or pymobiledevice3.")
        }
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Models/AppLog.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import UIKit

/// File logging for the host app, one file per process.
///
/// Written because the interesting failures here happen on a device with no
/// debugger attached — a DDI mount that aborts inside a Rust FFI leaves nothing
/// behind but a crash report, and `print` goes nowhere once the app ships. One
/// file per PID keeps a crash-and-relaunch cycle from overwriting the very run
/// that failed, which is the one worth reading.
final class AppLog {
    static let shared = AppLog()

    /// Serial: several threads log (the mount runs on its own), and interleaved
    /// partial writes would corrupt exactly the file being relied on.
    private let queue = DispatchQueue(label: "com.copyapp.ictrl.applog")
    private let handle: FileHandle?
    private let formatter: DateFormatter

    let fileURL: URL?

    static var directory: URL? {
        guard let base = FileManager.default.urls(for: .libraryDirectory,
                                                  in: .userDomainMask).first else { return nil }
        let dir = base.appendingPathComponent("Logs/iCTRL", isDirectory: true)
        try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        return dir
    }

    private init() {
        formatter = DateFormatter()
        formatter.dateFormat = "HH:mm:ss.SSS"

        let pid = ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier
        let stamp = ISO8601DateFormatter()
        stamp.formatOptions = [.withYear, .withMonth, .withDay, .withTime]
        let name = "ictrl-app-\(Self.launchStamp())-pid\(pid).log"

        guard let dir = Self.directory else {
            fileURL = nil
            handle = nil
            return
        }
        let url = dir.appendingPathComponent(name)
        FileManager.default.createFile(atPath: url.path, contents: nil)
        fileURL = url
        handle = try? FileHandle(forWritingTo: url)

        Self.pruneOldFiles()
        write(header())
    }

    private static func launchStamp() -> String {
        let f = DateFormatter()
        f.dateFormat = "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss"
        return f.string(from: Date())
    }

    private func header() -> String {
        let d = UIDevice.current
        return """
        ── iCTRL app log ─────────────────────────────
        started : \(Date())
        pid     : \(ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier)
        device  : \(DeviceInfo.modelIdentifier) · \(d.systemName) \(d.systemVersion)
        app     : \(Bundle.main.infoDictionary?["CFBundleShortVersionString"] as? String ?? "?") \
        (\(Bundle.main.infoDictionary?["CFBundleVersion"] as? String ?? "?"))
        ──────────────────────────────────────────────
        """
    }

    func log(_ message: String) {
        let line = "[\(formatter.string(from: Date()))] \(message)"
        #if DEBUG
        print(line)
        #endif
        write(line)
    }

    private func write(_ text: String) {
        guard let handle else { return }
        queue.async {
            if let data = (text + "\n").data(using: .utf8) {
                try? handle.write(contentsOf: data)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Every log on disk, newest first.
    static func allFiles() -> [URL] {
        guard let dir = directory,
              let urls = try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
                  at: dir, includingPropertiesForKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]) else { return [] }
        return urls.filter { $0.pathExtension == "log" }.sorted {
            let a = (try? $0.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]).contentModificationDate) ?? .distantPast
            let b = (try? $1.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]).contentModificationDate) ?? .distantPast
            return a > b
        }
    }

    /// Keep the last 20 runs. A per-PID file means one crash loop could
    /// otherwise fill the container with hundreds of near-empty logs.
    private static func pruneOldFiles(keeping limit: Int = 20) {
        let files = allFiles()
        guard files.count > limit else { return }
        for url in files.dropFirst(limit) {
            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
        }
    }

    static func removeAll() {
        for url in allFiles() { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url) }
    }
}

/// Shorthand, so logging a line stays cheap enough to actually do.
func ictrlLog(_ message: String) { AppLog.shared.log(message) }
```

```swift
import SwiftUI
import Network

class AppState: ObservableObject {
    @Published var isServerRunning = false
    @Published var sessions: [AuthSession] = []
    @Published var pendingAuthRequest: PendingAuth?
    @Published var serverAddress: String = "—"
    @Published var serverError: String?

    @AppStorage("autoStartServer") var autoStartServer = false
    @AppStorage("serverPort") var serverPort = 8200
    @AppStorage("allowRemoteAccess") var allowRemoteAccess = false

    private var server: JSONRPCServer?

    struct PendingAuth: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let clientName: String
        let completion: (Bool) -> Void
    }

    init() {
        AuthManager.shared.delegate = self
        updateServerAddress()

        if autoStartServer {
            DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.5) { [weak self] in
                self?.startServer()
            }
        }
    }

    func startServer() {
        guard !isServerRunning else { return }

        let s = JSONRPCServer(port: UInt16(serverPort), localOnly: !allowRemoteAccess)
        server = s

        s.onStateChange = { [weak self] running in
            DispatchQueue.main.async {
                self?.isServerRunning = running
                if running {
                    self?.serverError = nil
                    self?.updateServerAddress()
                }
            }
        }

        s.onRPCRequest = { method, params, completion in
            completion(nil, .serverError("RPC not available in app mode. Use the UITest runner for automation."))
        }

        do {
            try s.start()
            serverError = nil
        } catch {
            print("🔴 Failed to start server: \(error)")
            serverError = error.localizedDescription
            isServerRunning = false
        }
    }

    func stopServer() {
        server?.stop()
        server = nil
        isServerRunning = false
    }

    func refreshSessions() {
        sessions = AuthManager.shared.activeSessions
    }

    func revokeSession(id: String) {
        AuthManager.shared.revokeSession(id: id)
        refreshSessions()
    }

    func revokeAllSessions() {
        AuthManager.shared.revokeAll()
        refreshSessions()
    }

    func updateServerAddress() {
        let ip = allowRemoteAccess ? (getWiFiAddress() ?? "127.0.0.1") : "127.0.0.1"
        serverAddress = "\(ip):\(serverPort)"
    }

    private func getWiFiAddress() -> String? {
        var address: String?
        var ifaddr: UnsafeMutablePointer<ifaddrs>?

        guard getifaddrs(&ifaddr) == 0, let firstAddr = ifaddr else { return nil }
        defer { freeifaddrs(ifaddr) }

        for ptr in sequence(first: firstAddr, next: { $0.pointee.ifa_next }) {
            let interface = ptr.pointee
            // ifa_addr may be NULL for an interface without an address.
            guard let sa = interface.ifa_addr, sa.pointee.sa_family == UInt8(AF_INET) else { continue }

            let name = String(cString: interface.ifa_name)
            guard name == "en0" else { continue }

            var hostname = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: Int(NI_MAXHOST))
            guard getnameinfo(
                sa, socklen_t(sa.pointee.sa_len),
                &hostname, socklen_t(hostname.count),
                nil, 0, NI_NUMERICHOST
            ) == 0 else { continue }
            address = String(cString: hostname)
        }

        return address
    }
}

extension AppState: AuthManagerDelegate {
    func authManager(_ manager: AuthManager, didReceiveAuthRequest clientName: String, requestID: String,
                     nearby: Bool, fingerprint: String?, completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        DispatchQueue.main.async {
            self.pendingAuthRequest = PendingAuth(clientName: clientName, completion: completion)
        }
    }

    func authManager(_ manager: AuthManager, didExpireAuthRequest clientName: String, requestID: String) {
        DispatchQueue.main.async {
            if self.pendingAuthRequest?.clientName == clientName { self.pendingAuthRequest = nil }
        }
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Models/NetworkPermission.swift`:

```swift
import CoreTelephony
import Foundation
import Network
import UIKit

/// The two network permissions iCTRL depends on, probed at every launch.
///
/// Neither has an API that asks for it directly: iOS shows each prompt the
/// first time the app does the thing it covers. Probing at launch puts both
/// prompts on a fresh install's first screen, instead of in the middle of the
/// DDI setup, where a silent denial looks like a download or tunnel failure.
///
/// - Network data (mainland China models): "Allow iCTRL to use wireless data?"
///   appears on the first request leaving the device; until it is allowed the
///   app has no network at all, and the DDI download fails.
/// - Local Network: the DDI mount connects to the tunnel's private address,
///   which iOS gates behind it.
@MainActor
final class NetworkPermission: ObservableObject {
    enum Status: Equatable { case unknown, allowed, denied }

    @Published private(set) var networkData: Status = .unknown
    @Published private(set) var localNetwork: Status = .unknown

    /// Something denied: what the launch alert names.
    var denied: [String] {
        var out: [String] = []
        if networkData == .denied { out.append(L10n.t(.networkDataPermission)) }
        if localNetwork == .denied { out.append(L10n.t(.localNetworkPermission)) }
        return out
    }

    private let cellular = CTCellularData()
    private var browser: NWBrowser?

    func probe() {
        probeNetworkData()
        probeLocalNetwork()
    }

    private func probeNetworkData() {
        // Reports .restricted only where the per-app data switch exists and
        // is off; elsewhere it is .notRestricted.
        cellular.cellularDataRestrictionDidUpdateNotifier = { [weak self] state in
            Task { @MainActor in
                guard let self else { return }
                switch state {
                case .restricted: self.networkData = .denied
                case .notRestricted: self.networkData = .allowed
                default: break
                }
                ictrlLog("Network data permission: \(self.networkData)")
            }
        }
        // A tiny request to the host the DDI download uses: on a fresh install
        // this is what raises the prompt.
        var req = URLRequest(url: DeveloperDiskImageStore.Component.buildManifest.remoteURL, timeoutInterval: 10)
        req.httpMethod = "HEAD"
        URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: req) { _, resp, err in
            ictrlLog("Network probe: \((resp as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode.description ?? err?.localizedDescription ?? "no answer")")
        }.resume()
    }

    private func probeLocalNetwork() {
        // Browsing for a Bonjour service is the documented way to raise the
        // Local Network prompt, and the browser reports a denial as a DNS
        // policy error. The service type must be listed in NSBonjourServices.
        let b = NWBrowser(for: .bonjour(type: "_ictrl._tcp", domain: nil), using: .tcp)
        b.stateUpdateHandler = { [weak self] state in
            Task { @MainActor in
                guard let self else { return }
                switch state {
                case .ready:
                    self.localNetwork = .allowed
                case .waiting(let err), .failed(let err):
                    if case .dns(let code) = err, code == DNSServiceErrorType(kDNSServiceErr_PolicyDenied) {
                        self.localNetwork = .denied
                    }
                default:
                    return
                }
                ictrlLog("Local Network permission: \(self.localNetwork)")
            }
        }
        b.start(queue: .main)
        browser = b
        // Long enough for the user to answer the prompt; the state is kept.
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 60) { [weak self] in
            self?.browser?.cancel()
            self?.browser = nil
        }
    }
}
```
