`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Models/RunnerAdmin.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

/// State behind the runner's client list and live log, shared by both screens.
///
/// Everything comes from the runner over `RunnerClient`: `config` lists and
/// revokes sessions, `logs` returns the recent log. Errors are kept as a short
/// user-facing notice instead of being thrown at the views.
@MainActor
final class RunnerAdmin: ObservableObject {
    struct Client: Identifiable, Equatable {
        let id: String
        let name: String
        let grantedAt: Date?
        let lastActiveAt: Date?
        /// Where its last request came from; nil before it was recorded.
        let lastAddress: String?
        /// `PeerSource` raw value: local, lan, nearby, vpn, cellular, other.
        let lastVia: String?
    }

    @Published private(set) var isPaired: Bool
    @Published private(set) var pairing = false
    /// Why the last operation failed, in the user's language; nil when fine.
    @Published private(set) var notice: String?
    @Published private(set) var clients: [Client] = []
    /// Who can reach the runner right now, from its `config`; nil until known.
    @Published private(set) var visibility: Visibility?
    /// Nearby discovery is switched on but not advertising yet (waiting for
    /// Wi-Fi or permission): `visibility` says what was chosen, this says it
    /// is not in effect.
    @Published private(set) var nearbyPending = false
    /// The runner reported that iOS refused it Local Network access.
    @Published private(set) var localNetworkDenied = false

    /// The runner's reach, widest first. Only local is safe from other devices.
    enum Visibility: Hashable {
        /// Loopback only: apps on this device and a computer over USB.
        case local
        /// Remote access on: anyone on the same network can try to pair.
        case lan
        /// Remote access on and advertised over AWDL to nearby Apple devices.
        case lanAndNearby
    }
    @Published private(set) var clientsLoaded = false
    @Published private(set) var logLines: [String] = []
    @Published private(set) var logsLoaded = false

    private let client: RunnerClient
    /// The runner keeps 500 lines at most per `logs` call.
    static let logLineLimit = 500

    init(port: Int) {
        client = RunnerClient(port: port)
        isPaired = client.isPaired
    }

    var ownSessionID: String? { client.sessionID }
    var otherClients: [Client] { clients.filter { $0.id != ownSessionID } }

    // MARK: - Pairing

    func connect() async {
        guard !pairing else { return }
        pairing = true
        notice = nil
        defer { pairing = false }
        do {
            try await client.pair()
            isPaired = true
            ictrlLog("Runner admin: paired as \(client.sessionID ?? "?")")
            await loadClients()
        } catch {
            handle(error)
        }
    }

    // MARK: - Clients

    func loadClients() async {
        guard client.isPaired else { isPaired = false; return }
        do {
            let result = try await client.call("config")
            clients = Self.parseClients(result["sessions"])
            visibility = Self.parseVisibility(result)
            let nearby = result["nearby"] as? [String: Any]
            nearbyPending = (nearby?["enabled"] as? Bool) == true && (nearby?["advertising"] as? Bool) != true
            localNetworkDenied = (result["nearby"] as? [String: Any])?["local_network"] as? String == "denied"
            clientsLoaded = true
            notice = nil
        } catch {
            handle(error)
        }
    }

    func revoke(_ id: String) async {
        do {
            let result = try await client.call("config", ["revoke_session_id": id])
            clients = Self.parseClients(result["sessions"])
            visibility = Self.parseVisibility(result)
            ictrlLog("Runner admin: revoked session \(id)")
        } catch {
            handle(error)
        }
    }

    /// Revoke every client except this app, one by one: the runner's
    /// `clear_sessions` would cut this app off too.
    func revokeOthers() async {
        for other in otherClients {
            await revoke(other.id)
            if !isPaired { return }
        }
    }

    /// Revoke this app's own key on the runner, then forget it here.
    func disconnect() async {
        if let own = ownSessionID {
            _ = try? await client.call("config", ["revoke_session_id": own])
        }
        client.forget()
        isPaired = false
        clients = []
        clientsLoaded = false
        visibility = nil
        logLines = []
        logsLoaded = false
        ictrlLog("Runner admin: disconnected")
    }

    // MARK: - Visibility

    @Published private(set) var changingVisibility = false

    /// Set who can reach the runner. Turning remote access on or off restarts
    /// the runner's listener, so the reply can be lost; the state is read back
    /// afterwards either way.
    func setVisibility(_ target: Visibility) async {
        guard target != visibility, !changingVisibility else { return }
        changingVisibility = true
        defer { changingVisibility = false }
        var params: [String: Any]
        switch target {
        case .local: params = ["allow_remote_access": false]
        case .lan: params = ["allow_remote_access": true, "nearby_discovery": false]
        case .lanAndNearby: params = ["allow_remote_access": true, "nearby_discovery": true]
        }
        do {
            _ = try await client.call("config", params)
            ictrlLog("Runner admin: visibility -> \(target)")
        } catch RunnerClient.Failure.notRunning {
            // The listener restarting under the reply; checked below.
        } catch {
            handle(error)
        }
        // Nearby confirms its advertisement a moment after it is switched on.
        try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 1_500_000_000)
        await loadClients()
    }

    // MARK: - Logs

    func loadLogs() async {
        guard client.isPaired else { isPaired = false; return }
        do {
            let result = try await client.call("logs", ["max_elements": Self.logLineLimit])
            let lines = result["lines"] as? [String] ?? []
            if lines != logLines { logLines = lines }
            logsLoaded = true
            notice = nil
        } catch {
            handle(error)
        }
    }

    // MARK: - Helpers

    private func handle(_ error: Error) {
        switch error as? RunnerClient.Failure {
        case .notRunning:
            notice = L10n.t(.runnerNotRunningHint)
        case .notPaired:
            isPaired = false
        case .keyRejected:
            isPaired = false
            clients = []
            notice = L10n.t(.keyRejectedHint)
        case .pairDenied:
            notice = L10n.t(.pairDeniedHint)
        case .pairUnavailable(let seconds, _):
            notice = String(format: L10n.t(.retryInSeconds), seconds)
        case .server(let message):
            notice = message
        case nil:
            notice = error.localizedDescription
        }
        ictrlLog("Runner admin: \(error)")
    }

    private static let iso = ISO8601DateFormatter()

    /// The chosen setting. Nearby counts as chosen while it is switched on,
    /// advertised or not — otherwise "LAN" could not be picked to switch off
    /// a nearby discovery that is still waiting for Wi-Fi; `nearbyPending`
    /// tells the two apart for display.
    private static func parseVisibility(_ config: [String: Any]) -> Visibility? {
        guard let remote = config["allow_remote_access"] as? Bool else { return nil }
        guard remote else { return .local }
        let nearby = config["nearby"] as? [String: Any]
        return (nearby?["enabled"] as? Bool) == true ? .lanAndNearby : .lan
    }

    private static func parseClients(_ value: Any?) -> [Client] {
        let rows = value as? [[String: Any]] ?? []
        return rows.compactMap { row in
            guard let id = row["session_id"] as? String else { return nil }
            return Client(id: id,
                          name: row["client_name"] as? String ?? id,
                          grantedAt: (row["granted_at"] as? String).flatMap(iso.date(from:)),
                          lastActiveAt: (row["last_active_at"] as? String).flatMap(iso.date(from:)),
                          lastAddress: row["last_address"] as? String,
                          lastVia: row["last_via"] as? String)
        }
        .sorted { ($0.lastActiveAt ?? .distantPast) > ($1.lastActiveAt ?? .distantPast) }
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Models/RunnerClient.swift`:

```swift
import CryptoKit
import Foundation

/// An authenticated connection from this app to the runner on the same device.
///
/// The runner owns the authorized clients and its log; this app is a separate
/// process and can only reach them over the runner's encrypted `/rpc`, like any
/// other client. So it pairs once — the user approves it in the runner's
/// notification, exactly as for a computer — and keeps the key in its own
/// Keychain. Nothing here bypasses that approval: an app that could manage the
/// runner's clients without it could also have granted itself access.
///
/// Calls go to 127.0.0.1 only. Pairing uses the X25519 mode so the key never
/// crosses even the loopback interface in the clear.
final class RunnerClient {
    enum Failure: LocalizedError, Equatable {
        /// Nothing answers on the port: the runner isn't running.
        case notRunning
        /// No key yet; `pair()` first.
        case notPaired
        /// The runner no longer accepts our key (revoked, expired, reinstalled).
        case keyRejected
        case pairDenied
        /// Another request is waiting, or one was just refused.
        case pairUnavailable(retryAfter: Int, busy: Bool)
        case server(String)

        var errorDescription: String? {
            switch self {
            case .notRunning: return "The runner is not running."
            case .notPaired: return "Not connected to the runner."
            case .keyRejected: return "The runner no longer accepts this app's key."
            case .pairDenied: return "The request was refused or not answered in time."
            case .pairUnavailable(let s, let busy):
                return busy ? "Another request is waiting for approval (retry in \(s)s)."
                            : "A request was just refused; retry in \(s)s."
            case .server(let m): return m
            }
        }
    }

    /// What the runner shows in its approval prompt and client list.
    static let clientName = "iCTRL App"
    private static let keychainAccount = "runner-admin"

    private struct Record: Codable {
        var key: String   // hex, 32 bytes
        var tok: String   // hex, 4 bytes: the session id on the runner
    }

    let port: Int
    private var record: Record?

    init(port: Int) {
        self.port = port
        if let data = KeychainStore.load(account: Self.keychainAccount) {
            record = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Record.self, from: data)
        }
    }

    var isPaired: Bool { record != nil }
    /// This app's own session id on the runner, so the client list can mark it.
    var sessionID: String? { record?.tok }

    func forget() {
        record = nil
        KeychainStore.clear(account: Self.keychainAccount)
    }

    // MARK: - Pairing

    /// Ask the runner for a key. Blocks until the user answers the runner's
    /// notification or it times out (60 s on the runner side).
    func pair() async throws {
        let priv = Curve25519.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey()
        let pub = priv.publicKey.rawRepresentation
        let (status, body) = try await post("/pair", json: [
            "client_name": Self.clientName,
            "pub": pub.base64EncodedString(),
        ], timeout: 90)

        switch status {
        case 200: break
        case 403: throw Failure.pairDenied
        case 429:
            let error = body["error"] as? [String: Any]
            let wait = error?["retry_after"] as? Int ?? body["retry_after"] as? Int ?? 15
            let busy = error?["code"] as? String == "pair_busy"
            throw Failure.pairUnavailable(retryAfter: wait, busy: busy)
        default: throw Failure.server(Self.message(body, status: status))
        }

        guard let devicePubB64 = body["pub"] as? String,
              let devicePub = Data(base64Encoded: devicePubB64),
              let wrappedHex = body["token_ct"] as? String,
              let wrapped = Data(hexString: wrappedHex), wrapped.count == 32 else {
            throw Failure.server("Malformed pairing response")
        }
        let peer = try Curve25519.KeyAgreement.PublicKey(rawRepresentation: devicePub)
        let shared = try priv.sharedSecretFromKeyAgreement(with: peer).withUnsafeBytes { Data($0) }
        let kWrap = SecureEnvelope.hmac(shared, Data(SecureEnvelope.labelPair.utf8) + pub + devicePub)
        let pad = SecureEnvelope.hmac(kWrap, Data(SecureEnvelope.labelWrap.utf8))
        let key = Data(zip(wrapped, pad).map { $0 ^ $1 })

        let rec = Record(key: key.hexString, tok: SecureEnvelope.tokenId(for: key))
        record = rec
        if let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(rec) {
            KeychainStore.save(data, account: Self.keychainAccount)
        }
    }

    // MARK: - RPC

    /// One enveloped JSON-RPC call; returns its `result` object.
    func call(_ method: String, _ params: [String: Any] = [:], timeout: TimeInterval = 15) async throws -> [String: Any] {
        guard let record, let key = Data(hexString: record.key), let tok4 = Data(hexString: record.tok),
              let nonce = SecureEnvelope.randomBytes(16) else { throw Failure.notPaired }

        let request: [String: Any] = ["jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params, "id": 1]
        let plaintext = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: request)
        let ts = UInt64(Date().timeIntervalSince1970)
        let kEnc = SecureEnvelope.hmac(key, Data(SecureEnvelope.labelEncRequest.utf8) + nonce)
        let kMac = SecureEnvelope.hmac(key, Data(SecureEnvelope.labelMac.utf8) + nonce)
        let ct = SecureEnvelope.keystreamXOR(key: kEnc, nonce: nonce, data: plaintext)
        let tag = SecureEnvelope.hmac(kMac, Data("v1".utf8) + tok4 + SecureEnvelope.be64(ts) + nonce + ct)

        let (status, body) = try await post("/rpc", json: [
            "v": 1, "tok": record.tok, "ts": Int(ts), "nonce": nonce.hexString,
            "ct": ct.base64EncodedString(), "tag": tag.hexString,
        ], timeout: timeout)

        if status == 401 {
            // Revoked from elsewhere, expired, or the runner was reinstalled:
            // the key is dead for good, so drop it rather than retry with it.
            forget()
            throw Failure.keyRejected
        }
        guard status == 200 else { throw Failure.server(Self.message(body, status: status)) }

        guard let respCtB64 = body["ct"] as? String, let respCt = Data(base64Encoded: respCtB64),
              let respTagHex = body["tag"] as? String, let respTag = Data(hexString: respTagHex),
              SecureEnvelope.tagMatches(respTag, message: Data("resp".utf8) + nonce + respCt, key: kMac) else {
            throw Failure.server("Response failed verification")
        }
        let kEncResp = SecureEnvelope.hmac(key, Data(SecureEnvelope.labelEncResponse.utf8) + nonce)
        let decoded = SecureEnvelope.keystreamXOR(key: kEncResp, nonce: nonce, data: respCt)
        guard let reply = try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: decoded) as? [String: Any] else {
            throw Failure.server("Malformed response")
        }
        if let error = reply["error"] as? [String: Any] {
            throw Failure.server(error["message"] as? String ?? "RPC error")
        }
        return reply["result"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
    }

    // MARK: - HTTP

    private func post(_ path: String, json: [String: Any], timeout: TimeInterval) async throws -> (Int, [String: Any]) {
        var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)\(path)")!)
        request.httpMethod = "POST"
        request.timeoutInterval = timeout
        request.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
        request.httpBody = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: json)
        do {
            let (data, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
            let status = (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode ?? 0
            let body = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data)) as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
            return (status, body)
        } catch let error as URLError where [.cannotConnectToHost, .networkConnectionLost,
                                             .cannotFindHost, .notConnectedToInternet].contains(error.code) {
            throw Failure.notRunning
        }
    }

    private static func message(_ body: [String: Any], status: Int) -> String {
        if let error = body["error"] as? [String: Any], let message = error["message"] as? String { return message }
        return "HTTP \(status)"
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Models/RunnerStatus.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

/// Live status of the automation server, probed over HTTP.
///
/// The server runs in the XCUITest runner — a separate process this app cannot
/// see into — so "is it running?" is answered by asking it, not by inspecting
/// local state. `/schema` is unauthenticated and cheap, and it carries the
/// version and capabilities, which is exactly what's worth showing.
@MainActor
final class RunnerStatus: ObservableObject {

    struct Info: Equatable {
        var serverVersion: String?
        var protocolVersion: Int?
        var capabilities: [String] = []
        var methodCount: Int?
    }

    enum State: Equatable {
        case unknown
        case checking
        case running(Info)
        case stopped
    }

    @Published private(set) var state: State = .unknown
    @Published private(set) var lastChecked: Date?

    private var pollTask: Task<Void, Never>?
    private let port: Int

    init(port: Int) { self.port = port }

    var isRunning: Bool { if case .running = state { return true }; return false }

    /// Poll while the view is on screen. The runner can be started or killed
    /// from outside this app (a URL scheme, a crash, iOS reclaiming it), so a
    /// one-shot check at appear would go stale while the user is looking at it.
    func startPolling(every seconds: TimeInterval = 3) {
        stopPolling()
        pollTask = Task { [weak self] in
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                await self?.check()
                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(seconds * 1_000_000_000))
            }
        }
    }

    func stopPolling() {
        pollTask?.cancel()
        pollTask = nil
    }

    func check() async {
        if case .unknown = state { state = .checking }

        var request = URLRequest(url: URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)/schema")!)
        // Short: this is a loopback call to a process on this device. Anything
        // slower than a moment means it isn't there.
        request.timeoutInterval = 2
        request.cachePolicy = .reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData

        do {
            let (data, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
            guard let http = response as? HTTPURLResponse, http.statusCode == 200,
                  let json = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any] else {
                state = .stopped
                lastChecked = Date()
                return
            }
            var info = Info()
            info.serverVersion = json["server_version"] as? String
            info.protocolVersion = json["protocol_version"] as? Int
            info.capabilities = json["capability_tags"] as? [String] ?? []
            info.methodCount = (json["methods"] as? [Any])?.count
            state = .running(info)
        } catch {
            state = .stopped
        }
        lastChecked = Date()
    }
}
```

```swift
import SwiftUI
import UIKit

/// Every log this app has written, one per run, newest first.
///
/// Exists so a failure that happened on a device with no debugger can leave with
/// the user: tap a run, read it, share it. The per-PID split is what makes that
/// useful — the run that crashed is still its own file after the relaunch.
struct LogListView: View {
    @State private var files = AppLog.allFiles()
    @State private var shareURL: ShareItem?
    @State private var confirmClear = false

    /// `sheet(item:)` wants Identifiable, and URL isn't.
    private struct ShareItem: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let url: URL
    }

    var body: some View {
        List {
            // The runner is a separate process with its own log; it is read
            // live over the runner's RPC rather than from a file here.
            Section {
                NavigationLink {
                    RunnerLogsView()
                } label: {
                    Label(L10n.t(.runnerLogs), systemImage: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right")
                }
            } header: {
                Text(L10n.t(.runnerSection))
            }

            Section {
                if files.isEmpty {
                    Text("No logs yet.")
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }

                ForEach(files, id: \.self) { url in
                    NavigationLink {
                        LogDetailView(url: url)
                    } label: {
                        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                            HStack {
                                Text(Self.title(for: url))
                                if url == AppLog.shared.fileURL {
                                    Text("current")
                                        .font(.caption2)
                                        .padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.vertical, 2)
                                        .background(Capsule().fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.15)))
                                        .foregroundColor(.accentColor)
                                }
                            }
                            Text(Self.subtitle(for: url))
                                .font(.caption)
                                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                        }
                    }
                    .swipeActions {
                        Button("Share") { shareURL = ShareItem(url: url) }
                            .tint(.blue)
                    }
                }
            } header: {
                Text(L10n.t(.appLogsSection))
            }
        }
        .navigationTitle("Logs")
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        .toolbar {
            ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarTrailing) {
                Menu {
                    if let current = AppLog.shared.fileURL {
                        Button {
                            shareURL = ShareItem(url: current)
                        } label: {
                            Label("Share current log", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up")
                        }
                    }
                    Button(role: .destructive) {
                        confirmClear = true
                    } label: {
                        Label("Delete all logs", systemImage: "trash")
                    }
                } label: {
                    Image(systemName: "ellipsis.circle")
                }
            }
        }
        .confirmationDialog("Delete all logs?", isPresented: $confirmClear, titleVisibility: .visible) {
            Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) {
                AppLog.removeAll()
                files = AppLog.allFiles()
            }
        } message: {
            Text("This removes every saved run, including the current one.")
        }
        .sheet(item: $shareURL) { item in
            ShareSheet(items: [item.url])
        }
        .onAppear { files = AppLog.allFiles() }
    }

    /// "Aug 15, 1:42 PM" — when the run happened, which is how you'd look for it.
    private static func title(for url: URL) -> String {
        let date = (try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]).contentModificationDate)
        guard let date else { return url.lastPathComponent }
        return date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened)
    }

    private static func subtitle(for url: URL) -> String {
        let size = (try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey]).fileSize) ?? 0
        let pid = url.lastPathComponent
            .split(separator: "-").last?
            .replacingOccurrences(of: ".log", with: "") ?? ""
        return "\(pid) · \(ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount: Int64(size), countStyle: .file))"
    }
}

/// One log's contents.
private struct LogDetailView: View {
    let url: URL
    @State private var text = ""
    @State private var showShare = false

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            Text(text.isEmpty ? "(empty)" : text)
                .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .textSelection(.enabled)
                .padding()
        }
        .navigationTitle(url.lastPathComponent)
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        .toolbar {
            ToolbarItem(placement: .navigationBarTrailing) {
                Button { showShare = true } label: {
                    Image(systemName: "square.and.arrow.up")
                }
            }
        }
        .sheet(isPresented: $showShare) { ShareSheet(items: [url]) }
        .onAppear {
            text = (try? String(contentsOf: url, encoding: .utf8)) ?? "(unreadable)"
        }
    }
}

/// The system share sheet. Shares the file URL rather than its text, so the
/// receiving app gets a real .log attachment instead of a wall of pasted lines.
struct ShareSheet: UIViewControllerRepresentable {
    let items: [Any]

    func makeUIViewController(context: Context) -> UIActivityViewController {
        UIActivityViewController(activityItems: items, applicationActivities: nil)
    }

    func updateUIViewController(_ controller: UIActivityViewController, context: Context) {}
}
```

```swift
struct RunnerVisibilityRow: View {

                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)

                    .font(.caption)
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .disabled(admin.changingVisibility)
    }

    /// 🟢 only for loopback; anything another device can reach is 🟡.
    static func text(_ visibility: RunnerAdmin.Visibility) -> String {
        switch visibility {
        case .local: return L10n.t(.visibilityLocal)
        case .lan: return L10n.t(.visibilityLAN)
        case .lanAndNearby: return L10n.t(.visibilityLANNearby)
        }
    }

// MARK: - Authorized clients

/// Every client holding a key to the runner, with revocation.
struct RunnerClientsView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var admin: RunnerAdmin
    @State private var pendingRevoke: RunnerAdmin.Client?
    @State private var confirmRevokeOthers = false
    @State private var confirmDisconnect = false

    var body: some View {
        List {
            if admin.isPaired {
                if let visibility = admin.visibility {
                    Section {
                        RunnerVisibilityRow(visibility: visibility)
                    }
                }
                clientsSection
                actionsSection
            } else {
                RunnerConnectSection()
            }
        }
        .navigationTitle(L10n.t(.authorizedClients))
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        .refreshable { await admin.loadClients() }
        // Alerts, not confirmation dialogs: newer iOS draws a dialog as a
        // popover pointing at its anchor, which from a list points at the
        // wrong row — and one attached to a row is not shown after a swipe.
        .alert(String(format: L10n.t(.revokeConfirmTitle), pendingRevoke?.name ?? ""),
               isPresented: Binding(get: { pendingRevoke != nil }, set: { if !$0 { pendingRevoke = nil } }),
               presenting: pendingRevoke) { client in
            Button(L10n.t(.cancelButton), role: .cancel) {}
            Button(L10n.t(.revokeButton), role: .destructive) {
                Task { await admin.revoke(client.id) }
            }
        } message: { _ in
            Text(L10n.t(.revokeConfirmBody))
        }
        .alert(String(format: L10n.t(.revokeOthersConfirm), admin.otherClients.count),
               isPresented: $confirmRevokeOthers) {
            Button(L10n.t(.cancelButton), role: .cancel) {}
            Button(L10n.t(.revokeOthers), role: .destructive) {
                Task { await admin.revokeOthers() }
            }
        } message: {
            Text(L10n.t(.revokeConfirmBody))
        }
        .alert(L10n.t(.disconnectThisApp), isPresented: $confirmDisconnect) {
            Button(L10n.t(.cancelButton), role: .cancel) {}
            Button(L10n.t(.disconnectThisApp), role: .destructive) {
                Task { await admin.disconnect() }
            }
        } message: {
            Text(L10n.t(.disconnectConfirmBody))
        }
        // A new client can pair while this screen is open; keep it current.
        .task(id: admin.isPaired) {
            while !Task.isCancelled && admin.isPaired {
                await admin.loadClients()
                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 5_000_000_000)
            }
        }
    }

    private var clientsSection: some View {
        Section {
            if !admin.clientsLoaded && admin.notice == nil {
                HStack { Spacer(); ProgressView(); Spacer() }
            } else if admin.clients.isEmpty {
                Text(L10n.t(.noClients)).foregroundColor(.secondary)
            }
            ForEach(admin.clients) { client in
                ClientRow(client: client, isSelf: client.id == admin.ownSessionID)
                    .swipeActions {
                        if client.id != admin.ownSessionID {
                            Button(L10n.t(.revokeButton), role: .destructive) { pendingRevoke = client }
                        }
                    }
                    .contextMenu {
                        if client.id != admin.ownSessionID {
                            Button(role: .destructive) { pendingRevoke = client } label: {
                                Label(L10n.t(.revokeButton), systemImage: "xmark.circle")
                            }
                        }
                    }

            }
        } header: {
            Text(L10n.t(.authorizedClients))
        } footer: {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                NoticeText()
                Text(L10n.t(.clientsFooter))
            }
        }
    }

    private var actionsSection: some View {
        Section {
            if !admin.otherClients.isEmpty {
                Button(role: .destructive) { confirmRevokeOthers = true } label: {
                    Label(L10n.t(.revokeOthers), systemImage: "person.crop.circle.badge.xmark")
                }

            }
            Button(role: .destructive) { confirmDisconnect = true } label: {
                Label(L10n.t(.disconnectThisApp), systemImage: "personalhotspot.slash")
            }

        }
    }
}

private struct ClientRow: View {
    let client: RunnerAdmin.Client
    let isSelf: Bool

    /// The app ships no .lproj, so Foundation formats in English by default;
    /// follow the language the rest of the UI is shown in instead.
    private static let locale: Locale = {
        switch L10n.lang {
        case .zhHans: return Locale(identifier: "zh-Hans")
        case .zhHant: return Locale(identifier: "zh-Hant")
        default: return Locale.current
        }
    }()

    private static let relative: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = {
        let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()
        f.unitsStyle = .short
        f.dateTimeStyle = .named
        f.locale = locale
        return f
    }()

    private static let absolute: DateFormatter = {
        let f = DateFormatter()
        f.locale = locale
        f.dateStyle = .medium
        f.timeStyle = .short
        return f
    }()

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
            HStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text(client.name).lineLimit(1)
                if isSelf {
                    Text(L10n.t(.thisApp))
                        .font(.caption2)
                        .padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.vertical, 2)
                        .background(Capsule().fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.15)))
                        .foregroundColor(.accentColor)
                }
            }
            if let via = client.lastVia {
                HStack(spacing: 6) {
                    HStack(spacing: 3) {
                        Image(systemName: Self.sourceIcon(via))
                        Text(Self.sourceName(via))
                    }
                    .font(.caption.weight(.medium))
                    .foregroundColor(Self.sourceColor(via))
                    // Loopback says nothing useful ("127.0.0.1"); the source does.
                    if let address = client.lastAddress, via != PeerSource.local.rawValue {
                        Text(address)
                            .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
                            .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                            .lineLimit(1)
                            .truncationMode(.middle)
                            .textSelection(.enabled)
                    }
                }
            }
            Text(subtitle)
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 2)
    }

    private static func sourceName(_ via: String) -> String {
        switch PeerSource(rawValue: via) {
        case .local: return L10n.t(.viaLocal)
        case .lan: return L10n.t(.viaLAN)
        case .nearby: return L10n.t(.viaNearby)
        case .vpn: return L10n.t(.viaVPN)
        case .cellular: return L10n.t(.viaCellular)
        case .other, nil: return L10n.t(.viaOther)
        }
    }

    private static func sourceIcon(_ via: String) -> String {
        switch PeerSource(rawValue: via) {
        case .local: return "iphone"
        case .lan: return "wifi"
        case .nearby: return "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right"
        case .vpn: return "lock.shield"
        case .cellular: return "antenna.radiowaves.left.and.right"
        case .other, nil: return "network"
        }
    }

    private static func sourceColor(_ via: String) -> Color {
        switch PeerSource(rawValue: via) {
        case .local: return .secondary
        case .lan: return .blue
        case .nearby: return .purple
        case .vpn: return .orange
        default: return .secondary
        }
    }

    private var subtitle: String {
        var parts = [String]()
        if let granted = client.grantedAt {
            parts.append(String(format: L10n.t(.pairedAt), Self.absolute.string(from: granted)))
        }
        if let active = client.lastActiveAt {
            // Clamp: the runner's clock reading can be a moment ahead of ours.
            let now = Date()
            parts.append(String(format: L10n.t(.lastActive),
                                Self.relative.localizedString(for: min(active, now), relativeTo: now)))
        }
        parts.append(client.id)
        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
    }
}

// MARK: - Runner log

/// The runner's recent log, pulled every 2 seconds while on screen.
struct RunnerLogsView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var admin: RunnerAdmin
    @State private var live = true
    @State private var filter = ""
    @State private var refreshing = false
    @State private var shareItem: ShareText?

    private struct ShareText: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let text: String
    }

    private static let pollInterval: UInt64 = 2_000_000_000

    private var shownLines: [String] {
        filter.isEmpty ? admin.logLines : admin.logLines.filter { $0.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(filter) }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            if admin.isPaired {
                logList
            } else {
                List { RunnerConnectSection() }
            }
        }
        .navigationTitle(L10n.t(.runnerLogs))
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        .toolbar {
            if admin.isPaired {
                ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .navigationBarTrailing) {
                    Button {
                        live.toggle()
                    } label: {
                        Image(systemName: live ? "pause.circle" : "play.circle")
                    }
                    .accessibilityLabel(live ? L10n.t(.pausedLabel) : L10n.t(.liveLabel))
                    Button {
                        Task { await refresh() }
                    } label: {
                        if refreshing { ProgressView().controlSize(.small) } else { Image(systemName: "arrow.clockwise") }
                    }
                    .disabled(refreshing)
                    Menu {
                        Button {
                            UIPasteboard.general.string = shownLines.joined(separator: "\n")
                        } label: {
                            Label(L10n.t(.copyButton), systemImage: "doc.on.doc")
                        }
                        Button {
                            shareItem = ShareText(text: shownLines.joined(separator: "\n"))
                        } label: {
                            Label("Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up")
                        }
                    } label: {
                        Image(systemName: "ellipsis.circle")
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .sheet(item: $shareItem) { item in ShareSheet(items: [item.text]) }
        // Pull on entry, then keep pulling while the screen is visible. `.task`
        // is cancelled when the view goes away, which ends the polling.
        .task(id: admin.isPaired) {
            guard admin.isPaired else { return }
            await admin.loadLogs()
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: Self.pollInterval)
                if live && !Task.isCancelled { await admin.loadLogs() }
            }
        }
    }

    private var logList: some View {
        ScrollViewReader { proxy in
            List {
                Section {
                    if admin.logsLoaded && shownLines.isEmpty {
                        Text(L10n.t(.noLogLines)).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    } else if !admin.logsLoaded && admin.notice == nil {
                        HStack { Spacer(); ProgressView(); Spacer() }
                    }
                    ForEach(Array(shownLines.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, line in
                        Text(line)
                            .font(.system(.caption2, design: .monospaced))
                            .textSelection(.enabled)
                            .listRowInsets(EdgeInsets(top: 1, leading: 12, bottom: 1, trailing: 12))
                            .listRowSeparator(.hidden)
                    }
                    Color.clear.frame(height: 1).id("bottom")
                        .listRowSeparator(.hidden)
                } header: {
                    // Above the lines, not in a footer: the bottom of the list
                    // sits under the search field.
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                        HStack(spacing: 6) {
                            Circle().fill(live ? Color.green : Color.secondary).frame(width: 7, height: 7)
                            Text(live ? L10n.t(.liveLabel) : L10n.t(.pausedLabel))
                            Spacer()
                            Text(verbatim: "\(shownLines.count)")
                        }
                        Text(L10n.t(.runnerLogsCaption))
                            .font(.caption2)
                            .textCase(nil)
                        NoticeText()
                            .font(.caption)
                            .textCase(nil)
                    }
                }
            }
            .listStyle(.plain)
            .environment(\.defaultMinListRowHeight, 0)
            .searchable(text: $filter, prompt: L10n.t(.filterPlaceholder))
            .refreshable { await refresh() }
            // Follow the newest line while live; a paused log stays where the
            // reader left it.
            .onChange(of: admin.logLines) { _ in
                guard live, filter.isEmpty else { return }
                proxy.scrollTo("bottom", anchor: .bottom)
            }
            .onAppear {
                DispatchQueue.main.async { proxy.scrollTo("bottom", anchor: .bottom) }
            }
        }
    }

    private func refresh() async {
        refreshing = true
        await admin.loadLogs()
        refreshing = false
    }
}
```

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct SessionListView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var appState: AppState

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            HStack {
                Text("Connected Sessions")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .fontWeight(.semibold)
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                Spacer()
                Button("Revoke All") {
                    withAnimation { appState.revokeAllSessions() }
                }
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundColor(.red)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal)

            ForEach(appState.sessions) { session in
                SessionRow(session: session) {
                    withAnimation { appState.revokeSession(id: session.id) }
                }
            }
        }
        .padding(.top, 12)
        .onAppear {
            appState.refreshSessions()
        }
    }
}

struct SessionRow: View {
    let session: AuthSession
    let onRevoke: () -> Void

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Circle()
                .fill(.green)
                .frame(width: 8, height: 8)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                Text(session.clientName)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .fontWeight(.medium)
                Text(formatRelative(session.lastActiveAt))
                    .font(.caption2)
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
            }

            Spacer()

            Button {
                onRevoke()
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: "xmark.circle.fill")
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary.opacity(0.5))
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
        }
        .padding(.horizontal)
        .padding(.vertical, 8)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10))
        .padding(.horizontal)
    }

    private func formatRelative(_ date: Date) -> String {
        let interval = Date().timeIntervalSince(date)
        if interval < 60 { return "Active now" }
        if interval < 3600 { return "\(Int(interval / 60))m ago" }
        if interval < 86400 { return "\(Int(interval / 3600))h ago" }
        return "\(Int(interval / 86400))d ago"
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLApp/Views/SettingsView.swift`:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import UIKit

/// The app's home screen.
///
/// Note what this app is NOT: automation runs in the XCUITest runner, a separate
/// process. This app can't serve RPC itself, so it doesn't try — it reports
/// whether the runner is able to launch (the DDI check) and offers a button that
/// launches it via `ictrl://start`.
struct SettingsView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var appState: AppState

    /// Re-probed whenever the view appears rather than held in AppState: the DDI
    /// can be unmounted while the app sits in the background, so a value cached
    /// at launch goes stale silently.
    @State private var ddi = DeveloperDiskImage.status()
    @State private var launchFailed = false
    @State private var showMountSheet = false
    @StateObject private var runner = RunnerStatus(port: 8200)
    @EnvironmentObject private var runnerAdmin: RunnerAdmin
    @State private var logCount = AppLog.allFiles().count


    /// The runner registers this scheme; opening it starts the automation server.
    ///
    /// `callback` asks the runner to bounce back to us once it has decided
    /// whether the server came up, appending `status` and `address`. Without it
    /// the user is left in the runner — a blank XCTest app with nothing to show
    /// — wondering whether anything happened.
    private static let runnerURL = URL(string: "ictrl://start?callback=ictrl-app://started")!

    /// Stopping goes through the URL scheme too. The only other route is
    /// `config{stop_server:true}` over /rpc, which needs an encrypted envelope —
    /// and this app deliberately holds no pairing key.
    private static let runnerStopURL = URL(string: "ictrl://stop?callback=ictrl-app://stopped")!

    /// Provides the local loopback tunnel StikDebug needs to reach lockdownd.
    /// Deliberately an App Store link and not a deep link: neither LocalDevVPN
    /// nor its predecessor StosVPN registers a URL scheme, so any
    /// `localdevvpn://` we invented would fail silently. StosVPN has also been
    /// pulled from the App Store, which is why LocalDevVPN is the one named here.
    private static let localDevVPNURL = URL(string: "https://apps.apple.com/app/localdevvpn/id6755608044")!

    /// StikDebug mounts the DDI on-device. It registers both `stikdebug://` and
    /// the legacy `stikjit://`; bare scheme just opens the app.
    private static let stikDebugURL = URL(string: "stikdebug://")!
    /// Used when StikDebug isn't installed — it's sideload-only, never on the
    /// App Store, so the fallback is its distribution site.
    private static let stikDebugSiteURL = URL(string: "https://stikdebug.xyz")!

    var body: some View {
        List {
            requirementsSection

            // Fallback only. The in-app mount above does the same job without
            // leaving iCTRL; StikDebug stays listed because it is the
            // battle-tested implementation this port is based on, and is worth
            // trying if our mount fails on a device we haven't seen.
            if !ddi.isMounted {
                Section {
                    HelperRow(
                        index: 1,
                        title: "LocalDevVPN",
                        detail: "Required either way — it makes this device's debug service reachable.",
                        actionTitle: "App Store",
                        url: Self.localDevVPNURL
                    )
                    HelperRow(
                        index: 2,
                        title: "StikDebug",
                        detail: "An alternative mounter, if the in-app one fails. Sideload from stikdebug.xyz — it isn't on the App Store.",
                        actionTitle: "Open",
                        url: Self.stikDebugURL,
                        fallbackURL: Self.stikDebugSiteURL
                    )
                } header: {
                    Text(L10n.t(.alternativeSection))
                } footer: {
                    Text(L10n.t(.alternativeFooter))
                }
            }

            if launchFailed {
                Section {
                    Label {
                        Text("Couldn't open the runner. Install iCTRLUITests-Runner with SideStore (or your own signing), then try again.")
                            .font(.footnote)
                    } icon: {
                        Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
                            .foregroundColor(.orange)
                    }
                }
            }

            serverSection

            deviceSection

            Section {
                HStack {
                    Text(L10n.t(.versionLabel))
                    Spacer()
                    Text("1.0.0")
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }
                HStack {
                    Text(L10n.t(.protocolLabel))
                    Spacer()
                    Text("JSON-RPC 2.0")
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }
                NavigationLink {
                    LogListView()
                } label: {
                    HStack {
                        Text(L10n.t(.logsLabel))
                        Spacer()
                        Text(verbatim: "\(logCount)")
                            .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            } header: {
                Text(L10n.t(.aboutSection))
            } footer: {
                // The mount runs through a Rust FFI that aborts rather than
                // throws, so when it fails the log is often the only artifact
                // besides a crash report — and it can be shared from here.
                Text(L10n.t(.logsFooter))
            }
        }
        .listStyle(.insetGrouped)
        .navigationTitle("iCTRL")
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        .onAppear {
            ddi = DeveloperDiskImage.status()
            logCount = AppLog.allFiles().count
            runner.startPolling()
        }
        .onDisappear { runner.stopPolling() }
        .onOpenURL { url in
            // The runner bounced back: ictrl-app://started?status=…&address=…
            guard url.scheme == "ictrl-app" else { return }
            // ictrl-app://started or ictrl-app://stopped
            let items = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)?.queryItems ?? []
            let status = items.first { $0.name == "status" }?.value
            launchFailed = (status == "failed")
            // Trust the probe over the reported status — by the time we're back,
            // asking the server directly is both cheap and authoritative.
            Task { await runner.check() }
        }
        .sheet(isPresented: $showMountSheet, onDismiss: {
            // Re-probe: a successful mount changes what the status row should say.
            ddi = DeveloperDiskImage.status()
        }) {
            DDIMountView()
        }
    }

    /// What must be true before automation can run at all.
    ///
    /// The Developer Disk Image is the one hard prerequisite: without it the
    /// XCUITest runner dies in dyld before any of our code runs, so a missing
    /// DDI is not a degraded mode — it is the whole feature not working. This
    /// section states that, and offers the fix either way: mount it when it's
    /// absent, re-mount when it's there but the user has reason to redo it
    /// (a reboot drops it, and the status here can only report what it can see).
    private var requirementsSection: some View {
        Section {
            HStack {
                Text(L10n.t(.developerDiskImage))
                Spacer()
                HStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Circle()
                        .fill(ddi.isMounted ? .green : .orange)
                        .frame(width: 8, height: 8)
                    Text(ddi.summary)
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }
            }

            if let layout = ddi.layout {
                HStack {
                    Text(L10n.t(.mountPoint))
                    Spacer()
                    Text(layout.rawValue)
                        .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
                        .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                }
            }

            // Offered in both states. Mounted is not the same as "nothing left
            // to do": the image is dropped by a reboot, and a stale or partial
            // mount looks identical from here, so re-mounting has to stay one
            // tap away rather than something you can only reach by rebooting.
            Button {
                showMountSheet = true
            } label: {
                Label(ddi.isMounted ? L10n.t(.remount) : L10n.t(.mountWithoutMac),
                      systemImage: ddi.isMounted ? "arrow.clockwise" : "externaldrive.badge.plus")
            }
        } header: {
            Text(L10n.t(.runtimeRequirements))
        } footer: {
            if ddi.isMounted {
                Text(L10n.t(.ddiReadyFooter))
            } else {
                Text(ddi.advice ?? "The Developer Disk Image isn't mounted, so the automation "
                                 + "runner can't launch.")
            }
        }
    }

    /// This device, read locally.
    ///
    /// Deliberately not sourced from the server's device_info: these values are
    /// available whether or not the runner is up, and they're most useful
    /// precisely when it isn't — "which iOS is this?" is the first question
    /// asked when the runner won't start.
    private var deviceSection: some View {
        Section {
            LabeledRow(L10n.t(.modelLabel), DeviceInfo.modelIdentifier)
            LabeledRow(L10n.t(.systemLabel), "\(UIDevice.current.systemName) \(UIDevice.current.systemVersion)")
            LabeledRow(L10n.t(.screenLabel), DeviceInfo.screenDescription)
            LabeledRow(L10n.t(.nameLabel), UIDevice.current.name, monospaced: false)
        } header: {
            Text(L10n.t(.deviceSection))
        }
    }

    /// Live state of the automation server.
    ///
    /// The server runs inside the XCUITest runner, a separate process, so this
    /// reports what an HTTP probe of it says rather than anything this app
    /// knows locally — the runner can be started or killed without the app
    /// being involved at all.
    private var serverSection: some View {
        Section {
            HStack {
                Text(L10n.t(.statusLabel))
                Spacer()
                switch runner.state {
                case .unknown, .checking:
                    HStack(spacing: 6) {
                        ProgressView().controlSize(.small)
                        Text(L10n.t(.checking)).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                case .running:
                    HStack(spacing: 6) {
                        Circle().fill(.green).frame(width: 8, height: 8)
                        Text(L10n.t(.running)).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                case .stopped:
                    HStack(spacing: 6) {
                        Circle().fill(.secondary).frame(width: 8, height: 8)
                        Text(L10n.t(.stopped)).foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            }

            HStack {
                Text(L10n.t(.addressLabel))
                Spacer()
                Text(verbatim: "127.0.0.1:\(appState.serverPort)")
                    .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
            }

            if case .running(let info) = runner.state {
                if let version = info.serverVersion {
                    HStack {
                        Text(L10n.t(.serverLabel))
                        Spacer()
                        Text(verbatim: version)
                            .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
                            .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
                if let proto = info.protocolVersion {
                    HStack {
                        Text(L10n.t(.protocolLabel))
                        Spacer()
                        Text(verbatim: "v\(proto)")
                            .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
                            .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
                if let methods = info.methodCount {
                    HStack {
                        Text(L10n.t(.methodsLabel))
                        Spacer()
                        Text(verbatim: "\(methods)")
                            .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    }
                }
                if !info.capabilities.isEmpty {
                    NavigationLink {
                        CapabilityListView(capabilities: info.capabilities)
                    } label: {
                        HStack {
                            Text(L10n.t(.capabilitiesLabel))
                            Spacer()
                            Text(verbatim: "\(info.capabilities.count)")
                                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                        }
                    }
                }
                if let visibility = runnerAdmin.visibility {
                    RunnerVisibilityRow(visibility: visibility)
                }
                if runnerAdmin.localNetworkDenied {
                    // Remote clients connecting in still work without it, so
                    // this is the only sign of why nearby discovery cannot.
                    Text(L10n.t(.runnerLocalNetworkDenied))
                        .font(.footnote)
                        .foregroundColor(.orange)
                }
                NavigationLink {
                    RunnerClientsView()
                } label: {
                    HStack {
                        Text(L10n.t(.authorizedClients))
                        Spacer()
                        if runnerAdmin.clientsLoaded {
                            Text(verbatim: "\(runnerAdmin.clients.count)")
                                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                        }
                    }
                }
                // Count and visibility without opening the list, kept current
                // while this screen is shown (remote access and nearby can be
                // switched from the runner's notification at any time). Only
                // once paired: pairing itself is never started from here.
                .task(id: runnerAdmin.isPaired) {
                    while !Task.isCancelled && runnerAdmin.isPaired {
                        await runnerAdmin.loadClients()
                        try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 5_000_000_000)
                    }
                }
                NavigationLink {
                    RunnerLogsView()
                } label: {
                    Text(L10n.t(.runnerLogs))
                }
                Button(role: .destructive) {
                    stopRunner()
                } label: {
                    Label(L10n.t(.stopServerButton), systemImage: "stop.fill")
                }
            } else {
                // Start lives here rather than in the toolbar: it belongs beside
                // the state it changes, and this is where the reason it might be
                // disabled is already on screen.
                Button {
                    startRunner()
                } label: {
                    Label(L10n.t(.startServer), systemImage: "play.fill")
                }
                .disabled(!ddi.isMounted)
            }
        } header: {
            Text(L10n.t(.serverSectionTitle))
        } footer: {
            if case .running = runner.state {
                Text("\(L10n.t(.addressLabel)): \(appState.serverPort) · \(L10n.t(.serverRunningFooter))")
            } else if !ddi.isMounted {
                Text(L10n.t(.mountFirstFooter))
            } else {
                Text(L10n.t(.startOpensRunnerFooter))
            }
        }
    }

    private func stopRunner() {
        // Opening the runner's scheme brings it to the front, where it stops its
        // server and ends the test. It bounces back here afterwards, but the
        // probe is what settles the displayed state.
        UIApplication.shared.open(Self.runnerStopURL) { _ in
            Task {
                // Give the runner a moment to actually tear the listener down;
                // probing instantly would still see it up and flip back to
                // "Running" for one cycle.
                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 1_500_000_000)
                await runner.check()
            }
        }
    }

    private func startRunner() {
        launchFailed = false
        UIApplication.shared.open(Self.runnerURL) { ok in
            // The usual cause is the runner simply not being installed — the two
            // IPAs ship separately, so having this app is no guarantee.
            launchFailed = !ok
        }
    }
}

/// One numbered step in the "mount without a Mac" recovery flow.
private struct HelperRow: View {
    let index: Int
    let title: String
    let detail: String
    /// `nil` for a step the user performs here rather than in another app.
    let actionTitle: String?
    let url: URL?
    /// Opened when `url` uses a custom scheme and the app isn't installed.
    var fallbackURL: URL? = nil

    var body: some View {
        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
            Text(verbatim: "\(index)")
                .font(.caption.bold())
                .foregroundColor(.white)
                .frame(width: 20, height: 20)
                .background(Circle().fill(.tint))

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                Text(title).font(.body)
                Text(detail)
                    .font(.caption)
                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                    .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 8)

            if let actionTitle, let url {
                Button(actionTitle) { open(url) }
                    .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
                    // Rows sit in a List; .borderless keeps the tap on the button
                    // instead of letting the whole row swallow it.
                    .buttonStyle(.borderless)
            }
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 2)
    }

    private func open(_ url: URL) {
        UIApplication.shared.open(url) { ok in
            // A custom-scheme open fails when that app isn't installed; falling
            // back to its download page turns a dead tap into a way forward.
            guard !ok, let fallbackURL else { return }
            UIApplication.shared.open(fallbackURL)
        }
    }
}

/// The capability tags the running server advertises.
///
/// A flat list rather than a summary: these are what a client feature-detects
/// against, so the useful question is "is X there", which a searchable list
/// answers and a count does not.
private struct CapabilityListView: View {
    let capabilities: [String]

    var body: some View {
        List(capabilities.sorted(), id: \.self) { tag in
            HStack {
                Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill")
                    .foregroundColor(.green)
                    .font(.caption)
                Text(verbatim: tag)
                    .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
            }
        }
        .navigationTitle("Capabilities")
        .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
    }
}

/// A right-aligned value row, the shape the rest of this screen already uses.
private struct LabeledRow: View {
    let label: String
    let value: String
    var monospaced = true

    init(_ label: String, _ value: String, monospaced: Bool = true) {
        self.label = label
        self.value = value
        self.monospaced = monospaced
    }

    var body: some View {
        HStack {
            Text(label)
            Spacer()
            Text(verbatim: value)
                .font(monospaced ? .system(.body, design: .monospaced) : .body)
                .foregroundColor(.secondary)
                .lineLimit(1)
                .truncationMode(.middle)
        }
    }
}

/// Facts about this device that don't need the server running.
enum DeviceInfo {
    /// e.g. "iPhone17,2". `UIDevice.model` only ever says "iPhone", which
    /// doesn't distinguish the hardware people actually care about here.
    static var modelIdentifier: String {
        // On the simulator `utsname.machine` reports the *host* architecture
        // ("arm64"), not a device model — the real identifier is passed in the
        // environment instead. Without this the row reads "arm64", which is
        // both wrong and confusing next to a real device's "iPhone17,2".
        if let simulated = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["SIMULATOR_MODEL_IDENTIFIER"] {
            return simulated
        }
        var sysinfo = utsname()
        uname(&sysinfo)
        let raw = withUnsafeBytes(of: &sysinfo.machine) { buf in
            buf.prefix { $0 != 0 }.map { UInt8($0) }
        }
        let id = String(decoding: raw, as: UTF8.self)
        return id.isEmpty ? UIDevice.current.model : id
    }

    /// Points and pixels — the two coordinate spaces the automation API mixes,
    /// so seeing both here saves a round trip when a screenshot looks wrong.
    static var screenDescription: String {
        let b = UIScreen.main.bounds
        let s = UIScreen.main.scale
        return "\(Int(b.width))×\(Int(b.height)) pt · \(Int(b.width * s))×\(Int(b.height * s)) px"
    }
}
```

```swift
import SwiftUI

@main
struct iCTRLApp: App {
    @StateObject private var appState = AppState()
    @StateObject private var permission = NetworkPermission()
    /// Clients and log of the runner on this device; shared by Settings and Logs.
    @StateObject private var runnerAdmin = RunnerAdmin(port: 8200)
    @State private var showPermissionAlert = false
    /// Outcome of a pairing file shared to the app, shown as an alert.
    @State private var sharedPairing: SharedPairingResult?

    struct SharedPairingResult: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let fileName: String
        let error: String?
    }

    init() {
        // Touch the logger during init so every run produces a file, even one
        // that crashes before the user does anything.
        ictrlLog("App launched")
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            NavigationStack {
                SettingsView()
                    .environmentObject(appState)
            }
            .environmentObject(appState)
            .environmentObject(runnerAdmin)
            .sheet(item: $appState.pendingAuthRequest) { request in
                AuthRequestView(request: request)
                    .environmentObject(appState)
            }
            // A pairing file shared to iCTRL from another app (Files, Mail,
            // AirDrop, a chat): validate, store, and say so either way.
            .onOpenURL { url in
                guard url.isFileURL else { return }
                let name = url.lastPathComponent
                do {
                    try PairingFileStore.importShared(from: url)
                    ictrlLog("Pairing file received via share: \(name)")
                    sharedPairing = SharedPairingResult(fileName: name, error: nil)
                } catch {
                    ictrlLog("Shared file \(name) rejected: \(error.localizedDescription)")
                    sharedPairing = SharedPairingResult(fileName: name, error: error.localizedDescription)
                }
            }
            .alert(item: $sharedPairing) { result in
                if let error = result.error {
                    return Alert(title: Text(L10n.t(.pairingRejectedTitle)),
                                 message: Text("\(result.fileName)\n\n\(error)"),
                                 dismissButton: .default(Text(L10n.t(.doneButton))))
                }
                return Alert(title: Text(L10n.t(.pairingReceivedTitle)),
                             message: Text(String(format: L10n.t(.pairingReceivedBody), result.fileName)),
                             dismissButton: .default(Text(L10n.t(.doneButton))))
            }
            // On a fresh install this raises the system prompts; afterwards it
            // only reads them back, and a denial is said once per launch.
            .task { permission.probe() }
            .onReceive(permission.$networkData.combineLatest(permission.$localNetwork)) { _ in
                if !permission.denied.isEmpty { showPermissionAlert = true }
            }
            .alert(L10n.t(.networkPermissionTitle), isPresented: $showPermissionAlert) {
                Button(L10n.t(.openSettings)) {
                    UIApplication.shared.open(URL(string: UIApplication.openSettingsURLString)!)
                }
                Button(L10n.t(.laterButton), role: .cancel) {}
            } message: {
                Text(String(format: L10n.t(.networkPermissionBody), permission.denied.joined(separator: ", ")))
            }
        }
    }
}
```
