`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLKit/NearbyService.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Network
import dnssd

/// What a nearby (peer-to-peer Wi-Fi) client sees of this device: a stable
/// random identifier and a display name.
///
/// The identifier is generated once and kept in the app's sandbox next to the
/// pairing keys, so clients can recognise the same device although its AWDL
/// address changes. It is random — not derived from any hardware identifier.
///
/// iOS does not give apps the user-assigned device name, so the default name is
/// the hardware model plus the first four characters of the identifier; a
/// paired client can replace it (`config{device_name}`).
enum NearbyIdentity {
    private struct Stored: Codable {
        var id: String
        var name: String?
    }

    private static let lock = NSLock()
    private static var cached: Stored?

    private static var fileURL: URL? {
        let fm = FileManager.default
        guard let base = fm.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first else { return nil }
        let dir = base.appendingPathComponent("iCTRL", isDirectory: true)
        try? fm.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        return dir.appendingPathComponent("nearby_identity.json")
    }

    private static func load() -> Stored {
        lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
        if let cached { return cached }
        if let url = fileURL, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
           let stored = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Stored.self, from: data), stored.id.count == 32 {
            cached = stored
            return stored
        }
        var bytes = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: 16)
        _ = SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, bytes.count, &bytes)
        let fresh = Stored(id: bytes.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined(), name: nil)
        save(fresh)
        cached = fresh
        return fresh
    }

    private static func save(_ stored: Stored) {
        guard let url = fileURL, let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(stored) else { return }
        try? data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)
    }

    /// 32 lowercase hex characters, stable for this installation.
    static var deviceID: String { load().id }

    /// The name advertised to nearby clients.
    static var name: String { load().name ?? defaultName }

    /// Whether `name` was set by a client rather than generated.
    static var hasCustomName: Bool { load().name != nil }

    static var defaultName: String { "\(modelName) (\(deviceID.prefix(4)))" }

    /// Longest name accepted: a DNS-SD instance name is one DNS label (63 bytes).
    static let maxNameBytes = 63

    /// Set a custom name; nil or blank restores the default. Returns the name in
    /// effect, or nil when the new name is too long.
    @discardableResult
    static func setName(_ newName: String?) -> String? {
        let trimmed = newName?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
        guard trimmed.utf8.count <= maxNameBytes else { return nil }
        var stored = load()
        stored.name = trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
        lock.lock()
        cached = stored
        lock.unlock()
        save(stored)
        return stored.name ?? defaultName
    }

    /// Marketing name of the hardware, e.g. "iPhone 11"; the generic family
    /// name for identifiers this table does not know yet.
    static var modelName: String {
        var size = 0
        sysctlbyname("hw.machine", nil, &size, nil, 0)
        var raw = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: max(size, 1))
        sysctlbyname("hw.machine", &raw, &size, nil, 0)
        let machine = String(cString: raw)
        if let known = models[machine] { return known }
        if machine.hasPrefix("iPad") { return "iPad" }
        if machine.hasPrefix("iPod") { return "iPod touch" }
        return "iPhone"
    }

    private static let models: [String: String] = [
        "iPhone11,2": "iPhone XS", "iPhone11,4": "iPhone XS Max", "iPhone11,6": "iPhone XS Max",
        "iPhone11,8": "iPhone XR",
        "iPhone12,1": "iPhone 11", "iPhone12,3": "iPhone 11 Pro", "iPhone12,5": "iPhone 11 Pro Max",
        "iPhone12,8": "iPhone SE",
        "iPhone13,1": "iPhone 12 mini", "iPhone13,2": "iPhone 12", "iPhone13,3": "iPhone 12 Pro",
        "iPhone13,4": "iPhone 12 Pro Max",
        "iPhone14,4": "iPhone 13 mini", "iPhone14,5": "iPhone 13", "iPhone14,2": "iPhone 13 Pro",
        "iPhone14,3": "iPhone 13 Pro Max", "iPhone14,6": "iPhone SE",
        "iPhone14,7": "iPhone 14", "iPhone14,8": "iPhone 14 Plus",
        "iPhone15,2": "iPhone 14 Pro", "iPhone15,3": "iPhone 14 Pro Max",
        "iPhone15,4": "iPhone 15", "iPhone15,5": "iPhone 15 Plus",
        "iPhone16,1": "iPhone 15 Pro", "iPhone16,2": "iPhone 15 Pro Max",
        "iPhone17,3": "iPhone 16", "iPhone17,4": "iPhone 16 Plus",
        "iPhone17,1": "iPhone 16 Pro", "iPhone17,2": "iPhone 16 Pro Max", "iPhone17,5": "iPhone 16e",
        "iPhone18,3": "iPhone 17", "iPhone18,1": "iPhone 17 Pro", "iPhone18,2": "iPhone 17 Pro Max",
        "iPhone18,4": "iPhone Air",
    ]
}

/// Advertises the device over Bonjour while nearby discovery is on: the
/// peer-to-peer listener on the AWDL interface, and the main listener on the
/// LAN (see `registerLAN`), so a first connection needs no typed address.
/// With nearby discovery off nothing is advertised anywhere.
///
/// The AWDL record is registered with the *specific* interface index of
/// `awdl0`, and must stay so: interface 0 or `kDNSServiceInterfaceIndexP2P`
/// with the AWDL flag would also put the peer-to-peer port on Wi-Fi/Ethernet
/// (dns_sd.h maps P2P on Register to "any interface, including P2P"), where
/// that listener refuses every connection anyway.
///
/// `awdl0` can exist while it is unusable (Wi-Fi off): a registration made
/// then never completes and never fails. So the interface's own state decides
/// whether to register, and it is re-checked every few seconds while enabled;
/// registration follows it both ways without the user doing anything.
final class NearbyAdvertiser {
    /// Why the device is or is not discoverable right now.
    enum Status: String {
        case off
        /// Registration sent, not yet confirmed.
        case starting
        case advertising
        /// No usable peer-to-peer interface: Wi-Fi is off (or the hardware has none).
        case needsWiFi = "needs_wifi"
        /// Refused by the system: Local Network access or the Bonjour declaration.
        case denied
        /// Any other registration error; retried periodically.
        case failed
    }

    /// The peer-to-peer interface as the system reports it.
    struct LinkState {
        var index: UInt32 = 0
        var up = false
        var running = false
        var linkLocal = false

        /// Whether a registration on it can complete.
        var usable: Bool { index != 0 && up && running }

        var json: JSONValue {
            .object(["index": .int(Int(index)), "up": .bool(up), "running": .bool(running),
                     "link_local": .bool(linkLocal)])
        }
    }

    private let port: UInt16
    /// The main (LAN) listener's port, advertised on the LAN while nearby
    /// discovery is on so a first connection needs no typed address.
    private let lanPort: UInt16
    private let queue: DispatchQueue
    private let log: (String) -> Void
    private var ref: DNSServiceRef?
    /// The awdl0 index `ref` was registered on. If the interface is rebuilt
    /// under a new index the old registration is silently dead.
    private var registeredIndex: UInt32 = 0
    private var lanRef: DNSServiceRef?
    private var lanRetryAt = Date.distantPast
    private var poll: DispatchSourceTimer?
    private var nextRetry = Date.distantPast
    private var stopped = true

    /// Called on `queue` whenever `status` changes.
    var onChange: ((Status) -> Void)?
    private(set) var status: Status = .off {
        didSet { if status != oldValue { onChange?(status) } }
    }
    var isAdvertising: Bool { status == .advertising }

    static let serviceType = "_ictrl._tcp"
    static let interfaceName = "awdl0"
    /// How often the interface is re-checked while enabled (a getifaddrs call).
    private static let pollInterval: TimeInterval = 5
    /// Back-off after a registration error before trying again.
    private static let retryInterval: TimeInterval = 30

    init(port: UInt16, lanPort: UInt16, queue: DispatchQueue, log: @escaping (String) -> Void) {
        self.port = port
        self.lanPort = lanPort
        self.queue = queue
        self.log = log
    }

    deinit {
        poll?.cancel()
        if let ref { DNSServiceRefDeallocate(ref) }
        if let lanRef { DNSServiceRefDeallocate(lanRef) }
    }

    func start() {
        queue.async {
            guard self.stopped else { return }
            self.stopped = false
            self.nextRetry = .distantPast
            self.lanRetryAt = .distantPast
            self.startPolling()
            self.evaluate()
        }
    }

    func stop() {
        queue.async {
            self.stopped = true
            self.poll?.cancel()
            self.poll = nil
            self.deregister()
            self.deregisterLAN()
            self.status = .off
        }
    }

    /// Re-register under the current `NearbyIdentity.name`.
    func refreshName() {
        queue.async {
            guard !self.stopped else { return }
            self.deregisterLAN()
            self.registerLAN()
            guard self.ref != nil else { return }
            self.deregister()
            let link = Self.linkState()
            if link.usable { self.register(index: link.index) } else { self.evaluate() }
        }
    }

    /// Check now instead of at the next poll (e.g. after a network change).
    func recheck() {
        queue.async { self.evaluate() }
    }

    /// Retry a refused registration now rather than after the back-off — for
    /// when the cause may just have been fixed (the permission prompt shown).
    func retryNow() {
        queue.async {
            self.nextRetry = .distantPast
            self.evaluate()
        }
    }

    /// Current state of `awdl0`.
    static func linkState() -> LinkState {
        var state = LinkState()
        state.index = if_nametoindex(interfaceName)
        guard state.index != 0 else { return state }
        var ifaddr: UnsafeMutablePointer<ifaddrs>?
        guard getifaddrs(&ifaddr) == 0, let first = ifaddr else { return state }
        defer { freeifaddrs(ifaddr) }
        for ptr in sequence(first: first, next: { $0.pointee.ifa_next }) {
            let entry = ptr.pointee
            guard String(cString: entry.ifa_name) == interfaceName else { continue }
            state.up = state.up || entry.ifa_flags & UInt32(IFF_UP) != 0
            state.running = state.running || entry.ifa_flags & UInt32(IFF_RUNNING) != 0
            if let addr = entry.ifa_addr, addr.pointee.sa_family == UInt8(AF_INET6) {
                state.linkLocal = true
            }
        }
        return state
    }

    // MARK: - On `queue`

    private func startPolling() {
        guard poll == nil else { return }
        let timer = DispatchSource.makeTimerSource(queue: queue)
        timer.schedule(deadline: .now() + Self.pollInterval, repeating: Self.pollInterval)
        timer.setEventHandler { [weak self] in self?.evaluate() }
        poll = timer
        timer.resume()
    }

    /// Bring the registration in line with the interface.
    private func evaluate() {
        guard !stopped else { return }
        if lanRef == nil, Date() >= lanRetryAt { registerLAN() }
        let link = Self.linkState()
        guard link.usable else {
            if status != .needsWiFi {
                log("📡 Nearby: \(Self.interfaceName) is not usable (index \(link.index), up \(link.up), running \(link.running)) — Wi-Fi off? Waiting for it")
            }
            deregister()
            status = .needsWiFi
            return
        }
        if ref != nil, link.index != registeredIndex {
            log("📡 Nearby: \(Self.interfaceName) is now index \(link.index) (was \(registeredIndex)) — registering again")
            deregister()
            register(index: link.index)
            return
        }
        switch status {
        case .advertising, .starting:
            return
        case .denied, .failed:
            guard Date() >= nextRetry else { return }
        case .off, .needsWiFi:
            break
        }
        register(index: link.index)
    }

    private func register(index: UInt32) {
        guard ref == nil else { return }
        var txt = TXTRecordRef()
        TXTRecordCreate(&txt, 0, nil)
        defer { TXTRecordDeallocate(&txt) }
        setTXT(&txt, "v", String(RPCMethodRegistry.protocolVersion))
        setTXT(&txt, "id", NearbyIdentity.deviceID)
        setTXT(&txt, "ch", "awdl")

        let name = NearbyIdentity.name
        var newRef: DNSServiceRef?
        // Unretained: the ref is always deallocated (on `queue`, or in deinit)
        // before this object goes away, and no callback is delivered after that.
        let context = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self).toOpaque()
        let err = DNSServiceRegister(
            &newRef, DNSServiceFlags(kDNSServiceFlagsIncludeAWDL), index,
            name, Self.serviceType, nil, nil, port.bigEndian,
            TXTRecordGetLength(&txt), TXTRecordGetBytesPtr(&txt),
            { _, _, errorCode, registeredName, _, _, context in
                guard let context else { return }
                let me = Unmanaged<NearbyAdvertiser>.fromOpaque(context).takeUnretainedValue()
                me.registrationCallback(errorCode, registeredName.map { String(cString: $0) })
            }, context)
        guard err == kDNSServiceErr_NoError, let newRef else {
            fail(err, "DNSServiceRegister failed")
            return
        }
        guard DNSServiceSetDispatchQueue(newRef, queue) == kDNSServiceErr_NoError else {
            DNSServiceRefDeallocate(newRef)
            fail(DNSServiceErrorType(kDNSServiceErr_Unknown), "could not attach to the dispatch queue")
            return
        }
        ref = newRef
        registeredIndex = index
        status = .starting
        log("📡 Nearby: registering \"\(name)\" on \(Self.interfaceName) (index \(index)), port \(port)")
    }

    private func registrationCallback(_ err: DNSServiceErrorType, _ registeredName: String?) {
        guard !stopped, ref != nil else { return }
        if err == kDNSServiceErr_NoError {
            log("📡 Nearby: advertised as \"\(registeredName ?? "?")\" on \(Self.interfaceName) only")
            status = .advertising
        } else {
            deregister()
            fail(err, "registration failed")
        }
    }

    private func fail(_ err: DNSServiceErrorType, _ what: String) {
        let denied = Int(err) == Int(kDNSServiceErr_NoAuth) || Int(err) == Int(kDNSServiceErr_PolicyDenied)
        log("📡 Nearby: \(what) (\(err))"
            + (denied ? " — Local Network access denied, or the service type is missing from NSBonjourServices" : "")
            + "; retrying in \(Int(Self.retryInterval))s")
        nextRetry = Date().addingTimeInterval(Self.retryInterval)
        status = denied ? .denied : .failed
    }

    // MARK: LAN

    /// Advertise the main listener on the ordinary (non peer-to-peer)
    /// interfaces: interface 0 without the AWDL/P2P flags, i.e. Wi-Fi and
    /// wired, never AWDL. Same name and device id as the AWDL record, port of
    /// the main listener, TXT ch=lan. Status reflects AWDL only; a LAN
    /// failure is logged and retried after the back-off.
    private func registerLAN() {
        guard !stopped, lanRef == nil else { return }
        var txt = TXTRecordRef()
        TXTRecordCreate(&txt, 0, nil)
        defer { TXTRecordDeallocate(&txt) }
        setTXT(&txt, "v", String(RPCMethodRegistry.protocolVersion))
        setTXT(&txt, "id", NearbyIdentity.deviceID)
        setTXT(&txt, "ch", "lan")

        var newRef: DNSServiceRef?
        let context = Unmanaged.passUnretained(self).toOpaque()
        let err = DNSServiceRegister(
            &newRef, 0, 0, NearbyIdentity.name, Self.serviceType, nil, nil, lanPort.bigEndian,
            TXTRecordGetLength(&txt), TXTRecordGetBytesPtr(&txt),
            { _, _, errorCode, registeredName, _, _, context in
                guard let context else { return }
                let me = Unmanaged<NearbyAdvertiser>.fromOpaque(context).takeUnretainedValue()
                me.lanRegistrationCallback(errorCode, registeredName.map { String(cString: $0) })
            }, context)
        guard err == kDNSServiceErr_NoError, let newRef,
              DNSServiceSetDispatchQueue(newRef, queue) == kDNSServiceErr_NoError else {
            if let newRef { DNSServiceRefDeallocate(newRef) }
            log("📡 Nearby: LAN registration failed (\(err)); retrying in \(Int(Self.retryInterval))s")
            lanRetryAt = Date().addingTimeInterval(Self.retryInterval)
            return
        }
        lanRef = newRef
    }

    private func lanRegistrationCallback(_ err: DNSServiceErrorType, _ registeredName: String?) {
        guard !stopped, lanRef != nil else { return }
        if err == kDNSServiceErr_NoError {
            log("📡 Nearby: also discoverable on the LAN as \"\(registeredName ?? "?")\", port \(lanPort)")
        } else {
            deregisterLAN()
            log("📡 Nearby: LAN registration failed (\(err)); retrying in \(Int(Self.retryInterval))s")
            lanRetryAt = Date().addingTimeInterval(Self.retryInterval)
        }
    }

    private func deregisterLAN() {
        if let lanRef { DNSServiceRefDeallocate(lanRef) }
        lanRef = nil
    }

    /// Drop the registration; callers set the resulting `status`.
    private func deregister() {
        if let ref { DNSServiceRefDeallocate(ref) }
        ref = nil
    }

    private func setTXT(_ txt: inout TXTRecordRef, _ key: String, _ value: String) {
        let bytes = Array(value.utf8.prefix(255))
        TXTRecordSetValue(&txt, key, UInt8(bytes.count), bytes)
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLKit/NetworkTypeMonitor.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import Network

/// Classifies the current default network path so callers can behave differently
/// on Wi-Fi vs cellular. On cellular the device's routable address is a
/// public/CGNAT address that is NOT reachable from outside and has no concept of
/// "Local Network" — so remote-access self-checks and the Local Network
/// permission prompt should be skipped there (they'd fail / be meaningless).
final class NetworkTypeMonitor {
    enum NetworkType: String {
        case wifi        // en0 / Wi-Fi — LAN reachable, Local Network applies
        case cellular    // pdp_ip / WWAN — public/CGNAT, not LAN-reachable
        case wired       // ethernet / USB
        case other       // loopback-only, VPN, or not yet determined
    }

    static let shared = NetworkTypeMonitor()

    private let monitor = NWPathMonitor()
    private let queue = DispatchQueue(label: "com.copyapp.ictrl.netmonitor")
    private let lock = NSLock()
    private var cached: NetworkType = .other
    /// Set once the first path update lands. Until then `current` is a default,
    /// not an observation — the distinction matters to anything gating UI on it.
    private var hasResolved = false
    private var observers: [(NetworkType) -> Void] = []

    private init() {
        monitor.pathUpdateHandler = { [weak self] path in
            self?.update(from: path)
        }
        monitor.start(queue: queue)
    }

    private func update(from path: NWPath) {
        let type: NetworkType
        if path.usesInterfaceType(.wifi) {
            type = .wifi
        } else if path.usesInterfaceType(.cellular) {
            type = .cellular
        } else if path.usesInterfaceType(.wiredEthernet) {
            type = .wired
        } else {
            type = .other
        }
        lock.lock()
        cached = type
        hasResolved = true
        let toNotify = observers
        lock.unlock()
        for notify in toNotify { notify(type) }
    }

    /// True once a real path update has been seen. `current` before this is the
    /// initial default and should not be treated as an answer.
    var isResolved: Bool {
        lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
        return hasResolved
    }

    /// Observe changes. Fires immediately if a path has already been resolved, so
    /// a late subscriber isn't left waiting for the next change that may never
    /// come on a stable connection.
    func observe(_ handler: @escaping (NetworkType) -> Void) {
        lock.lock()
        observers.append(handler)
        let resolved = hasResolved
        let type = cached
        lock.unlock()
        if resolved { handler(type) }
    }

    /// Current network type. Reflects the most recent path update; the monitor is
    /// started at init so this is populated within a moment of launch.
    var current: NetworkType {
        lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
        return cached
    }

    /// True when the LAN is meaningful here (Wi-Fi or wired) — i.e. remote access
    /// self-checks and the Local Network permission make sense.
    var isLANReachable: Bool {
        switch current {
        case .wifi, .wired: return true
        case .cellular, .other: return false
        }
    }
}
```

```swift
    static func generateJSONSchema() -> [[String: Any]] {
        methods.map { m in
            var dict: [String: Any] = [
                "name": m.name,
                "description": m.description,
                "returns": m.returns,
            ]
            dict["params"] = m.params.map { p in
                [
                    "name": p.name,
                    "type": p.type,
                    "required": p.required,
                    "description": p.description,
                ] as [String: Any]
            }
            return dict
        }
    }

    /// A self-describing document for models: top-level guidance + methods.
    /// Returned from GET /schema and GET / (Accept: application/json).
    /// Semantic server version — bump on every functional change. 1.2.0 is the
    /// release that added the encrypted auth channel plus the docs/Skill,
    /// clear-text, page-source, and reliability improvements. Single source of
    /// truth for /schema AND device_info.
    static let serverVersion = "1.98.12"

    /// When this binary was built, as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM".
    ///
    /// `serverVersion` alone cannot tell two builds apart — bumping it is a
    /// manual step and gets forgotten, so a freshly installed runner can report
    /// the same version as the one it replaced. That ambiguity has already cost
    /// real debugging time: a change looked "not deployed" when the actual
    /// question was which binary was loaded. This is stamped by
    /// Scripts/stamp-build.sh on every build, so it always differs.
    static let buildTimestamp = BuildStamp.value

    /// Server capability/protocol version. v1 = encrypted-envelope auth over /pair +
    /// /rpc. Bump when the wire capabilities change so clients can auto-detect.
    static let protocolVersion = 1

    /// Capability tags a client can feature-detect against, from ONE device_info
    /// call (no separate /schema fetch needed). Keep in sync with what the server
    /// actually implements.
    static let capabilityTags: [String] = [
        "envelope_v1",         // /pair + encrypted /rpc envelopes (HMAC-SHA256)
        "stream_ticket",       // stream_ticket RPC → single-use ?ticket= for /stream + /logs
        "video_stream",        // GET /stream (H.264-in-MPEG-TS live screen)
        "remote_ui",           // GET /remote (browser control page)
        "page_source_filter",  // page_source{filter:{...}}
        "visible_only",        // page_source{visible_only:true} — viewport culling for long lists
        "max_depth",           // page_source{max_depth}
        "find_element_ref",    // find_element → ref; tap{ref}
        "scroll_to_element",   // scroll_to_element → ref
        "clear_text",          // clear_text + type{clear:true}
        "open_url",            // open_url deep links
        "resolve_app",         // resolve_app name → bundle_id
        "page",                // page{direction} precise paging
        "collect",             // collect{pages}: page + read N screens in one call
        "stop_server",         // config{stop_server:true}
        "logs_history",        // GET /logs/history (persisted logs)
        "screenshot_jpeg",     // screenshot{format:'jpeg'|'png', quality} — jpeg is the default
        "reset",               // reset RPC (recover from a dropped accessibility connection)
        "nonui_lane",          // config/reset/logs answer while UI calls are blocked
        "system_metrics",      // device_info.system — thermal/cpu/memory/disk/battery/screen_locked/foreground_app
        "screen_text",         // Vision OCR fallback when the AX tree has no on-screen rows
        "cli_binary",          // GET /skill/clients/cli — static aarch64-musl client
        "nearby_discovery",    // Bonjour over peer-to-peer Wi-Fi (AWDL) on port+1, when turned on
    ]

                "pair": "POST /pair  {client_name, plain:true | pub:<b64 raw 32B X25519>} → the 32-byte key K. A byte pipe can't carry a per-request envelope, so it takes a SINGLE-USE ~60s ticket minted over the encrypted channel by the `stream_ticket` RPC.                 "whoami": "GET /whoami   unauthenticated {device_id, name, protocol_version, server_version}. device_id is stable per installation: store one key per device under it and use that key over every channel (USB, LAN, nearby). Every response also carries it as the X-ICTRL-Device header",

                "schema": "GET /schema  this document",

            "guidance": [
                "authorization":
                    "EVERY /rpc body is an encrypted envelope (protocol v1) — there is no plaintext/Bearer path; " +
                    "an unsealed POST gets 401 auth_required. All request-path crypto is HMAC-SHA256 only. " +
                    "STEP 1, pair once: POST /pair {client_name, plain:true} (127.0.0.1 only) or {client_name, pub} " +
                    "over the LAN, to obtain the 32-byte key K. This BLOCKS on an on-screen Allow/Deny prompt — " +
                    "use a timeout of AT LEAST 60s and do NOT retry early (each retry pops another prompt); 403 = denied. " +

                    "K_enc_req = HMAC(K, \"ictrl-v1|enc-req\"||nonce); K_mac = HMAC(K, \"ictrl-v1|mac\"||nonce); " +
                    "keystream(Kx) = HMAC(Kx, nonce||be32(0)) || HMAC(Kx, nonce||be32(1)) || … truncated; " +
                    "ct = body XOR keystream(K_enc_req); tag = HMAC(K_mac, \"v1\"||tok_4B||be64(ts)||nonce||ct). " +
                    "POST {v:1, tok, ts, nonce:<hex>, ct:<base64>, tag:<hex>}. " +
                    "STEP 3, open the reply: it is sealed under the SAME nonce — verify " +
                    "tag == HMAC(K_mac, \"resp\"||nonce||ct), then decrypt with K_enc_resp = HMAC(K, \"ictrl-v1|enc-resp\"||nonce). " +
                    "Expiry is IDLE-BASED: a key dies only after 30 days of no use, and every call slides that forward, " +
                    "so a key in regular use never expires and survives app restarts. Cache K and re-pair ONLY on " +
                    "401 auth_failed. Nonces must never repeat (replay is rejected within the ±120s window). "
                    + "Keys are PER DEVICE: cache them keyed by host:port so you can drive several devices "
                    + "concurrently, and never send one device's key to another.",
                "client_timeouts":
                    "Set generous client timeouts for /rpc: at least 30s, ideally 60-120s. " +
                    "/schema and /logs are static and reply instantly, but /rpc drives the real device — a cold app " +
                    "launch or heavy page can make a single call take many seconds. " +
                    "CRITICAL: a client-side curl timeout does NOT mean the action failed — the device keeps executing " +
                    "and the call usually completes. Before retrying a timed-out /rpc, GET /logs and look for a " +
                    "'⏱ ✓ <method>' entry — if it's there, the action already succeeded and retrying would DOUBLE it " +
                    "(e.g. a tap fires twice). Only retry if /logs shows no success and no in-flight entry.",
                "connection_reliability":
                    "The service runs inside an XCUITest process on the phone and can occasionally drop (iOS backgrounding " +
                    "limits, or a stuck long-running call). Treat 8200 as possibly-transient: " +
                    "(1) Before a session, probe with a SHORT timeout: GET /schema (1-2s) — 200 means ready. " +

    static func generateHTMLDoc() -> String {
        var html = """
        <!DOCTYPE html>
        <html><head>
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
        <title>iCTRL API</title>
        <style>
        * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }
        body { font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; background: #f5f5f7; color: #1d1d1f; padding: 20px; }
        h1 { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 8px; }
        .subtitle { color: #86868b; margin-bottom: 24px; }
        .endpoint { background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
        .endpoint-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 8px; }
        .method-name { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600; font-family: SF Mono, monospace; color: #0071e3; }
        .desc { color: #6e6e73; font-size: 14px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
        .params { font-size: 13px; }
        .param { display: flex; gap: 8px; padding: 4px 0; border-top: 1px solid #f5f5f7; }
        .param-name { font-family: SF Mono, monospace; font-weight: 500; min-width: 100px; }
        .param-type { color: #86868b; min-width: 60px; }
        .param-req { color: #bf4040; font-size: 11px; }
        .section { margin-top: 24px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; }
        .info { background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
        code { background: #f5f5f7; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 13px; }
        pre { background: #1d1d1f; color: #f5f5f7; padding: 12px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 13px; overflow-x: auto; margin-top: 8px; }
        </style>
        </head><body>
        <h1>iCTRL API</h1>
        <p class="subtitle">JSON-RPC 2.0 &middot; iOS Automation Server</p>

        <div class="info">
        <p><strong>RPC Endpoint:</strong> <code>POST /rpc</code></p>
        <p style="margin-top:4px"><strong>Pairing:</strong> <code>POST /pair</code> — <code>{client_name, plain:true|pub}</code> → 32-byte key <code>K</code>. Every <code>/rpc</code> body is then an encrypted v1 envelope.</p>
        <p style="margin-top:8px">All <code>/rpc</code> calls are encrypted v1 envelopes — no headers, no plaintext. Pair once, then seal every body with the key.</p>
        <pre>{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "tap", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 200}, "id": 1}</pre>
        </div>

        <div class="info" style="border-left:4px solid #ff9500">
        <p><strong>⏳ First, get a token — the user must approve it.</strong></p>
        <p style="margin-top:6px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        <code>POST /pair {client_name}</code> shows an <em>Allow / Deny</em> prompt on the device and BLOCKS until the user responds.
        Use a client timeout of <strong>at least 60 seconds</strong> and wait — do not retry early (each retry pops another prompt).
        On approval you receive a token (valid 30 days); on denial, HTTP 403.
        </p>
        </div>

        <div class="info" style="border-left:4px solid #5856d6">
        <p><strong>🔎 Version &amp; capabilities.</strong></p>
        <p style="margin-top:6px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        <code>device_info</code> (and <code>/schema</code>) report <code>server_version</code>, <code>protocol_version</code>
        and a <code>capabilities</code> array — feature-detect from ONE call and don't assume a method exists on an older
        <code>server_version</code>.
        </p>
        </div>

        <div class="info" style="border-left:4px solid #ff3b30">
        <p><strong>⚠️ Reliability &amp; timeouts — read before automating.</strong></p>
        <ul style="margin:6px 0 0 18px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px;line-height:1.6">
        <li><strong>Use long <code>/rpc</code> timeouts (≥30s, ideally 60–120s).</strong> <code>/schema</code> and <code>/logs</code> reply instantly, but <code>/rpc</code> drives the real device and a call can take seconds.</li>
        <li><strong>A client timeout ≠ failure.</strong> The device keeps executing. Before retrying, <code>GET /logs</code> and look for <code>⏱ ✓ &lt;method&gt;</code> — if present, it already succeeded and retrying would double the action.</li>
        <li><strong>Probe readiness with <code>GET /schema</code> (short timeout).</strong> If you woke the service via the <code>ictrl://</code> URL scheme, the <code>opened</code> flag is NOT proof the server is up — the runner cold-starts and needs a few seconds to bind :8200. Poll <code>/schema</code> until it returns 200.</li>
        <li><strong>If <code>/rpc</code> and <code>/logs</code> both go unreachable</strong>, the runner process died — re-wake via <code>ictrl://</code> and poll <code>/schema</code> until ready. Your cached key survives; only re-pair on a 401.</li>
        </ul>
        </div>

        <div class="info" style="border-left:4px solid #34c759">
        <p><strong>👁 Inspect the UI with <code>page_source</code> first.</strong></p>
        <p style="margin-top:6px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        <code>page_source</code> returns the view hierarchy as text (types, labels, identifiers, and frames
        already in <em>points</em>) — smaller, faster and more precise than an image. Use <code>screenshot</code>
        only when an element is missing from the tree or you need visual detail (and you can shrink it with <code>scale</code>).
        </p>
        <p style="margin-top:8px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        Rich pages can be big and the first call after a launch can be slow. <strong>Scope it:</strong>
        <code>page_source({"filter":{"label":"&lt;substring&gt;"}})</code> returns only matching nodes + ancestors;
        <code>{"max_depth":3}</code> gives just the top structure; <code>{"max_elements":200}</code> caps the count.
        A 500-node hard cap applies by default (<code>truncated:true</code> when hit).
        </p>
        </div>

        <div class="info" style="border-left:4px solid #0071e3">
        <p><strong>⚠️ Coordinates use POINTS, not pixels.</strong></p>
        <p style="margin-top:6px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        Screenshots come back in <em>pixels</em>; <code>tap</code>/<code>swipe</code>/<code>drag</code> take <em>points</em>.
        Convert: <code>point = pixel / scale</code>, taking <code>scale</code> from the
        <em>screenshot response</em> — not <code>device_info.screen_scale</code>, which is the
        panel ratio (3) while a screenshot is downscaled to 2 by default.
        The valid tap range (<code>point_width</code> × <code>point_height</code>) comes from either.
        </p>
        <p style="margin-top:6px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">
        Recommended flow: <code>device_info</code> → <code>resolve_app</code>/<code>launch_app</code> → <code>page_source</code> → tap frame center → verify.
        Fetch <code>GET /schema</code> for full machine-readable guidance (app binding, searching/typing, reliability…).
        </p>
        </div>

        <div class="info">
        <p><strong>Diagnostics &amp; logs (single-use <code>?ticket=</code> required, redacted):</strong></p>
        <ul style="margin:6px 0 0 18px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px;line-height:1.6">
        <li><code>GET /logs</code> — recent in-memory logs for the current process (includes <code>⏱ ✓ &lt;method&gt; &lt;ms&gt;</code> timings).</li>
        <li><code>GET /logs/files</code> — list persisted daily log files (survive crashes/restarts).</li>
        <li><code>GET /logs/history?date=YYYY-MM-DD</code> — read a persisted day's log. Use this to recover logs from BEFORE a crash.</li>
        <li><code>GET /schema</code> — this document, as JSON.</li>
        </ul>
        <p style="margin-top:8px;color:#6e6e73;font-size:14px">Stop the service remotely with <code>config {"stop_server": true}</code> — tokens persist, so relaunching the runner needs no re-auth.</p>
        </div>

        <p class="section">Methods (\(methods.count))</p>
        """

        for m in methods {
            html += """
            <div class="endpoint">
            <div class="endpoint-header"><span class="method-name">\(m.name)</span></div>
            <p class="desc">\(m.description)</p>
            """
            if !m.params.isEmpty {
                html += "<div class=\"params\">"
                for p in m.params {
                    let req = p.required ? "<span class=\"param-req\">required</span>" : ""
                    html += """
                    <div class="param">
                    <span class="param-name">\(p.name)</span>
                    <span class="param-type">\(p.type)</span>
                    <span>\(p.description) \(req)</span>
                    </div>
                    """
                }
                html += "</div>"
            }
            html += "</div>"
        }

        html += "</body></html>"
        return html
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLKit/RPCTypes.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

// MARK: - JSON-RPC 2.0 Types

struct JSONRPCRequest: Codable {
    let jsonrpc: String
    let method: String
    let params: [String: JSONValue]?
    let id: JSONValue?
}

struct JSONRPCResponse: Encodable {
    let jsonrpc: String = "2.0"
    let result: [String: JSONValue]?
    let error: JSONRPCError?
    let id: JSONValue?
}

struct JSONRPCError: Encodable {
    let code: Int
    let message: String
    let data: [String: JSONValue]?

    static let parseError = JSONRPCError(code: -32700, message: "Parse error", data: nil)
    static let invalidRequest = JSONRPCError(code: -32600, message: "Invalid Request", data: nil)
    static let methodNotFound = JSONRPCError(code: -32601, message: "Method not found", data: nil)
    static let invalidParams = JSONRPCError(code: -32602, message: "Invalid params", data: nil)
    static let internalError = JSONRPCError(code: -32603, message: "Internal error", data: nil)
    /// Auth failure. Distinct code (-32099) so the HTTP layer can map ONLY this to
    /// 401 — business errors use serverError(-32000) and must return HTTP 200 with
    /// the failure in the JSON-RPC error body (otherwise a slow/timed-out action
    /// looks like "unauthorized" to clients).
    static let unauthorizedCode = -32099
    static let unauthorized = JSONRPCError(code: unauthorizedCode, message: "Unauthorized: valid auth token required", data: nil)

    static func serverError(_ msg: String) -> JSONRPCError {
        JSONRPCError(code: -32000, message: msg, data: nil)
    }
}

// MARK: - JSON Value (heterogeneous)

enum JSONValue: Codable, Equatable {
    case string(String)
    case int(Int)
    case double(Double)
    case bool(Bool)
    case null
    case array([JSONValue])
    case object([String: JSONValue])

    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
        let container = try decoder.singleValueContainer()
        if container.decodeNil() {
            self = .null
        } else if let v = try? container.decode(Bool.self) {
            self = .bool(v)
        } else if let v = try? container.decode(Int.self) {
            self = .int(v)
        } else if let v = try? container.decode(Double.self) {
            self = .double(v)
        } else if let v = try? container.decode(String.self) {
            self = .string(v)
        } else if let v = try? container.decode([JSONValue].self) {
            self = .array(v)
        } else if let v = try? container.decode([String: JSONValue].self) {
            self = .object(v)
        } else {
            throw DecodingError.dataCorruptedError(in: container, debugDescription: "Unsupported JSON value")
        }
    }

    func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
        var container = encoder.singleValueContainer()
        switch self {
        case .string(let v): try container.encode(v)
        case .int(let v): try container.encode(v)
        case .double(let v): try container.encode(v)
        case .bool(let v): try container.encode(v)
        case .null: try container.encodeNil()
        case .array(let v): try container.encode(v)
        case .object(let v): try container.encode(v)
        }
    }

    var stringValue: String? {
        if case .string(let v) = self { return v }
        return nil
    }

    var doubleValue: Double? {
        switch self {
        case .double(let v): return v
        case .int(let v): return Double(v)
        default: return nil
        }
    }

    var boolValue: Bool? {
        if case .bool(let v) = self { return v }
        return nil
    }

    var intValue: Int? {
        switch self {
        case .int(let v): return v
        case .double(let v): return Int(v)      // JSON numbers often parse as double
        default: return nil
        }
    }

    var objectValue: [String: JSONValue]? {
        if case .object(let v) = self { return v }
        return nil
    }

    func toAny() -> Any {
        switch self {
        case .string(let v): return v
        case .int(let v): return v
        case .double(let v): return v
        case .bool(let v): return v
        case .null: return NSNull()
        case .array(let v): return v.map { $0.toAny() }
        case .object(let v): return v.mapValues { $0.toAny() }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Auth Types

struct AuthRequest: Codable {
    let clientName: String

    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
        case clientName = "client_name"
    }
}

struct AuthResponse: Encodable {
    let token: String
    let expiresIn: Int?

    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
        case token
        case expiresIn = "expires_in"
    }
}

/// One paired client. `id` is the token id (first 4 bytes of SHA256(K), hex) —
/// it is what the wire sends as `tok` and is a lookup handle only, never a
/// secret. `keyHex` is the actual 32-byte key K used to derive the per-request
/// MAC/encryption keys; it never leaves the device after pairing.
///
/// Expiry is idle-based: a session dies only after `inactivityWindow` of no use.
/// Every authenticated request slides `lastActiveAt` forward, so a token in
/// regular use never expires.
struct AuthSession: Identifiable, Codable {
    let id: String
    let keyHex: String
    let clientName: String
    let grantedAt: Date
    var lastActiveAt: Date
    /// Where the last authenticated request came from: the peer address
    /// (no port) and how it arrived — see `PeerSource`. Nil for sessions not
    /// used since this was recorded.
    var lastAddress: String?
    var lastVia: String?

    /// The 32-byte key, or nil if the stored record is corrupt.
    var key: Data? { Data(hexString: keyHex) }

    /// "Expiry if never used again" — informational, recomputed from last use.
    var expiresAt: Date { lastActiveAt.addingTimeInterval(AuthManager.inactivityWindow) }

    var isExpired: Bool { Date() >= expiresAt }

    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
        case id
        case keyHex = "key"
        case clientName = "client_name"
        case grantedAt = "granted_at"
        case lastActiveAt = "last_active_at"
        case lastAddress = "last_address"
        case lastVia = "last_via"
    }
}

/// How a request reached the server, judged by the interface it arrived on.
enum PeerSource: String {
    /// Loopback: an app on this device, or a computer over USB (usbmuxd
    /// forwards to the device's loopback, so the two look the same).
    case local
    /// Wi-Fi, Ethernet or the Personal Hotspot bridge.
    case lan
    /// Apple peer-to-peer Wi-Fi (AWDL): nearby discovery.
    case nearby
    /// A VPN or proxy tunnel (utun, ipsec, ppp).
    case vpn
    case cellular
    case other
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLKit/RemoteHTML.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

/// Static HTML for GET /remote — a browser control page: plays the live MPEG-TS
/// stream in <video> (via mpegts.js) and drives the device with the same JSON-RPC
/// as the desktop GUI (tap/swipe/scroll/keyboard + a side panel of buttons).
/// The visual style is a light-touch shadcn/ui port — Tailwind-flavor tokens,
/// Radix-ish surfaces (zinc, subtle border, rounded, focus rings) — hand-written
/// in CSS so the page stays a single self-contained file.
///
/// The page has NO external network dependency: CSS is inline, mpegts.js is
/// vendored into MpegtsJS.swift and inlined at build time. Works fully offline.
///
/// The page holds the 32-byte pairing key and does the protocol-v1 crypto in
/// the browser (WebCrypto HMAC-SHA256): every /rpc body is sealed locally and
/// the key itself is never transmitted.
enum RemoteHTML {
    /// Web app manifest for GET /remote/manifest.webmanifest. Added to the Home
    /// Screen, the page opens in full screen with nothing of the browser around it.
    static let manifest: String = #"""
{
  "name": "iCTRL Remote",
  "short_name": "iCTRL Remote",
  "start_url": "/remote?fullscreen=1",
  "scope": "/remote",
  "display": "fullscreen",
  "background_color": "#000000",
  "theme_color": "#000000",
  "icons": [{ "src": "/remote/icon.png", "sizes": "180x180", "type": "image/png" }]
}
"""#

<div id="status">
  <span class="dot off" id="statusDotBar"></span>
  <span id="statusText">Idle</span>
  <span class="sep">•</span>
  <span id="lastAction" class="toast" style="display:none"></span>
```
