`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLUITests/EarlyURLHook.m`:

```m
//
//  EarlyURLHook.m
//  Installs the ictrl:// URL capture hooks as early as possible — at bundle
//  load, BEFORE XCTest's setUp runs. This matters on a COLD start: iOS calls
//  the runner's application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: (carrying the launch
//  URL) before our Swift setUp executes, so a Swift-side install in setUp would
//  miss it. Here we capture the launch URL and any early openURL into a shared
//  store that the Swift URLSchemeHandler drains once the server is up.
//

#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
#import <UIKit/UIKit.h>
#import <QuartzCore/QuartzCore.h>   // CACurrentMediaTime
#import <objc/runtime.h>
#import <objc/message.h>
#import <notify.h>
#import <fcntl.h>
#import <unistd.h>

// Thread-safe stash of early-captured URLs. URLSchemeHandler (Swift) reads these
// via +[EarlyURLHook drainURLs] and merges them into its pending queue.
static NSMutableArray<NSURL *> *sEarlyURLs;
static NSMutableArray<NSString *> *sEarlyLogs;   // events captured before Swift log is ready
static NSLock *sEarlyLock;

// Set to YES by Swift (via +[EarlyURLHook markTestStarted]) once testStartServer
// actually begins. The bootstrap watchdog uses this to decide whether to re-kick
// runTestsInBackground: — the passcode prompt on first launch can interrupt the
// XCTest bootstrap so the test method never runs and the server never comes up.
static BOOL sTestStarted = NO;
static BOOL sEarlyBackgroundArmed = NO;

// Set to YES by Swift (via +[EarlyURLHook markSetUpEntered]) the moment
// setUpWithError runs. This distinguishes the two failure modes:
//   - setUp NEVER entered  → XCTest bootstrap never ran (passcode interrupted
//     runTestsInBackground:). Safe to re-kick — nothing is running to re-enter.
//   - setUp entered but test not "started" → the test IS running, just slow to
//     mark itself. Re-kicking here re-enters XCTest → the symbolication abort
//     crash. So we must NOT re-kick in this case.
static BOOL sSetUpEntered = NO;

// Bootstrap recovery: KEEP retrying runTestsInBackground: until the test starts
// or a total deadline elapses. The passcode ("Enable UI Automation") prompt can
// stay up for MINUTES, and each interrupted launch dies before setUp — so a
// once-only or short-window re-kick misses it entirely (confirmed on-device:
// 6+ minutes of passcode, +load fired repeatedly, but no re-kick could bridge
// it and the user had to tap the icon manually).
//
// Two things make continuous retry safe (avoiding the "symbolication service
// already set" double-bootstrap crash that killed the old aggressive watchdog):
//   1. The guard: only re-kick when NEITHER setUp NOR the test has begun. If a
//      bootstrap actually reached setUp, we never re-kick.
//   2. Serialization: at most one re-kick in flight at a time (sReKickInFlight),
//      cleared on a short delay, so we never stack concurrent runTestsInBackground:.
static double sBootstrapDeadline = 0.0;    // CACurrentMediaTime() past which we give up
static int    sReKickAttempts    = 0;      // diagnostics: how many re-kicks fired
static BOOL   sReKickInFlight     = NO;     // don't overlap re-kicks
static BOOL   sPollArmed          = NO;     // ensure the poll loop is armed once

// Diagnostic observation window (5 min — covers a slow passcode entry).
static const double kBootstrapMaxWindow = 300.0;

@interface EarlyURLHook : NSObject
+ (NSArray<NSURL *> *)drainURLs;
+ (NSArray<NSString *> *)drainLogs;
+ (void)hookDelegateInstance:(id<UIApplicationDelegate>)delegate;
+ (void)tryInstall;
+ (void)hookClass:(Class)cls;
+ (void)markTestStarted;
+ (void)markSetUpEntered;
+ (void)scheduleBootstrapWatchdogForDelegate:(id)delegate;
+ (void)armAbsoluteBootstrapFallback;
+ (void)reKickIfNeeded:(id)delegate;
+ (void)armBootstrapRetryLoop;
+ (void)pollBootstrapOnce;
@end

/// Append one +load-era line DIRECTLY to today's persisted log file. These lines
/// run before Swift logging exists and are normally only flushed when setUp/URL
/// handling drains the buffer — but if the first-launch passcode interrupts
/// bootstrap, setUp never runs and those lines (incl. the bootstrap watchdog /
/// fallback activity) are lost, creating an observability black hole. So we also
/// write straight to the file here, so the recovery path is always traceable.
static void earlyLogWriteToFile(NSString *msg) {
    @try {
        NSArray *dirs = NSSearchPathForDirectoriesInDomains(NSLibraryDirectory, NSUserDomainMask, YES);
        if (dirs.count == 0) { return; }
        NSString *dir = [dirs[0] stringByAppendingPathComponent:@"Logs/iCTRL"];
        [[NSFileManager defaultManager] createDirectoryAtPath:dir withIntermediateDirectories:YES attributes:nil error:nil];
        NSDateFormatter *df = [[NSDateFormatter alloc] init];
        df.dateFormat = @"yyyy-MM-dd"; df.locale = [NSLocale localeWithLocaleIdentifier:@"en_US_POSIX"];
        NSString *day = [df stringFromDate:[NSDate date]];
        NSString *path = [dir stringByAppendingPathComponent:[NSString stringWithFormat:@"ictrl-%@.log", day]];
        NSDateFormatter *tf = [[NSDateFormatter alloc] init]; tf.dateFormat = @"HH:mm:ss.SSS";
        NSString *line = [NSString stringWithFormat:@"[%@] %@\n", [tf stringFromDate:[NSDate date]], msg];
        int fd = open(path.fileSystemRepresentation, O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT, 0644);
        if (fd >= 0) { write(fd, line.UTF8String, strlen(line.UTF8String)); close(fd); }
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
}

/// Record an event to the console, the drain buffer (for the in-memory log), AND
/// straight to the persisted file (so it survives a bootstrap that never reaches
/// setUp — see earlyLogWriteToFile).
static void earlyLog(NSString *msg) {
    NSLog(@"%@", msg);
    [sEarlyLock lock];
    if (sEarlyLogs) { [sEarlyLogs addObject:msg]; }
    [sEarlyLock unlock];
    earlyLogWriteToFile(msg);
}

static void stashURL(NSURL *url) {
    if (![[url.scheme lowercaseString] isEqualToString:@"ictrl"]) { return; }
    [sEarlyLock lock];
    [sEarlyURLs addObject:url];
    [sEarlyLock unlock];
    earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔗 early-captured URL %@://%@", url.scheme, url.host ?: @""]);
}

// Replacement for application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: — reads launch URL,
// then CHAINS to the original impl (via the exchanged tmp selector) so XCTest's
// own boot logic still runs. If there was no original (we added, not exchanged),
// the tmp selector won't respond and we just return YES.
static BOOL hookedDidFinishLaunching(id self, SEL _cmd, id application, NSDictionary *options) {
    NSURL *url = options[UIApplicationLaunchOptionsURLKey];
    earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔎 didFinishLaunching fired; launchURL=%@; optionKeys=%@",
              url ? url.absoluteString : @"(none)", options.allKeys]);
    if ([url isKindOfClass:[NSURL class]]) { stashURL(url); }
    // Arm the bootstrap watchdog in case the passcode prompt interrupts the test
    // kickoff (self is the _XCTRunnerAppDelegate).
    [EarlyURLHook scheduleBootstrapWatchdogForDelegate:self];
    SEL orig = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:");
    if ([self respondsToSelector:orig]) {
        BOOL (*imp)(id, SEL, id, NSDictionary *) = (BOOL (*)(id, SEL, id, NSDictionary *))
            [self methodForSelector:orig];
        return imp(self, orig, application, options);
    }
    return YES;
}

// Replacement for application:openURL:options: — reads warm-path URLs, then
// chains to the original if present.
static BOOL hookedOpenURL(id self, SEL _cmd, id application, NSURL *url, NSDictionary *options) {
    earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔎 openURL fired; url=%@", url ? url.absoluteString : @"(none)"]);
    if ([url isKindOfClass:[NSURL class]]) { stashURL(url); }
    SEL orig = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_application:openURL:options:");
    if ([self respondsToSelector:orig]) {
        BOOL (*imp)(id, SEL, id, NSURL *, NSDictionary *) = (BOOL (*)(id, SEL, id, NSURL *, NSDictionary *))
            [self methodForSelector:orig];
        return imp(self, orig, application, url, options);
    }
    return YES;
}

// The runner uses a SCENE-based lifecycle: warm-path URLs arrive via
// -scene:openURLContexts: (a Set<UIOpenURLContext>). Extract each context's URL.
static void hookedSceneOpenURLContexts(id self, SEL _cmd, id scene, NSSet *contexts) {
    earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔎 scene:openURLContexts fired; count=%lu",
              (unsigned long)contexts.count]);
    for (id ctx in contexts) {
        if ([ctx respondsToSelector:@selector(URL)]) {
            NSURL *url = [ctx performSelector:@selector(URL)];
            if ([url isKindOfClass:[NSURL class]]) { stashURL(url); }
        }
    }
    SEL orig = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_scene:openURLContexts:");
    if ([self respondsToSelector:orig]) {
        void (*imp)(id, SEL, id, NSSet *) = (void (*)(id, SEL, id, NSSet *))[self methodForSelector:orig];
        imp(self, orig, scene, contexts);
    }
}

// COLD-path for scene lifecycle: -scene:willConnectToSession:options: carries a
// UISceneConnectionOptions whose .URLContexts holds the launch URL(s).
static void hookedSceneWillConnect(id self, SEL _cmd, id scene, id session, id connectionOptions) {
    NSSet *urlContexts = nil;
    if ([connectionOptions respondsToSelector:@selector(URLContexts)]) {
        urlContexts = [connectionOptions performSelector:@selector(URLContexts)];
    }
    earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔎 scene:willConnect fired; urlContexts=%lu",
              (unsigned long)urlContexts.count]);
    for (id ctx in urlContexts) {
        if ([ctx respondsToSelector:@selector(URL)]) {
            NSURL *url = [ctx performSelector:@selector(URL)];
            if ([url isKindOfClass:[NSURL class]]) { stashURL(url); }
        }
    }
    // Arm the bootstrap watchdog on the actual app delegate (which owns
    // runTestsInBackground:), in case the passcode prompt interrupted kickoff.
    [EarlyURLHook scheduleBootstrapWatchdogForDelegate:[UIApplication sharedApplication].delegate];
    SEL orig = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_scene:willConnectToSession:options:");
    if ([self respondsToSelector:orig]) {
        void (*imp)(id, SEL, id, id, id) = (void (*)(id, SEL, id, id, id))[self methodForSelector:orig];
        imp(self, orig, scene, session, connectionOptions);
    }
}

// Swizzled -[UIApplication setDelegate:] — fires the instant the runner installs
// its app delegate, which is GUARANTEED to be before UIApplicationMain calls
// application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:. That's the only reliable window to
// hook the delegate early enough to catch the cold-start launch URL.
static void (*original_setDelegate)(id, SEL, id<UIApplicationDelegate>);
static void swizzled_setDelegate(id self, SEL _cmd, id<UIApplicationDelegate> delegate) {
    if (delegate) {
        earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🔎 UIApplication delegate set: %@",
                  NSStringFromClass(object_getClass(delegate))]);
        [EarlyURLHook hookDelegateInstance:delegate];
    }
    if (original_setDelegate) { original_setDelegate(self, _cmd, delegate); }
}

/// Private XCTest API: the sanctioned way for a runner to open a URL.
@interface XCTRunnerDaemonSession : NSObject
+ (instancetype)sharedSession;
- (void)openDefaultApplicationForURL:(NSURL *)url
                          completion:(void (^)(BOOL result, NSError *error))completion;
@end

@implementation EarlyURLHook

+ (void)load {
    sEarlyURLs = [NSMutableArray array];
    sEarlyLogs = [NSMutableArray array];
    sEarlyLock = [[NSLock alloc] init];

    // Swizzle UIApplication setDelegate: so we hook the delegate the moment it's
    // set (before didFinishLaunching). Fall back to a direct class hook too.
    Method m = class_getInstanceMethod([UIApplication class], @selector(setDelegate:));
    if (m) {
        original_setDelegate = (void (*)(id, SEL, id<UIApplicationDelegate>))method_getImplementation(m);
        method_setImplementation(m, (IMP)swizzled_setDelegate);
    }

    // Also try the class-based hook now and on the main queue, as a backstop.
    [self tryInstall];
    dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{ [EarlyURLHook tryInstall]; });

    earlyLog(@"🟩 +load reached — early hooks + bootstrap fallback arming");

    // DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY bootstrap observer. We do NOT re-kick runTestsInBackground:
    // any more.
    //
    // Why re-kick was removed (crash 2026-07-17-220237, SIGABRT):
    // The crash backtrace showed the ORIGINAL bootstrap was alive and blocked
    // inside `-[XCUIDevice enableAutomationMode:]` (an XCTWaiter waiting on the
    // "Enable UI Automation" authorization) — it hadn't reached setUp, so our
    // `!sSetUpEntered` guard let the re-kick through. Re-invoking
    // runTestsInBackground: then ran a SECOND `_XCTestMain` →
    // `registerSharedServiceWithConfiguration:` → "shared symbolication service
    // already set" → abort(). This is exactly the double-bootstrap crash a9c60da
    // removed the watchdog for.
    //
    // From inside the process there is NO reliable way to tell "bootstrap is
    // BLOCKED on the passcode (alive)" from "bootstrap DIED" — didBecomeActive
    // fires in BOTH cases (the alert appearing/dismissing toggles active). So any
    // in-process re-kick risks re-entering a live bootstrap → crash. We therefore
    // only OBSERVE and log; recovery of a truly-dead bootstrap needs an external
    // relaunch (see notes in the repo).
    [self armBootstrapObserver];
    [self armEarlyBackgrounding];
}

/// Diagnostic observer: logs the bootstrap-relevant lifecycle events (retry
/// window + didBecomeActive) so a passcode repro is fully traceable, but never
/// calls runTestsInBackground:. Idempotent.
/// Clear the pre-setUp stall by backgrounding, once it is safe to.
///
/// XCTest can hang before setUp for 10-18s; backgrounding the runner releases
/// it immediately. The hazard is that on first launch XCTest also puts up its
/// own "enable UI automation" passcode prompt, and suspending into THAT cancels
/// the authorization and kills the launch — which an earlier version did,
/// because a device-lock check doesn't see it (the device is unlocked while it
/// shows).
///
/// The distinguishing signal is scene activation state. The prompt is presented
/// by LocalAuthenticationUIService and deactivates our scene while it is up, so
/// `foregroundInactive` means something is in front of us and we must wait.
/// UIKit maintains this independently of XCTest, so unlike XCUIApplication it is
/// safe to read this early.
+ (BOOL)isCoveredBySystemPrompt {
    for (UIScene *scene in UIApplication.sharedApplication.connectedScenes) {
        if (scene.activationState == UISceneActivationStateForegroundInactive) {
            return YES;
        }
    }
    return NO;
}

+ (void)armEarlyBackgrounding {
    if (sEarlyBackgroundArmed) { return; }
    sEarlyBackgroundArmed = YES;
    earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background armed — will suspend once nothing covers the runner");
    [self attemptEarlyBackgroundingWithRetriesRemaining:60];
}

/// Poll until nothing is covering us, then suspend once.
///
/// 60 x 0.5s = 30s, budgeted for a person typing a passcode rather than machine
/// latency. Giving up leaves the runner in front — a stall the user can clear,
/// which is much cheaper than a launch that dies.
+ (void)attemptEarlyBackgroundingWithRetriesRemaining:(NSInteger)retries {
    dispatch_after(dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, (int64_t)(0.5 * NSEC_PER_SEC)),
                   dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{
        if (sSetUpEntered || sTestStarted) {
            earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background skipped — bootstrap already progressed");
            return;
        }
        if ([self isCoveredBySystemPrompt]) {
            // Log the state once, not every 0.5s. If this signal turns out not to
            // track the passcode sheet, that fact needs to be visible in the log
            // rather than inferred from the outcome — this whole area has already
            // cost several rounds of guessing.
            // Every 2s rather than every tick: often enough to show progress,
            // rare enough not to bury the rest of the log.
            if (retries % 4 == 0) {
                earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:
                          @"🏠 early-background waiting — a system prompt covers the runner (%.0fs left)",
                          retries * 0.5]);
            }
            if (retries > 0) {
                [self attemptEarlyBackgroundingWithRetriesRemaining:retries - 1];
            } else {
                earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background gave up — a prompt is still up");
            }
            return;
        }
        // Device lock is a separate case: the runner can be launched from the
        // lock screen, and backgrounding then discards the launch in progress.
        static int lockToken = -1;
        uint64_t lockState = 0;
        if (lockToken == -1 &&
            notify_register_check("com.apple.springboard.lockstate", &lockToken) != NOTIFY_STATUS_OK) {
            lockToken = -2;
        }
        if (lockToken >= 0 && notify_get_state(lockToken, &lockState) == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK && lockState != 0) {
            if (retries % 4 == 0) {
                earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:
                          @"🏠 early-background waiting — device is locked (%.0fs left)", retries * 0.5]);
            }
            if (retries > 0) {
                [self attemptEarlyBackgroundingWithRetriesRemaining:retries - 1];
            } else {
                earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background gave up — device still locked");
            }
            return;
        }

        UIApplication *app = UIApplication.sharedApplication;
        SEL sus = NSSelectorFromString(@"suspend");
        if (![app respondsToSelector:sus]) {
            earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background unavailable — no suspend selector");
            return;
        }
        @try {
            ((void (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(app, sus);
            earlyLog(@"🏠 early-background: suspended (pre-setUp)");
        } @catch (NSException *e) {
            earlyLog([NSString stringWithFormat:@"🏠 early-background raised: %@", e.reason]);
        }
    });
}

+ (void)armBootstrapObserver {
    if (sPollArmed) { return; }
    sPollArmed = YES;
    sBootstrapDeadline = CACurrentMediaTime() + kBootstrapMaxWindow;
    earlyLog(@"👀 bootstrap observer armed (diagnostic-only, no re-kick)");

    [[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter]
        addObserverForName:UIApplicationDidBecomeActiveNotification
                    object:nil queue:[NSOperationQueue mainQueue]
                usingBlock:^(NSNotification * _Nonnull note) {
        if (sTestStarted || sSetUpEntered) { return; }
        earlyLog(@"🟢 didBecomeActive — bootstrap not yet at setUp (observing, NOT re-kicking)");
    }];
}

/// Kept for source compatibility — the delegate callbacks still call this. Now a
/// no-op-ish arming of the diagnostic observer.
+ (void)armAbsoluteBootstrapFallback {
    [self armBootstrapObserver];
}
+ (void)armBootstrapRetryLoop {
    [self armBootstrapObserver];
}
+ (void)pollBootstrapOnce { /* removed — no in-process re-kick */ }

/// Retained as a guarded no-op so any caller that still references it can't
/// accidentally re-introduce the double-bootstrap crash. Intentionally does
/// NOT call runTestsInBackground:.
+ (void)reKickIfNeeded:(id)delegate {
    (void)delegate;
    // Deliberately does nothing. In-process re-kick of runTestsInBackground: was
    // removed after it re-entered a live (passcode-blocked) bootstrap and
    // abort()ed on "shared symbolication service already set". Kept as a symbol
    // so existing call sites compile.
    (void)sReKickInFlight; (void)sReKickAttempts;   // silence unused-static warnings
    earlyLog(@"🔁 re-kick suppressed — in-process re-kick removed (double-bootstrap crash risk)");
}

/// Hook a concrete delegate INSTANCE's class (covers cases where the runner's
/// delegate is a subclass we didn't know the name of).
+ (void)hookDelegateInstance:(id<UIApplicationDelegate>)delegate {
    Class cls = object_getClass(delegate);
    if (!cls) { return; }
    [self hookClass:cls];
}

static BOOL sInstalled = NO;

+ (void)tryInstall {
    if (sInstalled) { return; }
    Class cls = NSClassFromString(@"_XCTRunnerAppDelegate");
    if (!cls) { return; }
    [self hookClass:cls];
}

+ (void)hookClass:(Class)cls {
    if (sInstalled) { return; }
    sInstalled = YES;

    // application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:  (cold path)
    SEL dfl = NSSelectorFromString(@"application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:");
    if (!class_addMethod(cls, dfl, (IMP)hookedDidFinishLaunching, "B@:@@")) {
        SEL tmp = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:");
        if (class_addMethod(cls, tmp, (IMP)hookedDidFinishLaunching, "B@:@@")) {
            Method a = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, dfl);
            Method b = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, tmp);
            if (a && b) { method_exchangeImplementations(a, b); }
        }
    }

    // application:openURL:options:  (warm path, app-delegate lifecycle)
    SEL ou = NSSelectorFromString(@"application:openURL:options:");
    if (!class_addMethod(cls, ou, (IMP)hookedOpenURL, "B@:@@@")) {
        SEL tmp = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_application:openURL:options:");
        if (class_addMethod(cls, tmp, (IMP)hookedOpenURL, "B@:@@@")) {
            Method a = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, ou);
            Method b = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, tmp);
            if (a && b) { method_exchangeImplementations(a, b); }
        }
    }

    // scene:openURLContexts:  (warm path, SCENE lifecycle — what the runner uses)
    SEL sou = NSSelectorFromString(@"scene:openURLContexts:");
    if (!class_addMethod(cls, sou, (IMP)hookedSceneOpenURLContexts, "v@:@@")) {
        SEL tmp = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_scene:openURLContexts:");
        if (class_addMethod(cls, tmp, (IMP)hookedSceneOpenURLContexts, "v@:@@")) {
            Method a = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sou);
            Method b = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, tmp);
            if (a && b) { method_exchangeImplementations(a, b); }
        }
    }

    // scene:willConnectToSession:options:  (COLD path, SCENE lifecycle)
    SEL swc = NSSelectorFromString(@"scene:willConnectToSession:options:");
    if (!class_addMethod(cls, swc, (IMP)hookedSceneWillConnect, "v@:@@@")) {
        SEL tmp = NSSelectorFromString(@"ictrlearly_scene:willConnectToSession:options:");
        if (class_addMethod(cls, tmp, (IMP)hookedSceneWillConnect, "v@:@@@")) {
            Method a = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, swc);
            Method b = class_getInstanceMethod(cls, tmp);
            if (a && b) { method_exchangeImplementations(a, b); }
        }
    }

    earlyLog(@"🔗 early URL hooks installed (app + scene lifecycle)");
}

+ (void)markTestStarted {
    sTestStarted = YES;
    earlyLog(@"✅ testStartServer began — bootstrap OK");
}

+ (void)markSetUpEntered {
    sSetUpEntered = YES;
}

// Bootstrap watchdog — recovers from the first-launch passcode prompt
// interrupting XCTest bootstrap (so runTestsInBackground: never ran and the test
// method never executes → silent, no setUp, no crash), WITHOUT reintroducing the
// symbolication re-entrancy crash.
//
// The crash happened when we re-kicked while the test was ALREADY running (just
// slow to mark itself started) — re-entering XCTest aborts with "shared
// symbolication service ... already set". The fix is to only re-kick when the
// test truly never began: setUp has NOT entered AND the test has NOT started. In
// the passcode-interrupted case neither ever fires (bootstrap never reached the
// test), so a single re-kick is safe; in the "running but slow" case sSetUpEntered
// is YES, so we DON'T re-kick and can't crash. Re-kick at most once, after a long
// delay (well past a normal cold start), guarded by @try.
+ (void)scheduleBootstrapWatchdogForDelegate:(id)delegate {
    if (!delegate) { return; }
    if (![delegate respondsToSelector:NSSelectorFromString(@"runTestsInBackground:")]) { return; }
    // The delegate callbacks (didFinishLaunching / scene:willConnect) just make
    // sure the continuous retry loop is armed — the loop itself owns re-kicking.
    [EarlyURLHook armBootstrapRetryLoop];
}

+ (NSArray<NSURL *> *)drainURLs {
    [sEarlyLock lock];
    NSArray *urls = [sEarlyURLs copy];
    [sEarlyURLs removeAllObjects];
    [sEarlyLock unlock];
    return urls;
}

+ (NSArray<NSString *> *)drainLogs {
    [sEarlyLock lock];
    NSArray *logs = [sEarlyLogs copy];
    [sEarlyLogs removeAllObjects];
    [sEarlyLock unlock];
    return logs;
}

@end

```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLUITests/FMP4Muxer.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreMedia

/// Fragmented MP4 (ISO BMFF) muxer for live H.264, targeting browser MSE.
///
/// Emits:
///   - `initSegment()`   → `ftyp` + `moov` (must be sent to every new subscriber
///                          before any fragment). Uses the SPS/PPS bytes captured
///                          from the encoder to build the avcC (avc1 SampleEntry).
///   - `fragment(...)`   → one `moof` + `mdat` per encoded frame. Baseline uses
///                          a fixed 90 kHz timescale and one sample per fragment,
///                          keeping the muxer stateless-per-frame and MSE-friendly.
///
/// Only what a browser <video> needs to demux and hand to the built-in H.264
/// hardware decoder — no audio track, no edit lists, no styp.
final class FMP4Muxer {

    private let timescale: UInt32 = 90_000    // matches TS convention; keeps
                                              // decode/presentation deltas exact.
    private let trackID: UInt32 = 1
    private var sequenceNumber: UInt32 = 1    // moof mfhd counter; browsers
                                              // expect monotonic per fragment.
    private var nextBaseDecodeTime: UInt64 = 0

    private let sps: Data
    private let pps: Data
    let width: Int
    let height: Int

    init?(width: Int, height: Int, sps: Data, pps: Data) {
        guard !sps.isEmpty, !pps.isEmpty, sps.count >= 4 else { return nil }
        self.width = width; self.height = height
        self.sps = H264LowDelaySPS.rewrite(sps) ?? sps; self.pps = pps
    }

    /// RFC 6381 codec string derived from the SPS. Format: `avc1.PPCCLL`
    ///   PP = profile_idc          (sps[1])
    ///   CC = constraint_set_flags (sps[2])
    ///   LL = level_idc            (sps[3])
    /// Must be handed to MSE (`addSourceBuffer("video/mp4; codecs=…")`) or
    /// the browser silently rejects the init segment.
    var codecString: String {
        String(format: "avc1.%02X%02X%02X", sps[1], sps[2], sps[3])
    }

    // MARK: - Public API

    /// One-shot init segment (`ftyp` + `moov`). Send to every new subscriber
    /// before any fragment; the browser buffers it and uses it to configure MSE.
    func initSegment() -> Data {
        var d = Data()
        d.append(ftyp())
        d.append(moov())
        return d
    }

    /// A single-sample fragment. `durationTicks` is in the muxer's 90 kHz scale;
    /// pass `UInt32(90_000 / fps)` for evenly spaced frames.
    func fragment(nalus: [Data], durationTicks: UInt32, keyframe: Bool) -> Data {
        // Sample data = one AVCC-formatted access unit: [4-byte length + NAL]…
        var mdatPayload = Data()
        for n in nalus {
            mdatPayload.append(u32be(UInt32(n.count)))
            mdatPayload.append(n)
        }
        let sampleSize = UInt32(mdatPayload.count)
        let baseDecodeTime = nextBaseDecodeTime
        nextBaseDecodeTime &+= UInt64(durationTicks)

        // Build `moof` (metadata) referring to `mdat` right after it.
        let moofData = moof(sequenceNumber: sequenceNumber,
                            baseDecodeTime: baseDecodeTime,
                            sampleSize: sampleSize,
                            sampleDuration: durationTicks,
                            keyframe: keyframe,
                            // trun.data_offset points into the mdat *from moof start*.
                            // We know the layout: moof + mdatHeader(8) + payload,
                            // so the sample begins at moof.count + 8. We patch it
                            // below once moof size is known.
                            trunDataOffsetPlaceholder: true)
        sequenceNumber &+= 1

        // Patch trun.data_offset now that moof is fully built.
        let patched = patchTrunDataOffset(moof: moofData,
                                          dataOffset: Int32(moofData.count + 8 /* mdat header */))
        var out = Data(); out.reserveCapacity(patched.count + 8 + mdatPayload.count)
        out.append(patched)
        out.append(box("mdat", body: mdatPayload))
        return out
    }

    // MARK: - Box builders (ISO/IEC 14496-12 + 14496-15)
    // Each `box("name", body:)` prepends a 4-byte big-endian total size and the
    // 4-char type. All ISO BMFF integers are big-endian.

    private func box(_ type: String, body: Data) -> Data {
        var out = Data(); out.reserveCapacity(8 + body.count)
        out.append(u32be(UInt32(8 + body.count)))
        out.append(type.data(using: .ascii)!)
        out.append(body)
        return out
    }
    private func fullBox(_ type: String, version: UInt8 = 0, flags: UInt32 = 0, body: Data) -> Data {
        var inner = Data()
        inner.append(version)
        inner.append(u24be(flags))
        inner.append(body)
        return box(type, body: inner)
    }

    // ftyp: brands. `iso5` + `avc1` covers every major browser MSE decoder.
    private func ftyp() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append("iso5".data(using: .ascii)!)     // major brand
        b.append(u32be(512))                      // minor version
        for brand in ["iso5", "iso6", "avc1", "mp41"] {
            b.append(brand.data(using: .ascii)!)  // compatible brands
        }
        return box("ftyp", body: b)
    }

    // moov = mvhd + trak + mvex
    private func moov() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(mvhd())
        b.append(trak())
        b.append(mvex())
        return box("moov", body: b)
    }

    private func mvhd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(0))              // creation_time
        b.append(u32be(0))              // modification_time
        b.append(u32be(timescale))      // timescale
        b.append(u32be(0))              // duration (0 for fragmented)
        b.append(u32be(0x00010000))     // rate 1.0
        b.append(u16be(0x0100))         // volume 1.0
        b.append(u16be(0))              // reserved
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 8))                          // reserved [2]
        // 3x3 unity matrix + [0 0 0x40000000]
        for v: UInt32 in [0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x40000000] {
            b.append(u32be(v))
        }
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 24))                         // pre_defined [6]
        b.append(u32be(0xFFFF_FFFF))    // next_track_ID (unused for frag)
        return fullBox("mvhd", body: b)
    }

    // trak = tkhd + mdia
    private func trak() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(tkhd())
        b.append(mdia())
        return box("trak", body: b)
    }

    private func tkhd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(0)); b.append(u32be(0))          // creation/modification
        b.append(u32be(trackID))                        // track_ID
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // reserved
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // duration
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 8))          // reserved [2]
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // layer
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // alternate_group
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // volume
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // reserved
        // matrix
        for v: UInt32 in [0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x40000000] {
            b.append(u32be(v))
        }
        b.append(u32be(UInt32(width) << 16))            // width  as 16.16
        b.append(u32be(UInt32(height) << 16))           // height as 16.16
        return fullBox("tkhd", flags: 0x000007 /* enabled|inMovie|inPreview */, body: b)
    }

    // mdia = mdhd + hdlr + minf
    private func mdia() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(mdhd())
        b.append(hdlr())
        b.append(minf())
        return box("mdia", body: b)
    }

    private func mdhd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(0)); b.append(u32be(0))          // creation/modification
        b.append(u32be(timescale))                      // timescale
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // duration
        // language: 'und' packed as 3x5-bit ISO-639-2/T
        let und: UInt16 = ((UInt16(0x15) & 0x1F) << 10) | ((UInt16(0x0E) & 0x1F) << 5) | (UInt16(0x04) & 0x1F)
        b.append(u16be(und))
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // pre_defined
        return fullBox("mdhd", body: b)
    }

    private func hdlr() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // pre_defined
        b.append("vide".data(using: .ascii)!)           // handler_type
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 12))         // reserved [3]
        b.append("iCTRL Video\0".data(using: .utf8)!)   // name (null-terminated)
        return fullBox("hdlr", body: b)
    }

    // minf = vmhd + dinf + stbl
    private func minf() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(vmhd())
        b.append(dinf())
        b.append(stbl())
        return box("minf", body: b)
    }

    private func vmhd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // graphicsmode
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 6))          // opcolor [3]
        return fullBox("vmhd", flags: 1, body: b)
    }

    private func dinf() -> Data {
        // A dref with a single "self-contained" url entry — all data is in this file.
        var url = Data()
        // dref inner is: entry_count u32 + entries.
        var dref = Data()
        dref.append(u32be(1))                           // entry_count
        // url_ entry: fullBox with flag 1 = self-contained
        dref.append(fullBox("url ", flags: 1, body: Data()))
        url.append(fullBox("dref", body: dref))
        return box("dinf", body: url)
    }

    // stbl = stsd (avc1 with avcC) + stts/stsc/stsz/stco (all empty for fragmented)
    private func stbl() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(stsd())
        // Empty tables required by the spec but populated by moof for fragments.
        b.append(fullBox("stts", body: u32be(0)))
        b.append(fullBox("stsc", body: u32be(0)))
        b.append(fullBox("stsz", body: Data([0,0,0,0]) + u32be(0) + u32be(0))) // sample_size=0, sample_count=0
        b.append(fullBox("stco", body: u32be(0)))
        return box("stbl", body: b)
    }

    private func stsd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(1))                              // entry_count
        b.append(avc1())
        return fullBox("stsd", body: b)
    }

    // avc1 SampleEntry (14496-15). Fixed-size prefix + avcC child box.
    private func avc1() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 6))          // reserved [6]
        b.append(u16be(1))                              // data_reference_index
        // VisualSampleEntry fields
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // pre_defined
        b.append(u16be(0))                              // reserved
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 12))         // pre_defined [3]
        b.append(u16be(UInt16(width)))
        b.append(u16be(UInt16(height)))
        b.append(u32be(0x00480000))                     // horizresolution 72dpi
        b.append(u32be(0x00480000))                     // vertresolution 72dpi
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // reserved
        b.append(u16be(1))                              // frame_count
        b.append(Data(repeating: 0, count: 32))         // compressorname (32 bytes)
        b.append(u16be(0x0018))                         // depth
        b.append(i16be(-1))                             // pre_defined
        b.append(avcC())
        return box("avc1", body: b)
    }

    // avcC (H.264 configuration record, 14496-15 §5.2.4.1).
    private func avcC() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(UInt8(1))                              // configurationVersion
        b.append(sps[1])                                // AVCProfileIndication
        b.append(sps[2])                                // profile_compatibility
        b.append(sps[3])                                // AVCLevelIndication
        b.append(UInt8(0xFF))                           // 6 bits reserved + lengthSizeMinusOne=3
        b.append(UInt8(0xE1))                           // 3 bits reserved + numOfSPS=1
        b.append(u16be(UInt16(sps.count)))
        b.append(sps)
        b.append(UInt8(1))                              // numOfPPS
        b.append(u16be(UInt16(pps.count)))
        b.append(pps)
        return box("avcC", body: b)
    }

    // mvex = mehd + trex — declares this is a fragmented movie.
    private func mvex() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(trex())
        return box("mvex", body: b)
    }

    private func trex() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(trackID))                        // track_ID
        b.append(u32be(1))                              // default_sample_description_index
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // default_sample_duration
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // default_sample_size
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // default_sample_flags
        return fullBox("trex", body: b)
    }

    // MARK: - Fragment (moof) — one sample per fragment

    /// Layout: moof(mfhd + traf(tfhd + tfdt + trun))
    /// trun's data_offset is patched in once we know the total moof size.
    private func moof(sequenceNumber: UInt32,
                      baseDecodeTime: UInt64,
                      sampleSize: UInt32,
                      sampleDuration: UInt32,
                      keyframe: Bool,
                      trunDataOffsetPlaceholder: Bool) -> Data {
        var moofBody = Data()
        moofBody.append(mfhd(sequenceNumber: sequenceNumber))
        moofBody.append(traf(baseDecodeTime: baseDecodeTime,
                             sampleSize: sampleSize,
                             sampleDuration: sampleDuration,
                             keyframe: keyframe))
        return box("moof", body: moofBody)
    }

    private func mfhd(sequenceNumber: UInt32) -> Data {
        return fullBox("mfhd", body: u32be(sequenceNumber))
    }

    private func traf(baseDecodeTime: UInt64,
                      sampleSize: UInt32,
                      sampleDuration: UInt32,
                      keyframe: Bool) -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(tfhd())
        b.append(tfdt(baseDecodeTime: baseDecodeTime))
        b.append(trun(sampleSize: sampleSize, sampleDuration: sampleDuration, keyframe: keyframe))
        return box("traf", body: b)
    }

    // tfhd: default-base-is-moof flag (0x020000) so trun offsets are relative
    // to the moof — matches CMAF/MSE expectations.
    private func tfhd() -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(trackID))
        return fullBox("tfhd", flags: 0x020000, body: b)
    }

    // tfdt v1: 64-bit decode time.
    private func tfdt(baseDecodeTime: UInt64) -> Data {
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u64be(baseDecodeTime))
        return fullBox("tfdt", version: 1, body: b)
    }

    // trun: one sample, with per-sample duration/size/flags, plus data-offset.
    // flags: 0x000001 data-offset present
    //        0x000004 first-sample-flags-present (used to mark keyframe cleanly)
    //        0x000100 sample-duration
    //        0x000200 sample-size
    private func trun(sampleSize: UInt32, sampleDuration: UInt32, keyframe: Bool) -> Data {
        let flags: UInt32 = 0x000001 | 0x000004 | 0x000100 | 0x000200
        var b = Data()
        b.append(u32be(1))                              // sample_count
        b.append(u32be(0))                              // data_offset (patched)
        // first-sample flags: is_leading=0, depends_on: 2 if keyframe / 1 if not,
        // is_depended_on=0, has_redundancy=0, is_non_sync_sample: 0 if key / 1 if not.
        let dependsOn: UInt32 = keyframe ? 2 : 1
        let nonSync: UInt32 = keyframe ? 0 : 1
        let firstFlags: UInt32 = (dependsOn << 24) | (nonSync << 16)
        b.append(u32be(firstFlags))
        b.append(u32be(sampleDuration))
        b.append(u32be(sampleSize))
        return fullBox("trun", flags: flags, body: b)
    }

    /// The trun's data_offset field sits at a fixed spot inside its box. Rather
    /// than track it through construction, locate the trun by scanning boxes
    /// and rewrite the placeholder u32 with the real offset.
    private func patchTrunDataOffset(moof: Data, dataOffset: Int32) -> Data {
        var out = moof
        // moof (8 header) → mfhd (16 total) → traf(header 8 + tfhd 16 + tfdt 16 + trun ...)
        // trun body starts at: 8 (moof) + 16 (mfhd) + 8 (traf) + 16 (tfhd) + 20 (tfdt v1) + 8 (trun hdr) + 4 (fullbox) = 80
        // trun body layout: sample_count(4) | data_offset(4) | first_flags(4) | duration(4) | size(4)
        // So the u32 to patch is at byte 80 + 4 = 84.
        let dataOffsetPos = 84
        precondition(dataOffsetPos + 4 <= out.count, "moof shorter than expected — layout drift")
        let be = UInt32(bitPattern: dataOffset).bigEndian
        withUnsafeBytes(of: be) { raw in
            out.replaceSubrange(dataOffsetPos..<dataOffsetPos + 4, with: raw)
        }
        return out
    }

    // MARK: - Big-endian helpers

    private func u16be(_ v: UInt16) -> Data { var b = v.bigEndian; return Data(bytes: &b, count: 2) }
    private func u24be(_ v: UInt32) -> Data { Data([UInt8((v >> 16) & 0xFF), UInt8((v >> 8) & 0xFF), UInt8(v & 0xFF)]) }
    private func u32be(_ v: UInt32) -> Data { var b = v.bigEndian; return Data(bytes: &b, count: 4) }
    private func u64be(_ v: UInt64) -> Data { var b = v.bigEndian; return Data(bytes: &b, count: 8) }
    private func i16be(_ v: Int16)  -> Data { var b = v.bigEndian; return Data(bytes: &b, count: 2) }
}

/// Declares "no frame reordering" in an H.264 SPS that does not say so.
///
/// VideoToolbox emits Baseline SPSs without VUI. Lacking
/// `bitstream_restriction`, a decoder must assume frames may be reordered up
/// to the whole DPB (about five frames at this size and level) and holds
/// that many before showing the first: about a second of latency at 5 fps,
/// and a player that seeks to the live edge again before then never plays at
/// all. The stream has no B-frames, so appending a VUI with
/// `max_num_reorder_frames = 0` is true and lets the decoder output each frame
/// as it arrives. Only the SPS changes; slices do not refer to the VUI.
///
/// Returns nil (keep the original) for anything not understood: an SPS that
/// already has VUI, scaling matrices, or a malformed one.
enum H264LowDelaySPS {
    static func rewrite(_ nal: Data) -> Data? {
        let bytes = [UInt8](nal)
        guard bytes.count > 4, bytes[0] & 0x1F == 7 else { return nil }
        var r = BitReader(rbsp: unescape(Array(bytes[1...])))
        guard let profile = r.u(8), r.u(8) != nil, r.u(8) != nil, r.ue() != nil else { return nil }
        if [100, 110, 122, 244, 44, 83, 86, 118, 128, 138, 139, 134, 135].contains(profile) {
            guard let chroma = r.ue() else { return nil }
            if chroma == 3 { guard r.u(1) != nil else { return nil } }
            guard r.ue() != nil, r.ue() != nil, r.u(1) != nil, let scaling = r.u(1), scaling == 0 else { return nil }
        }
        guard r.ue() != nil, let pocType = r.ue() else { return nil }
        if pocType == 0 {
            guard r.ue() != nil else { return nil }
        } else if pocType == 1 {
            guard r.u(1) != nil, r.se() != nil, r.se() != nil, let n = r.ue() else { return nil }
            for _ in 0..<n { guard r.se() != nil else { return nil } }
        }
        guard let maxRefFrames = r.ue(), r.u(1) != nil, r.ue() != nil, r.ue() != nil,
              let frameMbsOnly = r.u(1) else { return nil }
        if frameMbsOnly == 0 { guard r.u(1) != nil else { return nil } }
        guard r.u(1) != nil, let crop = r.u(1) else { return nil }
        if crop == 1 { for _ in 0..<4 { guard r.ue() != nil else { return nil } } }
        let vuiFlagAt = r.pos
        guard let vui = r.u(1), vui == 0 else { return nil }

        // Everything before vui_parameters_present_flag, then a VUI that only
        // carries bitstream_restriction (E.1.1), then rbsp trailing bits.
        var w = BitWriter()
        var copy = BitReader(rbsp: r.data)
        for _ in 0..<vuiFlagAt { w.put(copy.u(1)!, 1) }
        w.put(1, 1)                       // vui_parameters_present_flag
        for _ in 0..<5 { w.put(0, 1) }    // aspect, overscan, signal type, chroma loc, timing
        for _ in 0..<3 { w.put(0, 1) }    // nal hrd, vcl hrd, pic_struct
        w.put(1, 1)                       // bitstream_restriction_flag
        w.put(1, 1)                       // motion_vectors_over_pic_boundaries_flag
        w.ue(2); w.ue(1)                  // max_bytes_per_pic_denom, max_bits_per_mb_denom (defaults)
        w.ue(15); w.ue(15)                // log2_max_mv_length_horizontal/vertical (defaults)
        w.ue(0)                           // max_num_reorder_frames
        w.ue(max(1, maxRefFrames))        // max_dec_frame_buffering
        w.put(1, 1)                       // rbsp_stop_one_bit
        w.align()
        return Data([bytes[0]] + escape(w.bytes))
    }

    /// Drop emulation-prevention bytes (00 00 03 → 00 00).
    private static func unescape(_ b: [UInt8]) -> [UInt8] {
        var out: [UInt8] = []; out.reserveCapacity(b.count)
        var zeros = 0
        for x in b {
            if zeros >= 2 && x == 3 { zeros = 0; continue }
            out.append(x)
            zeros = x == 0 ? zeros + 1 : 0
        }
        return out
    }

    /// Insert emulation-prevention bytes before 00 00 0x (x ≤ 3).
    private static func escape(_ b: [UInt8]) -> [UInt8] {
        var out: [UInt8] = []; out.reserveCapacity(b.count + 4)
        var zeros = 0
        for x in b {
            if zeros >= 2 && x <= 3 { out.append(3); zeros = 0 }
            out.append(x)
            zeros = x == 0 ? zeros + 1 : 0
        }
        return out
    }

    private struct BitReader {
        let data: [UInt8]
        var pos = 0
        init(rbsp: [UInt8]) { data = rbsp }
        mutating func u(_ n: Int) -> Int? {
            guard pos + n <= data.count * 8 else { return nil }
            var v = 0
            for _ in 0..<n {
                v = v << 1 | Int(data[pos >> 3] >> (7 - UInt8(pos & 7)) & 1)
                pos += 1
            }
            return v
        }
        mutating func ue() -> Int? {
            var zeros = 0
            while true {
                guard let bit = u(1) else { return nil }
                if bit == 1 { break }
                zeros += 1
                if zeros > 31 { return nil }
            }
            guard let rest = zeros > 0 ? u(zeros) : 0 else { return nil }
            return (1 << zeros) - 1 + rest
        }
        mutating func se() -> Int? {
            guard let k = ue() else { return nil }
            return k & 1 == 1 ? (k + 1) / 2 : -(k / 2)
        }
    }

    private struct BitWriter {
        var bytes: [UInt8] = []
        var bit = 0
        mutating func put(_ v: Int, _ n: Int) {
            for i in stride(from: n - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
                if bit == 0 { bytes.append(0) }
                if (v >> i) & 1 == 1 { bytes[bytes.count - 1] |= UInt8(0x80 >> bit) }
                bit = (bit + 1) & 7
            }
        }
        mutating func ue(_ v: Int) {
            let x = v + 1
            let len = Int.bitWidth - x.leadingZeroBitCount
            put(0, len - 1)
            put(x, len)
        }
        mutating func align() { while bit != 0 { put(0, 1) } }
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLUITests/FastActionHandler.swift`:

```swift
import XCTest

class FastActionHandler {
    /// Where the last tap/press landed, for the settle check to watch that
    /// spot as well as the whole screen. Cleared per call by the dispatcher.
    var lastTouchPoint: CGPoint?
    private let app: XCUIApplication

    init(app: XCUIApplication) {
        self.app = app
    }

    func fastTap(x: Double, y: Double) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        lastTouchPoint = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventRecord = XCSynthesizedEventRecord(name: "Fast Tap")
        let point = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventPath = XCPointerEventPath(forTouchAt: point, offset: 0.0)
        eventPath.pressDown(atOffset: 0.0)
        eventPath.liftUp(atOffset: 0.05)
        eventRecord.add(eventPath)

        do {
            try eventRecord.synthesize()
            return (["message": .string("Fast tapped at (\(x), \(y))")], nil)
        } catch {
            return (nil, .serverError("Fast tap failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"))
        }
    }

    /// Two taps back to back, each its own synthesize call and no sleep between.
    /// Spacing is then whatever two IPC round-trips cost — not controlled by us,
    /// which is the whole risk: too slow and the system sees two single taps.
    func fastDoubleTapSeparate(x: Double, y: Double) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        let first = fastTap(x: x, y: y)
        if let err = first.1 { return (nil, err) }
        let second = fastTap(x: x, y: y)
        if let err = second.1 { return (nil, err) }
        return (["message": .string("Fast double tapped at (\(x), \(y)) (two records)")], nil)
    }

    /// Two taps close enough together to read as a double tap.
    ///
    /// Both presses live in ONE event path, so their spacing is set by the
    /// offsets below and nothing else. Sending two separate fastTap calls does
    /// NOT work: each is its own synthesize round-trip, so the real gap is the
    /// sleep plus two IPC hops — past the ~250ms system window, and TikTok read
    /// it as a single tap (the video paused instead of liking).
    func fastDoubleTap(x: Double, y: Double) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        lastTouchPoint = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventRecord = XCSynthesizedEventRecord(name: "Fast Double Tap")
        let point = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventPath = XCPointerEventPath(forTouchAt: point, offset: 0.0)
        eventPath.pressDown(atOffset: 0.0)
        eventPath.liftUp(atOffset: 0.05)
        eventPath.pressDown(atOffset: 0.12)   // 70ms gap — well inside the window
        eventPath.liftUp(atOffset: 0.17)
        eventRecord.add(eventPath)

        do {
            try eventRecord.synthesize()
            return (["message": .string("Fast double tapped at (\(x), \(y))")], nil)
        } catch {
            return (nil, .serverError("Fast double tap failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"))
        }
    }

    /// Press and hold at a point. Same synthesized path as fastTap, just holding
    /// the touch down for `duration` before lifting, so it never pays the
    /// quiescence wait that XCUICoordinate.press(forDuration:) does.
    func fastLongPress(x: Double, y: Double, duration: Double) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        lastTouchPoint = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventRecord = XCSynthesizedEventRecord(name: "Fast Long Press")
        let point = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        let eventPath = XCPointerEventPath(forTouchAt: point, offset: 0.0)
        eventPath.pressDown(atOffset: 0.0)
        // Hold with periodic samples at the SAME point. A path that only presses
        // and lifts carries no events in between, and UIKit's long-press
        // recognizer never sees the touch persist — WeChat opened the chat as if
        // it were a plain tap. Re-stating the position every 100ms keeps the
        // touch alive for the recognizer without moving it (which would cancel).
        var t = 0.1
        while t < duration {
            eventPath.move(to: point, atOffset: t)
            t += 0.1
        }
        eventPath.liftUp(atOffset: duration)
        eventRecord.add(eventPath)

        do {
            try eventRecord.synthesize()
            return (["message": .string("Fast long-pressed at (\(x), \(y)) for \(duration)s")], nil)
        } catch {
            return (nil, .serverError("Fast long press failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"))
        }
    }

    /// `hold`: how long the finger rests at the end before lifting. A finger
    /// that stops before it lifts leaves with no velocity, so the content
    /// stops where the drag ended — no momentum, whatever the drag speed.
    func fastSwipe(fromX: Double, fromY: Double, toX: Double, toY: Double, duration: Double = 0.3,
                   hold: Double = 0.05) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        let eventRecord = XCSynthesizedEventRecord(name: "Fast Swipe")
        let startPoint = CGPoint(x: fromX, y: fromY)
        let endPoint = CGPoint(x: toX, y: toY)
        let eventPath = XCPointerEventPath(forTouchAt: startPoint, offset: 0.0)
        eventPath.pressDown(atOffset: 0.0)
        eventPath.move(to: endPoint, atOffset: duration)
        // A long hold gets stationary samples at the end point. Without them,
        // iOS estimates lift-off velocity from the last moving segment and adds
        // momentum however long the finger rested. With them, a fast drag
        // stops where it was aimed.
        if hold >= 0.1 {
            var t = duration + 0.04
            var jitter = 0.3   // identical points may be coalesced away
            while t < duration + hold - 0.01 {
                eventPath.move(to: CGPoint(x: endPoint.x, y: endPoint.y + jitter), atOffset: t)
                jitter = -jitter
                t += 0.04
            }
        }
        eventPath.liftUp(atOffset: duration + hold)
        eventRecord.add(eventPath)

        do {
            try eventRecord.synthesize()
            return (["message": .string("Swiped from (\(Int(fromX)),\(Int(fromY))) to (\(Int(toX)),\(Int(toY))) over \(String(format: "%.2g", duration))s")], nil)
        } catch {
            return (nil, .serverError("Fast swipe failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"))
        }
    }

    func fastTypeText(_ text: String) -> ([String: JSONValue]?, JSONRPCError?) {
        let eventRecord = XCSynthesizedEventRecord(name: "Fast Type")
        let eventPath = XCPointerEventPath(forTextInput: ())
        eventPath.typeText(text, atOffset: 0.0, typingSpeed: 60, shouldRedact: false)
        eventRecord.add(eventPath)

        do {
            try eventRecord.synthesize()
            return (["message": .string("Fast typed: \(text)")], nil)
        } catch {
            return (nil, .serverError("Fast type failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"))
        }
    }
}
```

`vendor/ictrl/iCTRLUITests/ForegroundApp.h`:

```h
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
#import <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>   // CGRect in renderBoundedSnapshot:visibleRect:

NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_BEGIN

/// Resolves the bundle identifier of the app currently in the foreground.
/// Uses private XCTest accessibility APIs (same approach as WebDriverAgent).
/// Returns nil if it cannot be determined.
@interface ForegroundApp : NSObject

+ (nullable NSString *)currentBundleID;
/// pid of the app in front (SpringBoard at the home screen), from the
/// accessibility client's activeApplications; 0 if unavailable. Readable
/// where currentBundleID can't name the app: Xcode 27's XCTest dropped the
/// -[XCUIApplication initWithProcessID:] that pid → bundle id lookup used.
+ (pid_t)frontmostPID;
/// Cap how long one accessibility message to an app may take (XCTest's
/// AX timeout). Returns the previous value, or a negative number if the
/// private API is missing.
+ (double)setAXTimeout:(double)seconds;
/// pid XCTest knows for an app (0 if not running or not tracked). Used for
/// SpringBoard, which XCTest always tracks.
+ (pid_t)processIDForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// Lists installed apps as [{bundle_id, name}] via the private
/// LSApplicationWorkspace API. Returns nil if unavailable. `userOnly` filters
/// out system apps when possible.
+ (nullable NSArray<NSDictionary *> *)installedAppsUserOnly:(BOOL)userOnly;

/// Opens an app by bundle id WITHOUT blocking (LSApplicationWorkspace, same as
/// WebDriverAgent). Returns NO immediately if the app can't be opened — no hang.
+ (BOOL)openBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;
+ (nullable NSDictionary *)visibleListParts:(NSString *)bundleId screen:(CGRect)screen maxElements:(NSInteger)maxElements;

/// Opens an arbitrary URL (any scheme, with query) from inside the XCTest runner,
/// where UIApplication.openURL is unreliable. Uses LSApplicationWorkspace's
/// openSensitiveURL:/openURL: private APIs. Returns YES on success.
+ (BOOL)openURL:(NSURL *)url;

/// Activate an app by bundle id, catching any XCTest NSException (which Swift
/// cannot catch and which would otherwise abort the whole runner). Returns YES if
/// activation was attempted without throwing. Must be safe to call off-main.
+ (BOOL)safeActivateBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// Bring an app to the front, launching it if it isn't running.
///
/// `activate` alone is a no-op on a process that isn't up yet, which is the case
/// for SpringBoard after a reboot. WebDriverAgent branches the same way for its
/// home-screen route; this mirrors that.
+ (BOOL)activateOrLaunchBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// Terminate an app by bundle id, catching any XCTest NSException. Returns YES if
/// termination was attempted without throwing.
+ (BOOL)safeTerminateBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// Returns the XCUIApplicationState raw value for a bundle id, caught safely:
///   0 = unknown, 1 = notRunning, 2 = runningBackgroundSuspended,
///   3 = runningBackground, 4 = runningForeground.
/// Used to tell "app crashed/closed" from "app just not frontmost".
+ (NSInteger)appStateForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// The app's display name as the home screen shows it (its Application
/// element's accessibility label), caught safely. nil if the app isn't running
/// or the read throws. Costs one accessibility round-trip to the target app.
+ (nullable NSString *)safeLabelForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId;

/// Whether a system alert / permission dialog is currently on screen (owned by
/// SpringBoard, covering the app). When true, actions should target the system
/// UI to dismiss it first. Caught safely; returns NO on any error.
+ (BOOL)hasSystemAlert;

/// Benchmarks the two ways XCTest can fetch an accessibility tree, on the same
/// live UI, so we can tell where page_source's cost actually is.
///
/// `XCUIElement.snapshot()` (what page_source uses) resolves to
/// `snapshotForElement:attributes:parameters:` with `defaultParameters` — no
/// depth limit — so the target app walks and serializes its ENTIRE tree before
/// anything crosses the IPC boundary. Our max_depth/max_elements then trim the
/// already-materialized result, which cannot recover that cost.
///
/// XCUIAutomation exposes `maxDepth`/`maxChildren`/`maxArrayCount` parameter
/// keys that ride along with the request and are applied by the AX server on the
/// far side. Whether the server actually honours them is the open question this
/// answers empirically — the key existing in the binary is not proof it is
/// implemented on iOS 26.
///
/// Returns a dictionary of timings/sizes per variant, or nil if the private API
/// is unavailable. Never throws.
/// Takes `-[XCUIElement snapshotWithError:]` without letting it kill the runner.
///
/// XCTest raises an Obj-C NSException from snapshot() in states Swift cannot
/// intercept — `try?` only catches Swift `throws`, so the exception reaches
/// XCTest's terminate handler and the process dies with SIGABRT. That is exactly
/// what happened when the snapshot walk was promoted to find_element's primary
/// path: it aborted on the first call, before a single phase was logged.
///
/// Returns nil when the snapshot is unavailable, so callers can fall back.
+ (nullable id)safeSnapshotOfElement:(id)element;

/// Reads a BOOL property of an element without letting it kill the runner.
///
/// `exists` and `isHittable` look like plain property reads, but each one asks
/// the target app to resolve the query across IPC — and XCTest raises an Obj-C
/// NSException when that resolution fails. Swift cannot intercept it: `try?`
/// only catches Swift `throws`, so the exception unwinds into XCTest's
/// terminate handler and the process dies with SIGABRT.
///
/// Seen on iOS 16.1: `-[XCUIElement exists]` threw from inside
/// `-[XCTActivityRecordStack didFinishActivity:]` while the caller was on a
/// background queue, killing the runner outright. Older XCTest builds record
/// an activity per query and are stricter about the stack being balanced, so
/// this is far likelier off the main queue and on older systems.
///
/// `fallback` is returned when the read throws, letting the caller treat an
/// unanswerable query as "no" rather than as a crash.
+ (BOOL)safeBoolProperty:(NSString *)name ofElement:(id)element fallback:(BOOL)fallback;

/// As `safeBoolProperty:`, but tells a real NO apart from a read that threw:
/// returns 1 / 0, or -1 with the exception's reason in `outReason`.
///
/// The distinction is the whole point. `exists` throwing means XCTest could
/// not answer at all — the app is busy or backgrounded — and reporting that as
/// "element gone" sent a real incident's post-mortem down the wrong path.
+ (NSInteger)boolPropertyState:(NSString *)name ofElement:(id)element
                        reason:(NSString * _Nullable * _Nullable)outReason;

/// Fetches an accessibility snapshot with the traversal bounded ON THE DEVICE.
///
/// `XCUIElement.snapshot()` asks the target app to walk and serialise its whole
/// tree before anything crosses the IPC boundary, so a long-scrolled feed costs
/// seconds no matter what the caller intends to keep. XCTest's underlying
/// request accepts `maxDepth`/`maxChildren`, which the app applies while
/// walking — measured at 1.6s versus 6.5-8.5s for the same X timeline, with the
/// feed's text intact.
///
/// Returns an `XCUIElementSnapshot`-conforming root, or nil if any part of the
/// private path is unavailable (it moved four times on iOS 26 alone) — callers
/// must fall back to `snapshot()` rather than treating nil as an empty screen.
+ (nullable id)boundedSnapshotForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId
                                 maxDepth:(NSInteger)maxDepth
                              maxChildren:(NSInteger)maxChildren;

/// Every match for `query` in a bounded snapshot, ranked for acting on.
///
/// Returns @{candidates, visited, content_top, content_bottom, fingerprint,
/// scroll_container?}. Each candidate is @{how, label, identifier, type, x, y,
/// w, h, visibility ("in_view" | "partial" | "offscreen"), key ("label" |
/// "identifier"), ordinal, container?}. `ordinal` is the index a live
/// `label == X` (or identifier) query over the same `types` would give this
/// node, so the caller can re-resolve THIS element rather than the first one
/// that happens to share its label.
///
/// Ranking: in view > partly visible > off screen, then exact > id > contains,
/// then contains-hits on a token boundary, then shorter labels. `types` are
/// XCUIElementType raw values and must mirror the live query's type filter;
/// nil means any type. `fingerprint` summarises what is on screen, for telling
/// whether a scroll moved anything. Walks in Obj-C for the same reason as the
/// renderer below.
+ (nullable NSDictionary *)locateInBoundedSnapshot:(id)root
                                             query:(NSString *)query
                                          contains:(BOOL)contains
                                             types:(nullable NSArray<NSNumber *> *)types
                                          viewport:(CGRect)viewport
                                          maxDepth:(NSInteger)maxDepth;

/// Renders a bounded snapshot tree to the same one-line-per-node text
/// `page_source` produces.
///
/// Done here rather than in Swift because the returned object is an
/// `XCElementSnapshot`, and casting it to the `XCUIElementSnapshot` protocol
/// yields a value whose `frame` reads {{0,0},{0,0}} and whose `children` stops
/// after the first level — the tree looks 16 nodes deep and empty when it
/// actually holds hundreds. Reading the same properties through the runtime
/// returns the real values.
+ (nullable NSString *)renderBoundedSnapshot:(id)root
                                    maxDepth:(NSInteger)maxDepth
                                 maxElements:(NSInteger)maxElements
                                 nodesWritten:(NSInteger *)outCount
                                    truncated:(BOOL *)outTruncated;

/// As above, but emits only nodes intersecting `visibleRect` (plus the ancestor
/// path of each, so the result is still a tree). Pass CGRectNull for no culling.
///
/// On a recycling list this is the difference between a usable tree and a
/// useless one: WeChat's chat list returns 1500 nodes of which ~91% sit
/// offscreen (measured y from -9115 to +13204), and those exhaust maxElements
/// before the visible rows are reached. Culling during the walk — rather than
/// afterwards — means the element budget bounds VISIBLE content.
///
/// Note this cannot prune subtrees: a container's frame does not bound its
/// children in a recycling list, so every node is still visited.
+ (nullable NSString *)renderBoundedSnapshot:(id)root
                                    maxDepth:(NSInteger)maxDepth
                                 maxElements:(NSInteger)maxElements
                                 visibleRect:(CGRect)visibleRect
                                 nodesWritten:(NSInteger *)outCount
                                    truncated:(BOOL *)outTruncated;

/// What the snapshot API on THIS XCTest build accepts — class metadata only, no
/// snapshot taken, so it cannot hang the accessibility channel.
+ (NSDictionary *)snapshotAPICapabilities;

/// Selects the single snapshot property `benchmarkSnapshotForBundleID:` samples.
/// Undocumented getters can crash the process outright (SIGBUS, which @catch
/// cannot intercept), so exactly one is read per call and it is named here.
+ (void)setProbeSelectorName:(nullable NSString *)name;

+ (nullable NSDictionary *)benchmarkSnapshotForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId
                                               maxDepth:(NSInteger)maxDepth;

@end

NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_END

```

```m
+ (double)setAXTimeout:(double)seconds {
    @try {
        Class deviceClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCUIDevice");
        id device = [deviceClass performSelector:NSSelectorFromString(@"sharedDevice")];
        SEL ifaceSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"accessibilityInterface");
        if (![device respondsToSelector:ifaceSel]) { return -1; }
        id client = [device performSelector:ifaceSel];
        double previous = -1;
        SEL getSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"AXTimeout");
        if ([client respondsToSelector:getSel]) {
            double (*getFn)(id, SEL) = (double (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
            previous = getFn(client, getSel);
        }
        SEL setSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"_setAXTimeout:error:");
        if ([client respondsToSelector:setSel]) {
            NSError *err = nil;
            BOOL (*setFn)(id, SEL, double, NSError **) = (BOOL (*)(id, SEL, double, NSError **))objc_msgSend;
            if (!setFn(client, setSel, seconds, &err)) { return -2; }
            return previous;
        }
        SEL plainSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"setAXTimeout:");
        if ([client respondsToSelector:plainSel]) {
            void (*fn)(id, SEL, double) = (void (*)(id, SEL, double))objc_msgSend;
            fn(client, plainSel, seconds);
            return previous;
        }
        return -1;
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {
        return -3;
    }
}

+ (pid_t)frontmostPID {
    @try {
        Class deviceClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCUIDevice");
        SEL sharedSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"sharedDevice");
        SEL ifaceSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"accessibilityInterface");
        if (![deviceClass respondsToSelector:sharedSel]) { return 0; }
        id device = [deviceClass performSelector:sharedSel];
        if (![device respondsToSelector:ifaceSel]) { return 0; }
        id client = [device performSelector:ifaceSel];
        SEL sel = NSSelectorFromString(@"activeApplications");
        if (![client respondsToSelector:sel]) { return 0; }
        NSArray *apps = [client performSelector:sel];
        if (![apps isKindOfClass:[NSArray class]] || apps.count == 0) { return 0; }
        // iOS 27 lists exactly one element, the app in front (SpringBoard at
        // the home screen). Its pid is readable even where its bundle id isn't.
        id element = apps.firstObject;
        SEL pidSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"processIdentifier");
        // A crashed app can stay first in the list, sending every later read
        // to its dead pid. Skip pids that no longer exist
        // (kill(pid, 0) only checks; ESRCH = no such process).
        for (id a in apps) {
            if (![a respondsToSelector:pidSel]) { continue; }
            pid_t p = [[a valueForKey:@"processIdentifier"] intValue];
            if (p > 0 && (kill(p, 0) == 0 || errno != ESRCH)) { element = a; break; }
        }
        if (apps.count > 1) {
            // Diagnostic: which order does a multi-app list come in? Reads
            // landing on a stale app suggest firstObject is not always front.
            NSMutableArray *pids = [NSMutableArray array];
            for (id a in apps) {
                if ([a respondsToSelector:pidSel]) { [pids addObject:[a valueForKey:@"processIdentifier"] ?: @0]; }
            }
            static NSString *lastLogged;
            NSString *line = [pids componentsJoinedByString:@","];
            if (![line isEqualToString:lastLogged]) {
                lastLogged = line;
                NSLog(@"🔎 activeApplications count=%lu pids=[%@]", (unsigned long)apps.count, line);
            }
        }
        if (![element respondsToSelector:pidSel]) { return 0; }
        NSMethodSignature *sig = [element methodSignatureForSelector:pidSel];
        NSInvocation *inv = [NSInvocation invocationWithMethodSignature:sig];
        inv.selector = pidSel;
        [inv invokeWithTarget:element];
        pid_t pid = 0;
        [inv getReturnValue:&pid];
        return pid;
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {
        return 0;
    }
}

+ (pid_t)processIDForBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId {
    if (bundleId.length == 0) { return 0; }
    @try {
        Class appClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCUIApplication");
        if (!appClass) { return 0; }
        id (*initFn)(id, SEL, id) = (id (*)(id, SEL, id))objc_msgSend;
        id app = initFn([appClass alloc], @selector(initWithBundleIdentifier:), bundleId);
        SEL pidSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"processID");
        if (!app || ![app respondsToSelector:pidSel]) { return 0; }
        pid_t (*pidFn)(id, SEL) = (pid_t (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
        return pidFn(app, pidSel);
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {
        return 0;
    }
}

+ (nullable NSString *)currentBundleID {
    @try {
        // +sharedClient is gone on newer iOS: XCAXClient_iOS exposes no class
        // methods at all there, so the old call threw "unrecognized selector",
        // was swallowed below, and this returned nil — which surfaced as
        // foreground_app:null and a stream of bogus "app is in the background"
        // errors even with the app plainly on screen. Reach the client the way
        // XCUIElementQuery does (device -> accessibilityInterface) and keep
        // +sharedClient only as the legacy fallback.
        id client = nil;
        @try {
            Class deviceClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCUIDevice");
            SEL sharedSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"sharedDevice");
            if ([deviceClass respondsToSelector:sharedSel]) {
                id device = [deviceClass performSelector:sharedSel];
                SEL ifaceSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"accessibilityInterface");
                if ([device respondsToSelector:ifaceSel]) {
                    client = [device performSelector:ifaceSel];
                }
            }
        } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}

        if (!client) {
            Class clientClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCAXClient_iOS");
            if (!clientClass) { return nil; }
            SEL sharedClientSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"sharedClient");
            if (![clientClass respondsToSelector:sharedClientSel]) { return nil; }
            client = [clientClass performSelector:sharedClientSel];
        }
        if (!client) { return nil; }

        // activeApplications: first element is the frontmost app.
        SEL sel = NSSelectorFromString(@"activeApplications");
        if (![client respondsToSelector:sel]) { return nil; }

        NSArray *apps = [client performSelector:sel];
        if (![apps isKindOfClass:[NSArray class]] || apps.count == 0) { return nil; }

        // SpringBoard is always in this list, so it is skipped in favour of a
        // real app — but only an app that says it is in front. When SpringBoard
        // itself is what's showing (a system alert, the home screen), the next
        // entry can be an app already sent to the background; returning it made
        // callers query a window-less app, which on iOS 16 spun XCTest at 100%
        // CPU until the system killed the runner. state is answered by
        // testmanagerd without touching the accessibility tree — milliseconds.
        NSString *springboard = nil;
        for (id element in apps) {
            NSString *bid = [self bundleIDForElement:element];
            if (bid.length == 0) { continue; }
            if ([bid isEqualToString:@"com.apple.springboard"]) { springboard = bid; continue; }
            NSInteger state = [self appStateForBundleID:bid];
            if (state == 4 || state == 0) { return bid; }   // runningForeground, or unknown
        }
        if (springboard) { return springboard; }
        // Fallback: return whatever the first element resolves to.
        return [self bundleIDForElement:apps.firstObject];
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {
        return nil;
    }
}

+ (nullable NSString *)bundleIDForElement:(id)element {
    @try {
        // Try a direct bundleID-ish selector first.
        for (NSString *name in @[@"bundleIdentifier", @"bundleID"]) {
            SEL s = NSSelectorFromString(name);
            if ([element respondsToSelector:s]) {
                id v = [element performSelector:s];
                if ([v isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]) { return v; }
            }
        }
        // Otherwise resolve via process identifier.
        SEL pidSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"processIdentifier");
        if ([element respondsToSelector:pidSel]) {
            NSMethodSignature *sig = [element methodSignatureForSelector:pidSel];
            NSInvocation *inv = [NSInvocation invocationWithMethodSignature:sig];
            inv.selector = pidSel;
            [inv invokeWithTarget:element];
            pid_t pid = 0;
            [inv getReturnValue:&pid];
            if (pid > 0) {
                return [self bundleIDForPID:pid];
            }
        }
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
    return nil;
}

+ (nullable NSString *)bundleIDForPID:(pid_t)pid {
    @try {
        // XCUIApplication can be constructed by pid via a private initializer in
        // some XCTest versions; if unavailable, we can't resolve here.
        Class appClass = NSClassFromString(@"XCUIApplication");
        SEL initSel = NSSelectorFromString(@"initWithProcessID:");
        if (appClass && [appClass instancesRespondToSelector:initSel]) {
            id app = [appClass alloc];
            NSMethodSignature *sig = [app methodSignatureForSelector:initSel];
            NSInvocation *inv = [NSInvocation invocationWithMethodSignature:sig];
            inv.selector = initSel;
            [inv setArgument:&pid atIndex:2];
            [inv invokeWithTarget:app];
            void *result = NULL;
            [inv getReturnValue:&result];
            id appInstance = (__bridge id)result;
            if ([appInstance respondsToSelector:NSSelectorFromString(@"bundleID")]) {
                id bid = [appInstance performSelector:NSSelectorFromString(@"bundleID")];
                if ([bid isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]) { return bid; }
            }
        }
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
    return nil;
}

+ (nullable NSArray<NSDictionary *> *)installedAppsUserOnly:(BOOL)userOnly {
    @try {
        Class wsClass = NSClassFromString(@"LSApplicationWorkspace");
        if (!wsClass) { return nil; }
        id ws = [wsClass performSelector:@selector(defaultWorkspace)];
        if (!ws) { return nil; }

        NSArray *apps = nil;
        // WDA uses allApplications; try it first, fall back to allInstalledApplications.
        if ([ws respondsToSelector:@selector(allApplications)]) {
            apps = [ws performSelector:@selector(allApplications)];
        }
        if (![apps isKindOfClass:[NSArray class]] || apps.count == 0) {
            if ([ws respondsToSelector:@selector(allInstalledApplications)]) {
                apps = [ws performSelector:@selector(allInstalledApplications)];
            }
        }
        if (![apps isKindOfClass:[NSArray class]]) { return nil; }

        NSMutableArray *out = [NSMutableArray array];
        for (id proxy in apps) {
            @try {
                NSString *bid = nil, *name = nil, *type = nil;
                if ([proxy respondsToSelector:@selector(applicationIdentifier)]) {
                    bid = [proxy performSelector:@selector(applicationIdentifier)];
                }
                if ([proxy respondsToSelector:@selector(localizedName)]) {
                    name = [proxy performSelector:@selector(localizedName)];
                }
                if ([proxy respondsToSelector:@selector(applicationType)]) {
                    type = [proxy performSelector:@selector(applicationType)];
                }
                if (bid.length == 0) { continue; }
                if (userOnly && type && ![type isEqualToString:@"User"]) { continue; }
                [out addObject:@{
                    @"bundle_id": bid ?: @"",
                    @"name": name ?: @"",
                    @"type": type ?: @"",
                }];
            } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
        }
        // Sort by name for stable, readable output.
        [out sortUsingComparator:^NSComparisonResult(NSDictionary *a, NSDictionary *b) {
            return [a[@"name"] localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare:b[@"name"]];
        }];
        return out;
    } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {
        return nil;
    }
}

+ (BOOL)activateOrLaunchBundleID:(NSString *)bundleId {
```
